noi_dung:
1. Before leaving the home life

Venerable Hai Hien (1900 - 2013), secular name Van, name Xuyen Hien, courtesy name Thanh Tuyen, hometown of Thieu Bai Tu town, Duong Ha district, Nam Duong city, southwest of today's Henan province, was born on August 19 (1900) in the 26th year of Quang Tu at the end of the Qing Dynasty. Venerable Hai Hien's parents and grandparents were all devout Buddha disciples, with a family tradition of both farming and teaching, and loved doing good deeds, or giving, and were called great philanthropists by their countrymen. Venerable Hai Hien has an honest, simple nature, has deep roots, has been a vegetarian since he was a child, following his mother. When he was young, he was famous in the village for his filial conduct.

Venerable Hai Hien's mother, Lady Hoang Thi, was born in the 10th year of Dong Tri of the Qing Dynasty (1871). Her mother's family hometown is Tu Vien village, Chu Tap village, Xa Ky district, Nam Duong city, located in the southwest of today's Ha Nam province. Our ancestors were all honest, peaceful farmers. Because her parents were both devout Buddhist disciples, she became a vegetarian from a young age and took refuge in Buddha. At the age of 17, she married into the Van family of Thieu Bai Tu town, Duong Ha district, her husband's name was Van Tu Can, 8 years older than Hoang Thi. The ancestors of the Van family were from a family with a tradition of education and a talented family. By the time of Tu Can Cong, the family had declined, their family background was middle-class, but for many generations the Van family had a good tradition, inheriting and continuing the worship of the Three Jewels (Buddha, Dharma, Sangha), so women and children within a few dozen miles all knew the reputation of "good people" of Tu Can Cong's parents.

Although Hoang Thi and Tu Can Cong were young husband and wife, they were able to follow the same moral principles. They respected each other and were extremely affectionate. In the year Mrs. Hoang Thi got married, she had a son (the eldest brother of Venerable Hai Hien), and three years later gave birth to a daughter (sister of Venerable Hai Hien). The second son (Monk Hai Hien's second brother) was born not long after. Mrs. Hoang Thi suffered from acute mastitis, commonly known as mastitis. There was no way to breastfeed the child. Not knowing what to do, the couple had to give the child to a relative family to raise.

When Venerable Hai Hien was born, Ms. Hoang Thi was 29 years old. Văn gia là đại gia tộc, vai vế trong anh em họ, Hòa thượng Hải Hiền xếp thứ bảy. 35-year-old Mrs. Hoang Thi gave birth to another son, extremely handsome, ranked eighth among cousins. A few months after the child was born, a Taoist entered the predestined house and told Mrs. Hoang Thi that although the child had a handsome appearance, he could not grow up in the Van family.

Indeed, as the Taoist said, this child was weak and had many diseases, walking unsteadily until he was 3 years old. Mrs. Hoang Thi blamed her son for karma, and after discussing with her husband, gave him to a relative who had no children.

Natural disasters and looting for many years caused this not-so-rich family to quickly fall into poverty. At that time, Venerable Hai Hien's sister suffered from a lung disease that was difficult to recover from, causing the family, which was already difficult to maintain, to fall into difficulty. To treat his daughter's illness, Tu Can Cong sold 7 acres of dry land left by his father, and together with his eldest son, he went to work for a cotton processing shop, rolling cotton and whipping cotton for people. That year, when Venerable Hai Hien was only 9 years old, he went to work herding buffaloes for a rich family to support his family.

In the year when Venerable Hai Hien was 12 years old, Ha Nam suffered a severe drought, with no harvest, the shop that hired Tu Can Cong and his son to work was also forced to stop doing business. Faced with that situation, there was no other way, Tu Can Cong could only go to Sui Chau in Hubei to beg for food to maintain the family's livelihood. Unexpectedly, he encountered evil bandits and died in a foreign land. That year, Tu Can Cong was 48 years old. At that time, Tu Can Cong was on his way to beg for food. He encountered bandits who robbed and set fire to the residential area. Tu Can Cong carried water to put out the fire, but when the bandits returned to check, the bandits caught him and beat him to death. After many days, when the fleeing villagers returned to the village, they saw a horrifying scene: A corpse was standing upright hugging a big tree, a group of hungry dogs sat on the ground, surrounding him on the inside and outside. The people in the village thought that these hungry dogs wanted to compete for the dead, so they came together to chase away the hungry dogs. Unexpectedly, these hungry dogs were beaten to tears and refused to disperse. Only then did everyone know that these dogs turned out to be holding the body of the benefactor who protected their homeland! No one who saw it cried sobbing. The people of the village brought his body back to his hometown, but Tu Can Cong was buried according to the rites of his elders.

That year, China fell into the period of chaos between the Republic of China and the military regime of the Beiyang government. His father passed away not long ago, Venerable Hai Hien's eldest brother was forced into the army, and the two brothers were separated for 24 years.

Next, an incident occurred in the family that adopted the second brother of Venerable Hai Hien and had to send the 15-year-old child back to the Van family. The second brother's health was weak and he had many illnesses, so his return increased the family's burden. Fortunately, the older sister's illness eventually healed, and she got married the following year.

Venerable Hai Hien's mother was skillful and did very good housekeeping. There is no land in the house, Mrs

Hoang Thi had to rely on sewing, washing and starching clothes, earning a small salary to support this seriously damaged family.

Ms. Hoang Thi often stays up all night embroidering handkerchiefs to wipe sweat, making shoes embroidered with flowers, then selling them for food. Venerable Hai Hien saw that his mother was working too hard, so he hid from her and secretly went out to beg for food, thinking that this way would lighten her mother's burden. After more than three months, he was finally discovered by his mother. She hugged her son and cried for a while, not letting him go out to beg for food anymore.

On Chu Tap Street, a restaurant owner named Thoi, after hearing about Venerable Hai Hien's filial behavior, was very moved, so he personally came to his house to visit and invited Hai Hien, who was only 13 years old, to work at the restaurant. Since then, the situation in the house gradually changed for the better. Venerable Hai Hien worked at a restaurant continuously until he was 18 years old. That year, he developed a poisonous pimple on his leg and almost lost his life because of it.

When he was a teenager, a number of things happened to him that strongly urged him to steadfastly and unchangedly walk the path of leaving the home life in the days to come.

The Venerable Aunt Tam's personality is not good, very domineering, and often scolds people and neighbors. One time, when she scolded Aunt Nam, she tore and stripped Aunt Nam's clothes. Later, many incidents happened in succession, all corresponding to the proverb - evil will be rewarded with evil. Aunt Tam gave birth to four sons, all of whom died prematurely; Aunt Tam's tongue kept getting bitten by her own teeth (as people often say, "chewing the base of the tongue"), and kept bleeding, until her tongue was chewed off by herself, and she couldn't eat rice; Later, Aunt Tam, while giving birth to her daughter at the age of 32, died painfully.

The tragic situation at the time of her death made Venerable Hai Hien's sister so scared that she suffered from nervous symptoms. Uncle Tam himself was both angry and sick and said goodbye to the world.

Venerable Hai Hien's mother saw Aunt Tam day and night, morning and night, flirting with each other, and finally dying with a very unsightly appearance, so she told Venerable Hai Hien that she must be remembered and absolutely cannot learn from her. She told Venerable Hai Hien: "You must be kind and tolerant towards others. Absolutely do not do evil or commit crimes!" His mother's words were deeply engraved in the Venerable's mind.

In addition, one thing also had a great impact on Venerable Hai Hien when he was young. One time, he grew a large squash, which was stolen by their younger brother. The monk kept repeating for three consecutive days: “Whoever steals my squash will cause that person to get pimples and get sick.” Who would have thought that after three days, the Venerable's younger cousin got really sick with pimples, was bedridden, and was speechless. After Aunt knew, she went to Him and said: "Don't chant anymore, your little brother just picked a squash, then you thought he would get pimples all over his body and it hurt so much that he called his father and mother." Venerable Hai Hien was extremely surprised and thought: Are human thoughts really that powerful? So immediately correct the thought: “Quickly make her well again! Hurry and make her well again!” Their younger brother's illness really got better quickly.

If you recite something, it will appear, so you can no longer recite evil thoughts. Regardless of whether it was a coincidence or not, from then on, he did not dare to blame anyone anymore, nor did he dare to resent anyone anymore. This made him understand the inconceivability of the power of mindfulness. Although he did not read the books of the Sages or study the scriptures of the Saints, his nature was kind, his heart pure and compassionate, and he could often gain inspiration in daily life.

According to rumors, when Venerable Hai Hien was 18 years old, the Venerable's legs developed poisonous pimples and large, severe ulcers. His mother asked him to find medicine everywhere for him, but there was no way to save him. Finally, he understood that this was a karma disease, he understood the cause and effect of retribution, complaining that: "A miracle medicine that can't be cured by unjust karma." So I threw away the medicine and went back to praying to Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara.

Chinese folk, no one does not know Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva is great compassion, saves suffering and rescues, if there is a request, there is a response, so he sincerely recites the Holy name Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. After chanting for more than a month, the poisonous pimples naturally disappeared. This is touch! Therefore, he had deep and unquestioning faith in Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva to save suffering and rescue, and was even more convinced that Bodhisattva was truly compassionate, with absolutely no lies. Reciting Buddha, reciting Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva can really solve the problem.

The title of merit is inconceivable, the power of thought is inconceivable. But why is it that some people's recitation is not spiritual, but when he recites it, it is spiritual? That's because His thoughts are pure, He's focused, and doesn't have so many delusions and distracting thoughts. If you are single-minded in your thoughts, your thoughts will be effective. Venerable Hai Hien has an honest nature, listens to words, truly acts, has a sincere heart, a pure mind and a respectful mind. If these conditions are met, his recitation is effective. It was His faith and thoughts that cured his own illness.

From then on, Venerable Hai Hien knew that the path of birth and death was dangerous, and birth and death were a big matter, so he had a mind of renunciation. When he was 19 years old, his 22 year old third brother passed away due to illness, this made Venerable Hai Hien steadfast to the end and determined to leave the home life to practice.

2. leaving the home life

In 1920, Venerable Hai Hien, 20 years old, left the home life with the old Venerable Chuyen Gioi at Van Dai meditation pagoda on the top of Thai Bach Dong Bach mountain, located at the junction of Henan and Hubei. The old monk gave him the precepts and gave him the Dharma name Hai Hien, from Tanh Thanh. At the age of 23, he went to Vinh Bao Temple in Hubei to receive full ordination (Bhikkhu ordination).

meditation from Yuntai is the Patriarch of the White Cloud sect, Lam Te Zen school of China, said to be the "Potala Palace of China". The Lam Te sect is one of the five Zen schools of Chinese Buddhism. The style of this sect is simple and straightforward, its sharp and intense speech, making people suddenly awaken is the unique feature of the sect, so it is very popular with soldiers, laymen, generals, politicians, etc. Most of them also follow this Zen school method. By the Qing Dynasty, the Rinzai sect became the main stream of Chinese Zen school because of its free meditation style.

The monk took off his hair for Venerable Hai Hien, the Venerable Chuyen Gioi, from Bach Khuu, Ha Nam Duong district (the old district name of Ha Nam). He used to be the meditation master Truc Tanh (literally Chan Khong). At that time, he could be said to be a master of meditation. He later followed meditation master Truc Tanh to Maitreya monastery.

Beijing, in addition to serving, also took on the position of hall master. After the newly established Chinese government returned to Dong Bach mountain, he led his disciples, planted thatch grass to reclaim land, and personally served as medical staff.

As a Venerable of the Bach Van sect, Lam Te sect, the Venerable Chuan Gioi did not teach Hai Hien zazen meditation, nor did he teach him to preach sutras and preach the Dharma. He only passed down the six-letter name "Namo Amitabha Buddha", instructing him to recite it continuously. Venerable Hai Hien followed his teacher's advice all his life.

After leaving the home life, Venerable Hai Hien always resided at Pho Hoa Pagoda, Van Dai Pagoda, and Thap Vien Pagoda on Dong Bach Mountain. In 1976, after "Van Cach" ended, many lay people invited him to Lai Buddha pagoda, Xa Ky district under the mountain to preside over the Dharma. Around 1981, Venerable Hai Hien permanently resided at Lai Buddha pagoda, until 2013 for rebirth.

noi_dung:
3. Filial piety

As a child, Venerable Hai Hien was famous in the countryside for his filial piety. From a very young age, he began working hard to help support his family's expenses. When he left the home life in Dong Bach mountain, right in the first years of the Republic's power, the militaristic bases were in chaos. Venerable Hai Hien's mother, Mrs. Hoang Thi, and her young son depended on each other, struggling to survive day by day. Venerable Hai Hien was very filial. He worked in the mountains on reclaimed land, dug up herbs to exchange for food, then walked more than a hundred miles to carry food back to his hometown to make offerings for his mother, nine years like that without interruption.

In the 18th year of the Republic of Korea (1929), the 22-year-old younger brother of

Venerable Hai Hien unfortunately passed away. At this time, my mother

He is old and has no one around to take care of him.

This made Venerable Hai Hien quite worried. In order to conveniently take care of her, Venerable Hai Hien took her mother to Dao Hoa cave on top of Thai Bach, where Dong Bach mountain took care of her. She lived on the mountain for 27 years, until a year before her rebirth, when Venerable Hai Hien took her down the mountain and returned to her hometown.

According to Buddha's regulations, leaving the home life requires asking parents. If you have brothers and sisters who can trust you, you can propose leaving the home life to your parents. If your parents agree, then you can leave the home life. Otherwise, you can't let your hair down. After leaving the home life, if you have a problem and your parents have no support, you will have to reduce your medical conditions to take care of your two relatives. That's why in history there is a story where people praise Truong Lo Tong's foster mother.

Recorded in "Pure Land Thanh Hien Luc", meditation master Tong Tac of the Song Dynasty, lost his father at a young age, was raised by his mother Tran Thi, after growing up, knowledgeable and knowledgeable about worldly books, left the home life at the age of 29, had a profound understanding of meditation's principles and meanings, later lived in Truong Lo Pagoda, welcomed his mother to live in the east room of the Phuong Truong room, advised her to recite Buddha's name to pray for birth in Pure Land, after 7 years, his mother recited Buddha's name and passed away.

After Venerable Hai Hien's mother lived in the mountains for seven years, his second brother, who was forced to become a soldier 24 years ago, finally returned. He came to the Venerable.

Hai Hien. The two brothers were separated for many years, but not long after they met again, the second brother died of a sudden brain hemorrhage in the arms of Venerable Hai Hien. Because conditions at that time were too difficult, Venerable Hai Hien was unable to bring his second brother back to his hometown, so he had to bury him poorly on Dong Bach mountain.

In 1956, the mother of the 86-year-old Venerable Hai Hien proposed that he want to return to his hometown. The Venerable Hai Hien followed his mother back to her hometown. He stayed at home to accompany and take care of her until the second year when she was reborn.

Venerable Hai Hien is a filial son. Even when he was over 100 years old, on Thanh Minh festival or the 10th day of the 10th lunar month every year, he still did not forget to sacrifice to the Ancestor. Every year at this time, no matter which monastery he was in or which way he recited Buddha's name, he always reminded himself: "I have to return quickly. October 1st is here. I have to go back to the tomb to worship my ancestors. I also have to go to Dong Bach mountain monastery and worship my teacher."

Ancient Chinese people promoted filial piety, offering sacrifices to the ancestors twice a year. Ancient Chinese education first taught people to be filial to their parents, to be kind and brotherly, to apply benevolence, propriety, wisdom, and trust. That is, to learn to be human first, to be filial and loyal, to be respectful, to be honest, to be kind, to be kind, to be peaceful, and then to be considered virtuous, and then to learn to work.

Mahayana Buddha Dharma also promotes filial piety, "Pure karma Three blessings" extracted from the "Infinite Life Buddha Sutra", is the highest guiding principle of Buddhist students, the first blessings in the "three blessings" total four sentences: “Be filial and take care of your parents, serve your teacher, be kind and do not kill, practice the ten good karmas.”

Therefore, we can know that filial piety is the basis of all virtues. Venerable Hai Hien truly put into practice the two roots of "filial piety", because of his lifelong achievements in karma, he built a solid foundation.

4. Chief Master Phung

Buddha said, parents have the gift of nurturing, and elders have the gift of teaching. If you can make respectful offerings, not only will you repay the favor, but you can also naturally receive blessings, which are blessings that repay the favor. To be filial and take care of one's parents, to serve one's teacher is to practice good filial piety, filial piety, and loyalty, etc. which exists in the world, and at the same time is pure karma that Pure Land practitioners chanting Buddha rebirth Ultimate Bliss must practice.

The Precepts Transmission Master of Venerable Hai Hien once lived at Dong Bach y chi mountain.

meditation master Truc Tanh, later, moved to Maitreya Institute in Beijing (at the end of the Qing Dynasty, Maitreya Institute was one of the institutes affiliated with Quang Te Pagoda in the capital). In order to repay his teacher's Dharma Embrace, he followed meditation master Truc Tanh to Maitreya Monastery in Beijing, served first and foremost, and at the same time accepted the position of hall master. Venerable Hai Hien once told his disciple Dharma Master An Chi that his master practiced at Quang Te Temple in Beijing and did not leave the meditation hall for 12 years. After the new Chinese state was established, the meditation hall stopped offering incense and lamps, and Chuyen Gioi Cong returned to Dong Bach mountain to make reclaimed thatch grass, leading his disciples to work hard and diligently in farming, at the same time cultivating medicinal herbs, and personally doing medical work.

In China, from the Sui Tang to the mid-Qing Dynasty, Buddha Dharma flourished, and in every sect there were Venerable Monks appearing, people with clear minds and true nature. Venerable Hai Hien has already clear his mind to see his nature. His master, the Master of Transmission Precepts, is also a person who has his mind to see his nature. The master can see that this disciple is a dharma weapon, this is his practice. Looking out from where? From His nature, it is also the innate nature that we talk about. Venerable Chuyen Gioi knows that although this person has never gone to school and is a very poor child, he has a very good nature, is sincere, honest, obedient, and works hard. Any person like that will have achievements. As long as the path is correctly guided, this person can really succeed.

Venerable Hai Hien's master can contemplate the opportunity, he responds to the opportunity and teaches what dharma to whom. If this person has enlightenment, knows that this world is suffering, hopes to leave suffering, has also heard that the Ultimate Bliss World is happy, prays for rebirth, this is a person of superior capacity, a person of superior capacity is advised to recite the Buddha's name to enter the initiation; People of intermediate capacity only meditate on the initiation; People of low capacity repent and enter the temple.

Venerable Hai Hien's master only taught him a phrase "Namo Amitabha Buddha", instructing him to recite it continuously. Hai Hien happily accepted. He did not disobey his teacher, did not disobey the teachings, followed his teacher's teachings, saying "Amitabha Buddha" from morning to night, one sentence after another without interruption, his whole life remained unchanged. After enlightening my mind and seeing my nature, I know everything, but I don't say anything. If someone asked Him, He smiled without answering, neither admitting nor denying.

During the "Great Cultural Revolution", the Red Guards destroyed the Buddhist monk's stupa, but discovered the grave was empty and no ashes were visible. Venerable Chuyen Gioi foresaw and hid the ashes under the tower, so they were not discovered. Later, Venerable Hai Hien found his master's ashes under a blue stone below the grave. He encountered countless difficulties to preserve his master's ashes.

It was not until 1991 that Venerable Hai Hien personally led his disciples, built a tower next to Dao Hoa cave on Dong Bach mountain, and buried his master's ashes. Every year during the worship period, Venerable Hai Hien must go and worship his master's tower tomb.

meditation master Truc Tanh, master of Dharma Master Chuyen Gioi, master of Venerable Hai Hien, at the end of the Qing Dynasty and early in the Republic of China could be called meditation subject of master virtue, noble morality. In the last years of his life, at the request of the northern disciples, he immigrated to Maitreya Monastery in Beijing, local meditation guests, hearing the name, came like thick clouds, Maitreya Monastery in a few days turned into Tung Lam (great monastery), with Cao Man Pagoda and Kim Son Temple in the South to contact and coordinate with each other from afar. At that time, meditation guests all knew "The South belongs to Cao Man, Kim Son, the North belongs to Maitreya Meditation Monastery". In 1952, meditation master Chan Khong (meditation master Truc Tanh) after entering samadhi for 14 days, sat upright and passed away, living 80 years. After cremation, there were more than 120 red and white relics.

In 1954, disciples of Venerable Chan Khong walked to Beijing, welcomed and escorted Venerable Chan Khong's remains for burial at Thap Vien Pagoda on Dong Bach Mountain.

Dharma Master Hai Mac and Dharma Master Hai Vien are the ones who together with Venerable Hai Hien held a group meditation retreat on Dong Bach mountain and Venerable Hai Hien himself has all joined the escort team this time.

Venerable Hai Hien not only practiced the virtue of respecting his teacher and teachers, but also during difficult years, single-handedly took care of five elderly elders.

In early 1948, a group of thugs impersonating the army came to Van Dai Pagoda, Pho Hoa Pagoda and Bao An Pagoda, etc. looted, and at the same time forced monks and nuns to leave the temple. Young monks fled en masse. There were only five old and weak monks who did not have the strength to go down the mountain. Venerable Hai Hien welcomed the elders to Thap Vien pagoda to take care of them.

During a long period of decades, the temple did not have offerings of incense or lamps. Most Venerable Hai Hien worked hard and diligently all day long, until each of them were reborn. During this time, the old Venerable also had to take care of his elderly mother. During the day, the Venerable plowed fields, dug up herbs, and bowed to the Buddha at night, often bowing until his head was dizzy and his eyes were dizzy! The monk continued like that, day after day of hardship and hardship.

Buddha said we must "be filial, take care of our parents, and serve our teachers." Inside filial piety is parents as representatives, respect is teachers as representatives, we must respect teachers, respect the teachings they have taught, the so-called respecting teachers. Our life comes from our parents, our life (wisdom) comes from our teachers, a person must remember the merit of planting a tree all his life, these two benefactors must not be forgotten.

Filial piety and respect for teachers are also virtues of traditional Chinese culture. Filial piety is the foundation of traditional Chinese culture, and respect is the foundation of traditional Chinese culture. Let's take plants as an example, the base is the tree trunk, it is born from the root, on the tree trunk there are branches, from the tree branches are divided into branches, there are also fruit branches and leaves, these fruit branches and leaves are all produced from the same root.

Sage education, Mahayana Buddha Dharma, are based on filial piety, so traditional Chinese culture and Mahayana Buddha Dharma are the same root. On Qingming Festival and the 1st of October every year, the Venerable Hai Hien must return to his hometown, go to the grave to pay homage to his ancestors, and worship his teachers. This is on the one hand filial piety, on the other hand is filial piety, on the other hand, "filial piety" these two words, Venerable Hai Hien has set an example for people.

5. The first years on Dong Bach mountain

Venerable Hai Hien left the home life from the age of 20 to the age of 81, before coming to Lai Buddha Pagoda to permanently reside, continuously living on Dong Bach mountain. At that time, because the mountain roads were bumpy and the temples were far away and in remote places with few people, there were very few making offerings from lay people and lay people, and their livelihoods were completely dependent on their own labor and cultivation.

Venerable Hai Hien is extremely diligent, doing any job without sparing effort, carrying water, washing vegetables, cooking rice, washing dishes, cleaning pots, doing every job. The monk tried his best not to let his teacher and brothers get involved, always thinking in his heart that they would have more time to practice. The temples, top and bottom, inside and out, including the toilets, were all repaired and cleaned by Venerable Hai Hien, putting himself into work and feeling comfortable and happy; The monks can also promptly wash and arrange the clothes and daily belongings of the teacher and his brothers, Buddhist tools, dharma objects and decorative items, so as not to get dirty with mud. At that time, the Dharma Master, Hai Hien's teacher, often said to his disciples: “Hai Hien is a Buddhist monk in real life, this is the rarest thing!”

Venerable Hai Hien not only devoted himself and tried his best to manage the work above and below in the temple, but he also tried his best to do more. From 1940 to 1942, Venerable Hai Hien together with the high monks Dharma Master Hai Mac, Dharma Master Hai Vien, and Dharma Master The Quang at Thap Vien pagoda on Dong Bach mountain built a cottage for group meditation. At that time, Thap Vien Pagoda allotted land to everyone, so that everyone could plow and cultivate. Venerable Hai Hien alone covered all the land of the three of them. He recalled saying: “Thap Vien Pagoda allocated land to three people - The Quang's, Hai Mac's, and Hai Vien's. The land of the three of them was abandoned, I dug it up alone."

Dharma Master Dien Cuong and Venerable Hai Hien are old friends for more than 40 years. Dharma Master Dien Cuong, due to unbearable leg pain from rheumatism many years ago, once threw away his shoe, hence the nickname "Thiet Cuoc Monk".

Dharma Master Dien Cuong praised Venerable Hai Hien as a highly virtuous monk at one time. When he met the Venerable, he was already six or seventy years old, but his body was still very healthy. Master Dien Cuong said: “Hien Cong goes to the mountains to work every day.”

The fate of leaving the home life of this Dharma Master Dien Cuong, who is called "Thiet Cuoc Tang" is very special. One evening before becoming a monk, he dreamed that Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara said to him: “It's time, prepare to depart!” Just like that, he left the home life in Dong Bach mountain.

At that time, conditions were very difficult, there was no food, so Dharma Master Dien Cuong never concentrated on practicing. He did not forget the earthly world, did not forget his family, until one day, he met Venerable Hai Hien in Dao Hoa cave. Dharma Master Dien Cuong still remembers clearly how Venerable Hai Hien helped him that time. “He gave me some pine trees, a kilo of red sugar and 40 kilos of taro seeds. I went home and planted taro, and in the fall I had a big harvest, and the taro grew really well! From that moment on, I began to concentrate on practicing."

The life of Venerable Hai Hien at that time was not abundant at all. As soon as Dharma Master Dien Cuong mentioned the life of Venerable Hai Hien, tears welled up in his eyes and he said: “At that time, life was so miserable!”

That day, Venerable Hai Hien reclaimed land and planted crops on the mountain. After he cleared the wasteland, planted sweet potatoes and taro, this was their main food. If there are practitioners who have already gone up the mountain, He will also give them some more. If you don't have enough to eat, you dig up herbs, sell them, and exchange them for some food. In the fall, he picked chestnuts from the mountains, dried them and stored them. At that time, Venerable Hai Hien, in addition to clearing land for cultivation, also planted trees on wild mountains. Either he planted the saplings himself, or he went to the forestry site to dig up sycamore roots and plant them on the mountain. Wizard Dien Cuong could not help but sadly say: “The trees on Dong Bach mountain planted by Hien Cong himself are too many to count! When I first went up the mountain, I planted many trees with him."

After Venerable Hai Hien left the home life, he went through five months of a series of unrest, militarism, eight years of war against Japan, three years of civil war and the later "Great Cultural Revolution", etc. During such arduous days, Venerable Hai Hien cleared a total of fourteen wild mountains and over a hundred acres of land; making offerings Thousands and thousands of monks and lay people; Planting trees in wild mountains, participating in building bridges, roads, rivers, and local clinics is even more incalculable.

Before and after "Van Cach", Venerable Hai Hien often went with local people to repair bridges and roads, usually going for several months.

Like Dharma Master Dien Cuong, Dharma Master An Chi, a disciple of Venerable Hai Hien, every time he mentioned his master, he always felt countless emotions. One time, He expressed himself simply and vividly in His own way, letting people around him imagine how diligent His master was, sadly saying: “The Venerable's type of hard work - in fact, there is no way to imagine!”

He once told Dharma Master Dien Cuong: “Literature saves sentient beings and martial arts practice! You want to become a Buddha, you don't try, you don't work, you don't sweat, where is it so easy?"

Nong meditation is an ancient Chinese Zen school monastery that relies on economic basis to survive and develop. Clearing wasteland and "one day without work, one day without eating" is the style left by the Tang Dynasty. The famous Dutch Sinologist Hua Ly Hoa (Erik Zurcher 1928 - 2008) said that Buddhism in China is not a model or system of thought, but first and foremost is a way of living and a highly disciplined mode of behavior. This point is where Zen school monks have achieved concentrated expression.

Venerable Hai Hien is considered equally important by "Nong Tinh". During the day he worked and at night recited Buddha's name. Dharma Master Dien Cuong imagined Venerable Hai Hien's life at that time, saying: “At that time I was the clearest person. (He) worked during the day, there - tired to the point of dizziness! At night, I still chant Buddha, bowing to the Buddha all night long."

Venerable Hai Hien demonstrated the best practice method of this modern era. He worked (his job was farming) and recited a Buddha phrase to the end.

6. Conclusion of group meditation

During the two years from 1940 to 1942, Venerable Hai Hien, together with Dharma Master Hai Mac, Dharma Master Hai Vien and Dharma Master The Quang, established a group meditation practice at Thap Vien pagoda on Dong Bach mountain.

Every time Venerable Hai Hien mentioned this old story, he always praised the three Dharma Masters for their cultivation. One day in 2012, four months before Venerable Hai Hien's rebirth, in response to a request from Indonesian lay people to tell the story of the group meditation that year, he said: “Hai Vien is at Buddha Nha Tower in Beijing, Hai Mac died in the earthen cave of Nam Linh Son Pagoda, it has been more than 40 years since he died this year. Hai Mac knows how to lecture, he preaches sutras - he knows how to preach any sutra."

Dharma Master Hai Mac (1896 - 1968), nicknamed Dai Hac, was 4 years older than Venerable Hai Hien. Venerable Hai Hien used to call him "Old Venerable Dai Hac". Shaman Hai Mac came from the Phuong family, his ancestors were very wealthy, both of his parents died early, he was raised by his grandmother, he was a student at Huangpu military school, he also studied at the Japanese officer school, and served as chief of staff of 30 troops of the national revolutionary army. At first, he did not believe in Buddha. He once renovated a monastery into a school. Once he stayed at a friend's house. He conveniently took the Shurangama Sutra and read it. Following them all day, working hard to cut down, taking care of farming, without any bureaucratic habits, rich people. Master Hai Mac likes to study scriptures and is good at giving speeches.

In the year 26 of the Republic of China (1937), Dharma Master Hai Mac's grandmother passed away. The Dharma Master built a grass house next to the grave, recited Mahayana sutras to his grandmother, filial piety for three years, and delivered the deceased grandmother. In the fall of 2008, Venerable Hai Hien, when talking about this story with everyone, tearfully praised: “Old Venerable Dai Hac's filial piety is truly touching! I guess he must have been enlightened after three years of reciting Buddha's grave."

In 1964, Dharma Master Hai Mac lived in Linh Son Pagoda, Nghi Duong District, Luo Duong, Ha Nam. From then on, he let go of all fate, dug an earthen cave behind the pagoda, called himself "Dai Hac Quat", and lived in the cave diligently reciting the Buddha's name. Twice I felt Amitabha's light emitting light, signaling the time of rebirth. On September 23 of the lunar calendar, 1968, Master Hai Mac said goodbye to his disciples and was reborn in the West. Aged 72 years old.

The relationship between Dharma Master Hai Mac and Venerable Hai Hien is extremely good. When Venerable Hai Hien was alive, he told many stories of Dharma Master Hai Mac. He still clearly remembered that Venerable Dai Hac liked to eat fried cakes.

At the beginning of the establishment of the new Chinese state, Dharma Master Hai Mac lived for two or three years at Lai Buddha Temple. At that time, Dharma Master Hai Mac was harassed by people all day asking him to tell stories. He sat cross-legged on a stone board in the courtyard, people surrounded him, listening to him tell ancient stories and the period of the war against Japan. One time, while everyone was listening to Him tell a story, they heard movement outside the temple wall, someone said: “Is it true that a guest has arrived?” Old Venerable Dai Hac said: “Don't worry about them, just a barber passing by this way.” Everyone ran to the mountain gate and looked, unexpectedly it was a barber! That's why I admire the old Venerable to the ground.

Shaman Hai Vien (1904 - 2000) of the Chuong family, from Chuong Lau village, Dai Ha Don commune, Duong district

Ha, Ha Nam province. From a very young age, under the influence of his aunt, he was steadfast in his ambition to propagate Buddha Dharma. At the age of 13 (1919), at the ceremony of the Venerable Truyen Tai at Van Dai pagoda at Thai Bach peak, he left the home life. At the age of 16, he went to Qui Nguyen pagoda in Wuhan to receive full ordination. Shaman Hai Vien is a descendant of the eleventh generation of the Lam Te sect. In the spring of the thirty-third year of the Republic of China (1944), 40-year-old Dharma Master Hai Vien went down Dong Bach Mountain to study in Beijing. He once resided at Maitreya Institute and Quang Te Pagoda. He left for more than 50 years and never returned.

Dharma master Hai Vien is extremely talented and has been chanting the Shurangama sutras for a lifetime, practicing pure meditation. In 1979, the Chinese Buddhist Association Committee sent Dharma Master Hai Yuan to Linh Quang Pagoda in Beijing's Eight Great Lands to guard the Buddha's Relic Tower, which he kept for 21 years. When Dharma Master Hai Vien came to Linh Quang Pagoda, he was 75 years old. At that time, "Van Cach" had just ended, there were not many tourists in the Eight Great Lands, there were even fewer people in winter, the entire eight-sided Tay Son was empty, deserted without any human footprints. Rice had to be cooked by herself, vegetables had to be grown by herself, drinking water had to be carried from far away, she was the only one keeping the tower, the hardship of that job goes without saying. His situation at that time can be felt a little from the words of a poem called "Tao Lock" that he wrote at that time.

Nguyet Thi meditation subtly posts you

The high praise of Shurangama shakes the three heavens.

Under the chairmanship of Dharma Master Hai Vien, the monastery was restored, and foreign relations were also opened, allowing the world to admire the Buddha tooth relic, one of two still preserved in the world.

On February 1, 2000, highly virtuous Dharma Master Hai Vien passed away at the age of 96. After cremation, nearly two thousand relics were extracted. Up to now, the statue of Dharma Master Hai Vien has been erected at Linh Quang Pagoda, and there are countless people coming to admire it.

Referring to Dharma Master Hai Vien, Venerable Hai Hien highly praised: “Hai Vien practices, that is not the usual type of diligence! When we are together, he often forgets to eat and sleep!”

The letter that Dharma Master Hai Vien wrote to Venerable Hai Hien several decades ago, every time Venerable Hai Hien received the letter, he would find layperson Vuong Xuan Sanh to read it to him. After "Van Cach", it was because Dharma Master Hai Vien told Venerable Hai Hien in a letter about the trend of religious policy that Lai Buddha Pagoda was promptly rebuilt.

Dharma Master The Quang (1924 - 2005), family member of the Vien family, from Hang Thanh Ha Nam, surnamed An Huyen, 52nd generation of the Lam Te sect, Venerable Hai Hien used to call him "An Huyen". 14-year-old Dharma Master The Quang alone entered Hac Long town, Duong Ha district, Ha Nam province, opened the mountain, and left the home life under the court of Dharma Master Hai Son at Pho Hoa pagoda. His extraordinary nature, having been close to the Venerable Venerable Venerable Hu Van, Dharma Master Vien Anh, meditation master Lai Qua, etc., was so deep that Venerable Hu Van praised him and was recognized as the person who received Venerable Hu Van's heart seal. On January 24, 2005, Dharma Master The Quang passed away.

Dharma Master The Quang all his life persevered in taking precepts as his teacher, taking farming and meditation equally seriously, not eating after noon, wearing a torn robe all year round, even during the "Van Cach" period, years when people left the home life were forced to change their clothes as usual, Dharma Master The Quang still wore the same torn robe as before. Often said: “Leaving the home life must maintain the precepts of sitting meditation, obeying the rules set by the group.” Sinh Tien once held the position of Vice President of the Management Board of the second term of the Jiangxi Province Buddhist Association, head of Dong Lam Lo Son Pagoda, etc.

According to the chronology of Dharma Master The Quang, 19-year-old Dharma Master The Quang, after coming to Bao Thong Temple in Wuhan, Hubei, received full ordination, respectfully went up Linh Mountain.

Nham worshiped the relics of Great Master An Quang, but resided at the ashram for many years.

After that, Dharma Master The Quang went to Van Mon Pagoda to follow Venerable Hu Van to meditate and personally experience the "Van Mon transformation".

When Dharma Master The Quang went to check on the condition of Venerable Hu Van's wound, the Venerable gave him a verse, urging him to leave immediately. The verse read:

disappearing close to the ceiling.

After Dharma Master The Quang left Van Mon Pagoda, he returned to Thap Vien Pagoda on Dong Bach Mountain to live for nearly two years. In the 80s of the twentieth century, he also returned to Dong Bach Mountain many times to visit his old friends. Venerable Hai Hien once told an old story, during the "Van Cach" period, Red Guards severely criticized Dharma Master The Quang.

“The Red Guard let An Huyen stand on a bench, wearing a small mill chopping board around his neck. Who doubts that An Huyen knows how to elaborate! Plug the code set tightly on the bench and it won't budge. There was a red guard who used his foot to kick the bench, but no matter how he kicked it, it didn't budge. He called many people to kick it together. The bench fell, and the red guards also fell. They looked back at An Huyen, still firmly planted on the ground. These Red Guards are terrified and don't dare fight him anymore."

Dharma Master The Quang lived for more than 30 years at Chan Nhu pagoda on Van Cu mountain. Later, at the invitation of Giang Tay followers, from 1990, he became a meditation monk at Tinh Cu pagoda on Thanh Nguyen mountain. Many ancient trees in Tinh Cu pagoda had dried up and died. After Dharma Master The Quang moved Thanh Nguyen mountain pagoda, under extremely arduous conditions, to revive the Patriarch's ashram, the dry trees sprouted new leaves and regained vitality. Dharma Master The Quang was the abbot of Tinh Cu pagoda for 15 years. He founded the Buddhist temple, established the teachings, inherited the tradition of valuing meditation equally in Chinese Buddhism, and revived the Patriarch's ashram until he passed away.

Elderly Venerable Ban Hoan highly praised Dharma Master The Quang and said: “meditation monk The Quang, when he was young, left the home life, became a virgin. Maintain the forbidden precepts and adhere to real learning. Revive the Thanh Nguyen family, continue to promote the family style. Receiving them calmly, virtue and virtue spread far and wide, helping them countlessly. What an example of a monk!”

Before Dharma Master The Quang passed away, he once instructed his disciples in Jiangxi to build a memorial tower on the land where four people meditated together at Thap Vien pagoda in the past. After Dharma Master The Quang passed away, Dharma Master The Quang's disciples solemnly complied with the old Venerable's will, sent people to Lai Buddha Pagoda to pay homage to Venerable Hai Hien, and reported that they wanted to use Dharma Master The Quang's fingernails and hair to build a worship tower. Old Venerable Hai Hien happily praised and immediately went to Thap Vien Pagoda to choose this construction location. Senior Dharma Master Dien Tu of Dharma Master The Quang said: “We chose many places, all of which were a bit unsuitable. noi_dung:
7. Mother rebirth

In 1956, Venerable Hai Hien's mother was 86 years old. After living for 27 years in the mountains, one day, she suddenly mentioned that she wanted to return to her hometown to live. She told Venerable Hai Hien: “Can you let old age die on this mountain top?” Hearing his mother say that, Venerable Hai Hien had to follow his mother's wishes and take her down the mountain to his hometown in Thao Tu village, Duong Ha district.

The house is no more. Venerable Hai Hien first arranged for his mother to live in a neighbor's house, and then went himself to find the village chief for help. With the consent of the village chief, Venerable Hai Hien tidied up the three cottages in the vegetable garden of the production team and moved in with his mother.

One year before the Venerable's rebirth, several lay people from Indonesia paid a visit to the Venerable. The Venerable calmly narrated this rebirth story to everyone.

“In the vegetable garden there are three houses... Why do we have a house? It's from the production team.

I moved in, finished cleaning three rooms, I live there, I have to grow vegetables."

The lay people, who had not yet heard and understood, were very surprised and asked: “Can the old lady still grow vegetables?”

The old Venerable replied a little louder: “We still do it well!

Can do that! We grow vegetables.”

His mother was a vegetarian since childhood, so when the two of them went down the mountain, Venerable Hai Hien still carried his own pot. He said: “Can we eat other people's food? Do not be tempted to break the precepts.”

The old Venerable remembers very clearly, on the 20th day of the 8th lunar month, he and his mother came down from the mountain. Last year, it was also the 5th day of July 1957, and the mother was reborn.

One day before her rebirth, she personally wrapped dumplings to eat, and told Venerable Hai Hien to inform her sister and a cousin, telling them to definitely return the next day. She also entrusted Venerable Hai Hien to help her move her bed outside the room because she wanted to sleep outside. She said to the Venerable: “Teacher, please go sleep outside.”

The Venerable asked: “Why are you sleeping outside, Mom? There are many mosquitoes outside.”

She tilted her head and said: “Can you let me die in this room tomorrow?”

The old Venerable quickly agreed: “Okay! Okay!" He carried the bed and mattress out to the room and placed it right at the door.

The next day, the Venerable Hai Hien's sister and their younger sister both came, and she also cooked rice for everyone.

She pointed to the white sugar and canned food that the two cousins brought and said: “Since I brought it back, can I not feed it to the old man?” She ate all the canned food, even drank all the soup in the can, then informed everyone, saying: "I've drank all the water, I won't eat anymore at noon today."

After lunch, she went to the bathroom to urinate. After coming out, she lay down again for a while, then she said to Venerable Hai Hien: “Teacher, wake up and sit for a bit, okay?”

Venerable Hai Hien said: “It's not as good as mom lying there.”

“That's right! Lie there for a bit, right!” Having finished speaking, he lay down again.

She turned her face away and lay on her side. She then lay there peacefully, then took a deep breath, rebirth. The old monk said this, waving his left hand upward: “There was no abuse!”

The mother of the old Venerable Hai Hien, a lay person, like the old Venerable, did not go to school, was illiterate, just recited the phrase "Amitabha Buddha" for a lifetime. The 87-year-old woman was reborn, knew the time and date in advance, had no illness, and transformed herself into others.

After many years of leaving her hometown, she suddenly proposed to return to her hometown, in fact she wanted to return to her hometown for rebirth. In her hometown, she still had her daughter and granddaughter. She went back to show her daughter and granddaughter, to let them see, a sentence "Amitabha Buddha" can help people die so peacefully. So before her rebirth, she gathered her daughter and granddaughter together, and the whole family reunited very happily. Her daughter, also the older sister of Venerable Hai Hien, saw her mother's unimaginable rebirth, so not long after her mother's rebirth, she took her son with her to Dong Bach mountain to leave the home life.

People who recite Buddha's name know where they come from in life and where they go when they die. They are very happy, without any worries or fears. The task of saving sentient beings in this world has completed one stage, one's own merit is complete, one knows the day and time in advance, does not need the help of others, says and goes immediately, freely reborn.

Shakyamuni Buddha Buddha said, people in the human world have the suffering of birth, old age, sickness, and death. These four types of suffering are not easy for ordinary people to avoid. None of the treasures in the world can relieve the suffering of birth, old age, sickness, and death. If you want to relieve these four types of suffering, this one sentence "Amitabha Buddha" is effective. This one sentence “Amitabha Buddha” is a Dharma Jewel. Old Venerable Hai Hien, his mother Hoang, and his junior brother Dharma Master Hai Khanh, all three of them only have the suffering of birth, not the suffering of old age, illness, or death, this is a manifestation for us to see.

The conditions at that time for Venerable Hai Hien were extremely difficult, the pagodas were small temples in the countryside, there were very few incense burners, everyone relied on himself, hard work and diligence in farming to maintain prosperity, so after three days he recited Buddha's name for his mother, and had to use a thin coffin to bury her simply. He is a filial son, although the situation is pressing, in his heart he is still as uneasy as ever. Because of this, he feels ashamed, thinking that he is at fault with his mother. Eight years later, the situation had changed for the better. Venerable Hai Hien wanted to build a stele to rebury his mother. Unexpectedly, he dug up a grave, opened the coffin, and found no one. Inside there were only a few large nails used to close the coffin.

In Chinese history, there was once an example like this. Sơ tổ Thiền tông Trung Quốc Tổ sư Đạt Ma từ nước Nam Thiên Trúc (cách gọi nước Ấn Độ thời xưa) đến Trung Quốc truyền Pháp, sau khi viên tịch, chôn ở Trung Quốc. After a few months, a person came from Tay Vuc and said he met Patriarch Dat Ma in Tay Vuc. He also said that Patriarch Dat Ma at that time wore a grass shoe on one foot and barefoot on the other. Thời gian này vừa đúng mấy ngày sau khi chôn cất Tổ sư Đạt Ma. People don't believe it, he has passed away, how can he run away to the Western Regions? Then I dug up the coffin and when I opened it, there was no one there. There was only one shoe in the coffin.

After more than a thousand years, we encounter the same story again. Therefore, some people say, is the mother of Venerable Hai Hien the reincarnation of Bodhisattva? In theory, it makes sense to say so, but in the absence of evidence, we ordinary people, without supernatural powers, do not dare to speculate.

noi_dung:
8. Be the captain of the production team

In 1966, the “Great Cultural Revolution” began. The Red Guards went to temples and burned scriptures and Buddha statues, severely criticized and blamed monks, paraded them on the streets, and forced monks to return to the secular life.

Dharma Master An Chi once asked Dharma Master Dien Cuong "Thiet Cuoc Tang", in the past whether Venerable Hai Hien was assigned to the production team or not. If you want to go home, go home.” Venerable Hai Hien said: “I don't have a home, I'm not going home.” Having no other choice, Venerable Hai Hien was arranged to go to Ngo Gia Loan under Dong Bach mountain to participate in labor, he was the head of the production team. Even though he left the temple and went down the mountain to work, he always wore monk's uniform, determined not to return to the secular world, which is truly rare and precious. After many years, when the disciple asked Venerable Hai Hien why he was determined not to return to the secular world, this old man who had not gone to school said: “When you study the Dharma, you know that your mind is the Buddha. When you practice, you should take the precepts as your teacher. Leaving the home life and returning home is not as good as flowers not blooming.”

At that time, reciting the Buddha's name was not allowed, then Venerable

Hai Hien silently chanted in his mind; Prostration is not allowed

Buddha, he bowed silently in the evening. Elaboration of

He does not interrupt.

During the working time in the production team, because Venerable Hai Hien was a loyal and honest person, he treated people harmoniously, everyone wanted to be close to him. The old Venerable's family name was Van, so everyone intimately called him "Van Trai Cong", meaning that he was a vegetarian. When the production team had a group meal, if there was salty food in the pot, he would immediately eat the vegetables next to the pot. “I just stewed some radishes to eat, I stopped my mouth, I didn't eat (salty).” Elder Venerable Hai

Hien said, "My Cong Trai, no matter what, I am not allowed to break the precepts."

Layman Liu once visited the Venerable and asked him: “You have never drank alcohol in your life, have you?”

Venerable Hai Hien said: “Wine? Why didn't you drink when you were young?

“When you were young, did you like to drink alcohol?”

Venerable Hai Hien asked back: “When you were young in the production team, you cleaned people's houses, could you not drink alcohol?”

Layman Luu nodded very understandingly and replied: “Oh, I can't drink it.” “Yes!” A guy next to me chimed in.

Local people like to drink wine, there is a custom, when inviting guests, if the owner drinks wine but the invited guest does not drink, it is impossible, it is disrespectful to the owner.

Layman Liu casually said a sentence that seemed to conclude: “More or less drink a little, right?”

Unexpectedly, old Venerable Hai Hien said with a smiling face: “Approximately a kilo is not enough for me to drink.”

As soon as the voice ended, the lay people at the scene couldn't help but burst into laughter together.

Buddhism is flexible. When Venerable Hai Hien drinks wine here, he opens a predestined relationship, not a precept. His purpose is to make everyone happy, so that everyone can understand Buddha's teachings.

Precepts are prescribed by Buddha for us, the most basic are "killing, religion, lust, and delusion", these four things themselves are sins. Among the five precepts, the last one is called "not drinking alcohol". Drinking alcohol itself has no fault, so this one precept and the previous four precepts are not the same. There is no sin, why do we have to make it a serious precept? Because after getting drunk, you will violate the previous four precepts. Therefore, this precept of "not drinking alcohol" is called the precept, its nature is to be prepared and reserved.

Trinh Huyen was a Great Master of Classics in the last years of the Eastern Han Dynasty, annotated throughout the Confucian classics. After Trinh Huyen drank 300 glasses of wine, even the smallest rituals were not lost. He had a high tolerance for alcohol. Therefore, Master Ly Binh Nam once told his students that if everyone had the same tolerance for alcohol as Trinh Huyen, Buddha's precept of "not drinking alcohol" might not be needed, these precepts would not be needed.

During the time that Venerable Hai Hien was in that production team, working, reciting Buddha, reciting Buddha, labor was still the same as before. During those years, it is not allowed to recite, using the words of Venerable Hai Hien: “People don't allow recitation! Why? It's all 'the masses', do you dare to recite Buddha's name?"

Venerable Hai Hien always obeys all sentient beings. If Buddha is not allowed to recite, he silently recites in his mind; Not allowed to bow to the Buddha, then he silently bowed to the Buddha at night. While tending the buffalo, after he drove the buffalo to the top of the mountain, he sat on a rock and recited Buddha's name. His daily work is uninterrupted, in form some are reduced, but in his heart there is no reduction, his thoughts and thoughts are all Buddha-named.

After the initial period of "Van Cach" passed, the situation relaxed a bit, Venerable Hai Hien left the production team and returned to the temple.

9. Dress up a great cow

Old Venerable Hai Hien, no matter what job he did, was extremely proficient, and also had exceptional wisdom.

When he was the leader of the production team in the village, the production team raised a large buffalo. This buffalo has a very big head and can do things very well, but it is often irritable. If it doesn't want to do something, it doesn't do it. If it lies there, it won't get up. No one can do anything with it. Everyone in the production team said they wanted to sell it. Venerable Hai Hien said: “Don't sell it, I'll negotiate with it slowly.” But he refused to listen and sometimes even got angry.

The big buffalo lies there and does not get up. What should I do? Its appearance is so big that using a stick is not easy to control, because its head is simply too big.

So Venerable Hai Hien then thought of a solution. Isn't the buffalo lying down? Venerable Hai

Hien then used an iron shovel to dig a hole below the buffalo's mouth. After digging a small hole, he took off his shirt, spread it over the small hole, and then tried his best to pull the buffalo's head and press it into the hole. But the buffalo's head is so big and its neck is so thick that it is absolutely impossible to press it. Venerable Hai Hien finished putting on his shirt and wrapped it up, but the buffalo's mouth and nose were completely covered by the shirt. This big buffalo couldn't breathe, so he quickly got up and ran away.

The big buffalo did a little, but didn't want to do it anymore, so he lay down there again. The old monk once again took the iron shovel and walked over. He started digging the hole again, then took off his shirt, spread it over the small hole, wrapped the shirt around the buffalo's mouth and nose, and the big buffalo stood up and ran away.

Then, as soon as it lay down there, the old monk carried an iron shovel and his shirt and walked towards it. As soon as the big buffalo saw it, he quickly stood up and started working. He knew that when he finished digging the small hole, he would be out of breath.

This story was told by the Venerable many times to everyone. "Every time he lay down there, I walked in that direction, took the iron shovel and my shirt in front of him, and he crawled up and quickly ran away." Whenever the old monk mentioned this passage, he would laugh happily.
