noi_dung:
10. The old monk and a python

Venerable Hai Hien throughout his life has depended on fate and destiny, and has never caused the public to have any trouble. He is compassionate towards animals and sincerely treats all living beings with kindness. He always brought money to make offerings, used it as expenses for publishing scriptures and releasing living beings. The old Venerable was a vegetarian in his life and liberated living beings - these two things are both to overcome evil and cultivate good.

In the past, he was on Dong Bach mountain. Every time before starting to work, he had to walk around the ground, one time and then another to notify the small insects on the ground: “Pick and shovel on the ground, insects will stay away.” Then recite the Buddha's signal for a while before starting to cultivate.

Normally, inside and outside the monastery, as long as Venerable Hai Hien sees small animals like dogs and cats, he immediately distributes fruit or food offerings on the Buddha altar for them to eat, but warns everyone not to hit them or hurt them, he said: “These are all sentient beings, just like us humans, they all have spiritual nature.”

Venerable Hai Hien has compassion, he is so precious towards small animals, let alone towards people!

The Venerable once resided at Thap Vien Pagoda on Dong Bach Mountain. Once, while the Venerable was walking on the mountain, he saw a snake on the side of the road that was pinned down by a large rock, unable to walk. This small snake was about a meter long. The rock was when the mountain massif rolled down from the mountain. The old monk took out the stone, only to see that the snake had been crushed to near death, not moving. The old monk was afraid that it would be hurt by passersby, so he pulled it to the side of the road, where people wouldn't step on it. The Venerable chanted Buddha's name for it, and after taking refuge for it, he left.

Later, this snake knew to periodically go to Thap Vien Pagoda to visit Venerable Hai Hien. In general, he could go several times a year. He also knew that he would stay for a period of time at the monastery before leaving.

This snake gets bigger and bigger, how big is it? Big and rough like the mouth of a large cup or tea cup; The beam in the room is about four meters long. It crawls up the beam, its body stretches from one end of the beam to the other end, and its head can even hang down. He kept going to visit the Venerable, because he had often gone since he was little, so the Venerable knew him and knew that this was the snake he had saved, so he was not afraid.

This snake is not afraid of the Venerable, every time

I'll play there for a while, I don't know when I'll leave. People who often go to Thap Vien Pagoda have encountered this snake more than once.

One time, a pregnant woman avoided the family planning department's inspection and went to stay for several days in Thap Vien pagoda. One day she went out, and when she returned, she pushed open the door and saw that big snake. She was so scared that she fainted on the spot. I don't know how long it took before I woke up. She didn't dare stay in the monastery anymore, so she quickly left.

The old monk severely criticized the snake, telling it not to go out and scare people. The snake was very obedient, and later when he came to the monastery, he curled up gently on the rafters and did not go out to roam around again.

It was not until after the Venerable went to Lai Buddha Pagoda that this snake did not come to Thap Vien Pagoda again.

11. THE MIDDLE STORY

tieu_de: 11. The story between the Venerable and the wolf
tom_tat: Lão Hòa thượng Hải Hiền xuất gia 92 năm, gặp phải sự việc chỉ là một câu Phật hiệu, không có niệm thứ hai. He encountered many obstacles and accidents, the most dangerous of which was meeting a wolf on the mountain. Question…
noi_dung:
11. The story between the Venerable and the wolf

Lão Hòa thượng Hải Hiền xuất gia 92 năm, gặp phải sự việc chỉ là một câu Phật hiệu, không có niệm thứ hai. He encountered many obstacles and accidents, the most dangerous of which was meeting a wolf on the mountain. This story was told by Dharma Master An Sanh during the dharma conference to establish a stele commemorating the hundred days of Venerable Hai Hien's return to the West.

Twenty years ago, one day the Venerable Hai Hien went to the mushroom hut to visit Dharma Master An Sanh, carrying a block of mountain honey in his hand. Dharma Master An Sanh asked: “Where does the honey come from?” The old Venerable then told the Dharma Master about his strange plight.

This day, the old Venerable Hai Hien went to Giai Gia Ha to work, passed by Thai Dam Cau, on a narrow winding road on a high steep cliff, a big wolf stood with its face raised, it was truly a narrow alley. The old Venerable deeply believed in cause and effect, so he did not avoid it, of course there was no place to avoid it, his mind thought: If it's a life debt, then you should repay your life. Just eat me and you'll have paid the debt. In His mouth, just recite Buddha's name.

Who would have thought that this wolf would come in front of the Venerable, bite down on his trouser leg, and keep dragging him inside the wolf's den of the cave. As soon as the Venerable looked, it turned out that a mother wolf had difficulty giving birth. The old Venerable understood that this male wolf did not want to eat Him, but hoped to receive His help. He closed his eyes, concentrated, and began to recite Buddha dedicating merit. After more than 10 minutes, the mother wolf gave birth to a litter of baby wolves.

The male wolf bowed his head before the Venerable, bowing his head in gratitude.

So the Venerable taught the male wolf: "You must reduce your evil deeds and do more good deeds. In the future, don't go down the path of animal birth again. How good it will be to achieve Buddhahood!"

The Venerable makes no distinction. He treats all sentient beings the same as Buddha; He can let go of all conditions, use a pure mind, and practice Bodhisattva with equality, helping all living beings to leave suffering and be happy.

The second day, the old monk returned from Giai Gia Ha after finishing his work. As soon as he got there, he discovered that male wolf was waiting for him on the small road. The male wolf stopped the old monk, then took out a piece of mountain honey from the grass cave, placed it in front of the old monk, and then began to bow his head to him, once again expressing his gratitude.

Having said this, the old monk told Dharma Master An Sanh: “An Sanh! You see, this wild animal also knows how to repay favors!”

Dharma Master An Sanh was both moved and moved at the same time.

The magician joked with the old monk: “Master! I'm a male comrade, but I didn't expect that this time I would even be a midwife!" The old monk also laughed.

During the time that Dharma Master An Sanh knew the Venerable Hai Hien for a long time, it was natural to know a little more about the things that happened to the Venerable. The shaman said, in the past, when the old Venerable lived at Thap Vien Pagoda, people saw that the old Venerable did not know how to lecture the sutras and preach the Dharma, and only worried about working all day, so he did not care and did not pay attention to the old Venerable and many things that happened around him.

When Venerable Hai Hien was still alive, no one did not respect him, no one did not seriously commit to studying him. It's clear that he was a saint, and everyone treated him like a normal person, and that's still the case today.

tom_tat: Lai Buddha Pagoda, located in An Trang village, Nhieu Luong town, Xa Ky district, Nam Duong city, Ha Nam province. The land of Xa Ky city district is called "Trung Nguyen De Nhat Ancient Town", Lai Buddha Pagoda is also a historical and cultural pagoda built...
noi_dung:
12. Lai Buddha ancient text

Lai Buddha Pagoda, located in An Trang village, Nhieu Luong town, Xa Ky district, Nam Duong city, Ha Nam province. The land of Xa Ky city district is called "Trung Nguyen De Nhat Ancient Town", Lai Buddha Pagoda is also a pagoda with deep cultural history accumulated over many years. According to the records on the inscription, the pagoda began to be built during the Sui Tang Dynasty and was rebuilt in 1976. At present, the pagoda occupies an area of nine acres, of which arable land is six acres and five parts, with 21 rooms. In the Vajra Pavilion of the eastern main hall, there is a gilded statue of the body of Bodhisattva Dharma Master Hai Khanh, which has been worshiped for more than 10 years now.

Legend has it that in the Sui Duong years, there was a layman who sold food in Duong Sach town, driving a buffalo cart to Nguyen Dam town to sell food, and encountered three old men coming with him. Going late at night, he stopped the car on the side of the road to rest. Early the next morning, he saw three old men who had transformed into three stone Buddhas.

Therefore, the believers started building the ashram right here, named "Lai Buddha Tu", meaning that Buddha Da reincarnated to this place.

Another legend is that when the layman Vuong saw three stone Buddhas in the middle of the road, each statue had a silver bar on its head. Layman Vuong then used these three silver ingots to organize followers in the village to change the Vuong's palace into a temple to worship the three Buddhas (three stone statues). Because the pagoda was rebuilt by the Tu Duong Vuong family, there is also a local manager who calls this place "Vuong Duong Mieu", later taking the name "Lai Buddha Tu", which is still used to this day.

Before the "Great Cultural Revolution", the monastery's architecture had a heroic spirit, the inner courtyard had stone stele and cedar over thousands of years old, extremely solemn, the three stone Buddhas were famous far and wide. During the mid-50s of the 20th century, the current abbot, Dharma Master In Tang, was a Buddhist representative from Tat Duong district (At that time Xa Ky district had not yet been established) to a conference organized by the Chinese Buddhist Association.

The first stage of the "Great Cultural Revolution". The Red Guards came to the temple, they burned scriptures, burned Buddha statues, three Stone Buddhas were pulled down and broken, all the trees in the temple were cut down, ancient trees and even their roots were dug up, the temple was destroyed, not even a single tile remained, Lai Buddha Pagoda became a wasteland.

The Dharma Masters of the monastery were all arranged to work in the production team, Dharma Master Hai Khanh was among them at that time. Local farmers and the old dharma protectors of the monastery lamented somewhat sadly: “It's not just being forced to do simple things like that! At that time, if he moved a little, the person blaming him would drag him out and parade him on the street. Today we see Khanh Cong achieving such great achievements, who knows how many insults and curses he endured!

Trung Kien Lai Buddha Temple

At the end of 1976, the old Venerable from Dong Bach Mountain went to the village where Lai Buddha Pagoda was to visit Dharma Master Hai Khanh, and also brought with him a letter from Dharma Master Hai Vien sent back from Beijing. The letter said: The "Van Cach" has ended, the religious policy will lift the blockade, and the destroyed ashram can be prepared to be restored. Everyone was extremely excited after receiving this news and immediately began to promote and restore Lai Buddha Pagoda.

The restoration of the monastery was difficult and many times encountered many problems, and in the end a few thatched cottages were built in the east. At that time, there was no statue of Buddha Bodhisattva, so we had to invite an artist to paint a statue of the Western Three Saints on white cotton for worship.

Many lay dharma protectors of Nam Duong and Xa Ky arranged to meet together at Thap Vien Pagoda on Dong Bach Mountain to invite Venerable Hai Hien to preside over the ashram of Lai Buddha Pagoda, but at that time Venerable Hai Hien was preparing to restore Thap Vien Pagoda, so he sent four disciples to permanently reside at Lai Buddha Pagoda first. He himself only came to stay occasionally for a period of time. Later, after experiencing many difficulties, the lay people demanded seven or eight acres of land for the monastery, so they built a few rooms in the north, this place is the main hall today. Therefore, Lai Buddha Pagoda only built the main hall and the Arhat hall, each with three rooms. Until today, the Buddha statues worshiped in the temple are all clay statues.

The monastery was built very simply and rustically, beneficial for cultivating the mind and cultivating the Dharma. The old Venerable Hai Hien of this generation was truly very cautious and sure. Regarding the construction of the ashram, he often said: "Not afraid of not having a temple, just afraid of not having religion." Around 1981, the Venerable Hai Hien came to live permanently at Lai Buddha Pagoda. In the fall of that year, everyone started plowing and preparing to plant barley. The layman Vuong, who invited Venerable Hai Hien to preside over the ashram, one day on the way home, passing by the monastery, saw 81-year-old Venerable Hai Hien and 72-year-old Dharma Master Hai Khanh busy working in the fields, one holding an iron harrow and digging, the other holding an iron shovel. He felt very uncomfortable in his heart, so he told them to quickly stop. But old Venerable Hai Hien said: “If you don't master plowing the land, you'll miss out on growing wheat.”

Layman Vuong complained that: "If you have any work to do, come find me. How can I let you do such a difficult job?"

The Venerable said: "You are also private households, nothing can bother you."

Layman Vuong was moved and said: "In the future, you can't say that anymore. If you have something to do, you must come to me. Even if it's my own work, I'll leave it there, and I'll have to finish it for you first." Otherwise, everyone would know that I took the lead in inviting you here. As a result, you have come here to suffer, do I still have the face to protect this Dharma? None of you monks are allowed to dig any more. Now I will go home and take my buffalo out here to plow."

Bodhisattva Bodhisattva Body

In a small temple in the village, although it did not seem to attract attention, two real Bodhisattvas appeared, one was the old Venerable Hai Hien, and there was also an extraordinary, accomplished Dharma Master, that was Dharma Master Hai Khanh. Dharma Master Hai Khanh is the same as Venerable Hai Hien, he did not go to school and was illiterate. They both have one thing in common: they are both old people, they are both obedient, and they are both real doers.

Master Hai Khanh is also from Ha Nam. He left the home life at the age of 11. At the age of 42, he came to live permanently at Lai Buddha Pagoda. He specialized in practicing Pure Land. He recited Buddha's name. People around Lai Buddha Pagoda all know that Dharma Master Hai Khanh treats people with kindness and honesty, has a gentle personality, and only knows how to recite "Amitabha Buddha". He spoke with a very heavy stutter. Only when he was reciting "Amitabha Buddha" did he speak clearly.

Master Hai Khanh lived a miserable life, but he was very happy. In the ashram, other people did not want to do the heavy work, but he did it all, but also did it to bring joy to the mind. A life that takes precepts as its teacher and suffering as its teacher. When He was alive, no one took Him seriously, but the mortals of the world saw Him wrongly. He left behind an indestructible diamond body. This is not something an ordinary person can do.

In December 1991, 82-year-old Dharma Master Hai Khanh was freely born in the West. After sitting in the jar for six years and nine months, the Venerable Hai Hien made the intention to enter the stupa for him. The jar was opened, only to see Dharma Master Hai Khanh sitting cross-legged, looking as if he were still alive, even his clothes were not damaged at all, the four disciples immediately worshiped his body in the temple. On the 1st and 15th, people all go to worship the body of Dharma Master Hai Khanh; Any family encountering difficulties will come to pray for this Bodhisattva body.

Lai Buddha Temple, because of the appearance of Bodhisattva's physical body, also became a bit bustling.

Sometime before or after the year 2000, there were a few people from the South who came, they came to the old Venerable Hai Hien, negotiated with the Venerable and said that Lai Buddha Pagoda was too sketchy, feeling sorry for Bodhisattva's body, they were willing to give fifty thousand coins to the temple, to bring the body of Dharma Master Hai Khanh to a big pagoda in the South to worship. Old Venerable Hai Hien was extremely wise. He did not directly refuse, but told them: “I haven't been in this temple since the beginning of the world, I can't make decisions! You go to the village to find layperson Vuong Xuan Sanh, this pagoda was rebuilt by him, you have to negotiate with him."

These people were very obedient and went to find layman Vuong to negotiate. Layman Vuong heard what they said, was both angry and laughed, and said to them: "Don't say you give fifty thousand dong to the pagoda. Even if you brought us 100 dong to bring three trains back, all using pure gold to build the halls of Lai Buddha Pagoda, we still cannot hand over Khanh Cong's body to you!"

Later, there were several more similar antics.

Lost Thief Meets Robber

Lai Buddha Pagoda is in the village, the countryside is poor, the land is poor, for many years no one is making offerings, life is very poor. During Buddha Bodhisattva's birthday, people came to the temple more often and provided blankets and mattresses for everyone to rest and had to go into the village to borrow from the people. When Mage Hai Khanh reborn, he didn't even have a standard uniform on his body.

On the one hand, the pagoda does not have incense making offerings all year round, on the other hand, people constantly come to the pagoda to steal - some lucky precious artifacts are left, plowing buffaloes are stolen, the lock on the merit box has been picked off countless times...

During his years at Lai Buddha Pagoda, Venerable Hai Hien endured all kinds of hardships. It was not until more than ten years before the Venerable's rebirth that the situation changed for the better, but similar incidents still arise from time to time.

In the fall of 2012, the old Venerable returned from Buddha's Recitation in Yiwu, Indonesia. As soon as he arrived, he immediately picked up a hoe and went to the fields. Three young men rode a motorbike to find the old monk, saying they wanted to exchange some change, the old monk said "no", as a result, two young men in the group held the old monk tightly, another person robbed all the lay people's money.

Nam Duong making offerings that the Venerable has in his possession.

There are also people who do not understand cause and effect, borrow money from the Venerable Master, and after many years of borrowing, refuse to pay it back. The old Venerable had compassion and ordered Dharma Master An Thuyen to come and repent. Who would have thought that the person who borrowed the money not only did not pay back, but also spoke without humility, scolding the old Venerable that he was about to go to the bottom, still not forgetting to collect the debt, can this money still be used after death?

Guarding the Monastery

Old Venerable Hai Hien at Lai Buddha Pagoda lived quiet days but was poor. Fortunately, he understood farming and was diligent. He loved to work and never had a single idle day.

In the summer of 2007, several followers went to Lai Buddha Pagoda to visit Venerable Hai Hien. The temple door was open, there was no one in the yard, they waited for a long time before the Venerable returned, it turned out he was alone working in the fields! The Venerable said: "Currently, I live alone in the temple. Farm work comes and I can't do it. Farm work doesn't wait for anyone."

Hearing the Venerable's story, several people's hearts suddenly felt heavy: More than 100 years old, here alone, tenaciously maintaining, still working so many fields, not even a caregiver nearby, the weather is very hot, working in the fields at noon, returning home and having to cook and wash clothes, even a young person can't stand it!

Some well-meaning people advise: “You are over 100 years old, and you still work so hard every day. In the end, what do you seek? With his status, it is completely possible to come to the ashram with good conditions and live peacefully through old age!”

The Venerable said: “If a person leaving the home life cannot keep his own ashram or temple, then what is the point of practicing? Do you let people speak in a pleasant way?

Venerable Hai Hien's household registration was more than 100 kilometers away in Dong Bach district, but he always wanted to transfer his household registration to Lai Buddha pagoda. He said that he had lived for decades at Lai Buddha Pagoda, so it was like the fallen leaves returned to their roots, and I also wanted to transfer my household registration here. In 2012, one year before His rebirth, under many urgings, two lay people together went through the procedures to transfer household registration to the Venerable Hai Hien. The first time I went, due to missing part of the proof from the Huong Dinh village police station at Lai Buddha pagoda, it could not be transferred within the day. A few days later, we continued on and transferred the Venerable's household registration to Lai Buddha Pagoda.

The Venerable was 111 years old. When he learned that his household registration had been transferred to Lai Buddha Pagoda, he happily said: "I have lived at Lai Buddha Pagoda for decades, my household registration is still outside, I want to transfer my household registration back soon, but today I am finally satisfied." He smiled very happily.

In the fall of 2008, the old Venerable solemnly entrusted Lai Buddha Pagoda to his disciple Dharma Master An Chi. Regarding the management of the monastery, He told Dharma Master An Chi: "Don't be afraid of not having a temple, just be afraid of not having religion." He also advised Dharma Master An Chi: "Neither deaf nor blind, not worthy of being an abbot", meaning to tell the Dharma Master to be patient and yield.

This small temple is in the countryside, it is easy to be overlooked, no one wants to live, no one comes to compete, people who truly practice here will have a peaceful mind. Old Venerable Hai Hien lived here peacefully for decades, did not compete with people, did not seek from the world, he completely relied on a farming life, so he did not ask anyone, did not need anyone to make offerings, at rebirth he showed a good appearance, using this to save sentient beings.

After the Venerable's rebirth

After the old Venerable's rebirth, the abbot of Lai Buddha Pagoda, Dharma Master An Chi solemnly announced a few things.

First, because Lai Buddha Pagoda has thoroughly inherited the old Venerable Hai Hien's family style, in the future it will not allow registration (i.e., staying in the temple), which is to say, whether it is a Dharma Master leaving the home life or a lay person, if he wants to stay at Lai Buddha Pagoda, all monasteries will not welcome him.

Second, if someone comes to Lai Buddha Pagoda to admire the relics, including the tomb tower of Venerable Hai Hien and the body of Dharma Master Hai Khanh, the temple welcomes it, but does not accept money from making offerings. The monastery hopes to maintain its own family style, growing its own crops to maintain its own living expenses. This is the family style formed by the old Venerable Hai Hien who worked 92 years without rest, truly practicing farming and practicing.

Third, if you are interested in recording optical discs or publishing scriptures and making them yourself, that's fine. Please do not send money to Lai Buddha Pagoda. The monastery is not large, there are not many people leaving the home life, I hope to be able to let those leaving the home life practice with Buddha in mind, not tired of other things.

Finally, the teaching style of Lai Buddha Pagoda is a sentence "Amitabha Buddha" recited to the end, without participating in any other debate, "If we want the Buddha's Dharma to flourish, only the Sangha will praise the Sangha."

Currently, at Lai Buddha Pagoda, there are about 20 people staying, persistently staying in Buddha's room all year round, only chanting Buddha's words.

Lay disciples and disciples leaving the home life both make vows to take Venerable Hai Hien as an example, following the teachings of Venerable Hai Hien: A Buddha verse recites to the end, taking precepts as a teacher, taking suffering as a teacher, six harmony ashrams, hundred rings, family style, hard work, thrift, bringing Buddha Dharma to fully implement in life, work and dealing with people.

tieu_de: 13. A day without work, a day without eating
tom_tat: Dharma Master An Quang, Patriarch of the Pure Land Sect of China, teaches us that in our time, the smaller the ashram, the better, because there is no need to worry about entertaining or taking care of guests, so we can use it ourselves.
noi_dung:
13. A day without work, a day without eating

Dharma Master An Quang, Patriarch of the Pure Land Sect of China, teaches us that in our time, the smaller the ashram, the better, because there is no need to worry about entertaining or taking care of guests, so we can put our own effort into it.

Lai Buddha Pagoda is not large, there are only five residents, sometimes even less. This small temple in the middle of the village has no one coming to burn incense all year round. No incense sticks, no making offerings. The economic base on which the temple survives depends entirely on agriculture. If it were not for diligent cultivation, the temple's livelihood would have been difficult.

"A day without work, a day without eating", this is the style left by the Tang Dynasty. People who practice true religion, inside and out, from ancient times to the present, are extremely pale in terms of desire for material enjoyment. After Buddhism was transmitted to China, Master Bach Truong promoted self-sufficiency and promoted agriculture, which was the economic source of the pagodas. Having had this origin, the person leaving the home life can no longer rely on people, not make karma, not donate, then his mind will be concentrated, no longer fraught with karma. Old Venerable Hai Hien was illiterate, his life's work was farming. Master An Chi said: "Master, all your life you have been a pure and honest farmer, an old man, a dedicated farmer. You have truly never left the land all your life, but the Venerable appears to be the general of leaving the home life."

Whenever it was the temple where the old Venerable resided or the Buddha hall, he often went to Thien Buddha pagoda, Lai Buddha pagoda, Vien Minh pagoda, Lam Xa Ky lay people, Yiwu Nam Duong Buddha chanting, Luc Phuong Buddha street, there were many tools and farming tools used in his work: Axes, hammers, saws, picks and hoes, etc., put together seem like a large collection of tools! Wherever the Venerable went, he often heard a saying that others described him as: "He is not free every day from morning to night, but he does all kinds of work." If he doesn't do this, he does that. If he sees that he has free time, then he must sit there quietly chanting "Amitabha Buddha".

From 2008 to 2009, Venerable Hai Hien lived at Thien Buddha Pagoda for one year. One winter day

In 2008, the Venerable was digging a very large tree stump in front of the monastery. In the ground he had dug a large, very deep hole, filled with clay all over the Venerable's body and face. Dharma Master An Ham, abbot of Thien Buddha Pagoda, said next to him: “Master, don't dig any more, the stump is so big, when will you dig? Throw it there until it composts itself."

The old Venerable did not stop, he continued digging and said: “Whatever you do, don't be afraid to make it difficult, I won't stop digging, you can still dig up anyway. If you dig it up, you can cook it, and the bare land can grow vegetables. I'll leave it here and wait until it composts itself. When should I wait?"

At this time, three young men came in from outside, they came to visit the Venerable. Wizard An Ham shook his head, looking confused, he turned around and said to a young man he knew among them: “I originally welcomed him here to let him enjoy those few days of quiet blessings, but instead he did my work for me. I'm not free all day from morning to night, no matter how much advice he gives me, he doesn't listen, I really have no choice but to deal with him!" As he spoke, he turned around and walked out to the backyard.

The old Venerable did not stop, but at this moment turned his head away, looking at the figure of Dharma Master An Ham, smiling like a child.

Dharma Master An Chi describes his master as “really adorable”! The teacher said: "The Venerable is most respected by everyone. The Venerable has that lovely appearance, that loving appearance, there is truly no words to describe!"

Wherever the old monk went, he did not rest.

One day, the Venerable had a New Year's Eve celebration at Thap Vien Pagoda. On the morning of the first day of the New Year, it was snowing heavily and heavily, and everyone suddenly discovered that the Venerable had disappeared. The Dharma Masters in the pagoda were all very urgent, hastily calling the layperson Vuong of Thanh Tuyen Pagoda on Dong Bach Mountain, Dharma Master An Sanh, the abbot of Thanh Tuyen Pagoda, and the layperson Vuong, two people heard the news immediately from Thanh Tuyen Pagoda and rushed to Thap Vien Pagoda.

The snowfall was so heavy, the footprints of people who had just passed by were immediately covered in white snow. The snow on the ground did not leave any traces, everyone had absolutely no way to judge which direction the old Venerable was going. A group of people searched for a long time without reaching their goal, without any harvest. At this time, everyone began to feel uneasy, worried that the Venerable would make a mistake. They impatiently aimed towards the top of the mountain and called out the Venerable's name.

Just when everyone had to give up, they suddenly discovered that on the top of the mountain there seemed to be a figure moving down the mountain. Everyone said that this could not be the old monk, because the snow and wind were too strong, even young people would not dare to casually go to the top of the mountain at this time, not to mention that he was over 100 years old? Everyone discussed without moving their eyes, glued to that person's silhouette, worried that he would disappear from sight. The figure slowly approached from far away, and finally saw clearly, only to see the old monk carrying a dry tree the size of a bowl on his shoulder, walking slowly but steadily. Everyone rushed forward, holding the dry branch on the Venerable's shoulder. The old monk smiled at everyone and said cheerfully: “Come on, let's go get warm!” Having said that, he left immediately. Leaving these people in the same place, they stared at each other for a while, not knowing whether to laugh or cry.

Regardless of whether the wind blew or snow fell, the Venerable always wanted to work whenever he had free time. One time, during the rapeseed harvest, suddenly there was torrential rain. Everyone ran towards the temple's main gate to avoid the rain. The old monk alone took the sickle and ran into the field. As soon as he entered the field, the sun appeared, the rain stopped, and the old monk alone began harvesting canola.

The old Venerable had no free time from day to night. He could always find something to do. One winter day in 2008, it was very cold. The Venerable was alone working in front of the big gate of Thien Buddha Pagoda. In the distance, he saw a lay person driving towards the pagoda. He smiled and greeted her: “Amitabha Buddha, you're back! It's cold on the street, get inside quickly!"

The layman stopped the car and asked him: “It's so cold, why are you still here working?”

The Venerable said: “The grass is growing on this side of the road, we have to do it now, it's unsightly to look at, and it's not convenient for children and students to walk around. I think using a shovel to level this grass, then brush it again, it's easy to walk on and easy to see."

The Venerable was truly compassionate towards others to the extreme. He always thought about others, not himself.

A day without work, a day without eating. He lived one day and worked one day, working diligently, not at all lazy, not at all avoiding hardship. Master Khai Trung, who often had the opportunity to be close to the Venerable, said that the Venerable had "hard work and patience that surpasses ordinary people"!

In front of the small room of Thien Buddha Pagoda where the old Venerable lived, in the past was also the road that students passed by going to and after school, the top was covered with rubble and hard, very hard rocks. He said that now no one uses this road anymore, the land is empty, it's a pity! So I used a hoe and a shovel to dig through the bricks and stones on the road, truly "work sharpens iron, one day you will make money". After many days of tireless labor, the small road had been abandoned, this unusually hard road surface had actually been repaired by the Venerable to become loose, flat karma farmland. He personally peeled each peanut seed, then sowed it evenly into the soil. From leveling the land to sowing seeds, He did it all himself.

Heaven did not disappoint people, that fall brought joy and great harvest.

Behind the main hall of the pagoda, there is also a very narrow piece of empty land. Venerable Hai Hien also carefully picked the worms, then planted some sweet potatoes, also reaping the same excitement.

The Venerable One day before his rebirth, he still worked during the day like every other day. He worked all day, pulling weeds, watering, and leveling the soil in the vegetable garden. The so-called work one day. The monk rings the bell one day, one day does not work, one day does not eat. Old Venerable Hai Hien is really serious and responsible for his work. He respects things, respects things, respects work - respects karma.

4. WHATEVER

SERVANT,

noi_dung:
14. Tell the servant to serve everything, then you will go backwards

Don't Bother People

The land of Lai Buddha Pagoda is located in a remote and not wealthy place, the temple has no one making offerings, and the food depends on growing it yourself. In the fields outside the monastery, almost every day one can see the figure of old Venerable Hai Hien, digging the ground, pulling weeds, growing food, growing vegetables, and cleaning the yard, picking up manure and gathering firewood... From morning to night, inside and out, it's constantly busy.

One time, a lay monk saw the old monk chopping wood in the temple and advised him: "If you're so old, don't do these jobs anymore. You're too tired, what should you do?"

He smiled and said: “Being a human has many jobs! If you can do it yourself, do it yourself, don't expect others."

The old Venerable doesn't like causing trouble to others. If he can do it himself, he definitely won't let others do it. Unless he actually can't do it himself, then let others help. He washed all his own belongings and clothes; His clothes were torn, he installed a thimble and sewed it himself, never opening his mouth to bother others; Saws, hammers, pliers, and wrenches used while working, he went to the street to buy them himself. He has a healthy body, works diligently, has fluent movements, and meticulous manual work. He said: "I can still walk, my eyes are not dizzy, I can do it myself, I have to ask people to serve me everything, so I'm going backwards."

This word "backward", in addition to having the meaning of retreating, retreating, is also used to describe, because of a decline in will or encountering difficulties.

That year, when preparing to restore and rebuild Lai Buddha Pagoda, layperson Vuong Xuan Sanh went to Dong Bach Mountain to invite the Venerable Hai Hien to preside over the ashram of Lai Buddha Pagoda, but the Venerable at that time was preparing to restore Thap Vien Pagoda, so he only sent four disciples to Lai Buddha Pagoda. He himself stayed at Thap Vien Pagoda, only occasionally having to go to Lai Buddha Pagoda to stay for a few days. At that time, there were very few cars, so every time the Venerable walked to Lai Buddha Pagoda, he had to travel more than 120 - 130 miles. Although it was said that at that time, His body was still as good as a young man's, but after all, he was still in his 70s.

Layman Vuong very sincerely said to the Venerable: “Master! Don't go back on your own, when I drive to call you, you will come back." But the old Venerable did not bother him, and each time he still walked there on his own.

Even if the old Venerable is over 100 years old, he is still the same. He can walk without bothering others. There was a time when the Venerable had to stay at the Thien Buddha Pagoda of Dharma Master An Ham's disciple for a period of time. During that time, he sometimes had to go out to work. The bus station is approximately 5 miles from Thien Buddha Pagoda, the Venerable often gets off the bus and walks home. He refused to spend money to rent a car, nor did he agree to bother his disciples to pick him up. He was thrifty and hard-working all his life, and everywhere he put helping others and making it convenient for others first, and adding to his own hardship was not important.

Lay people in Nam Duong often welcome the Venerable to recite Buddha's name in Nam Duong and stay for a few days. Every time he left, an enthusiastic young layperson in charge of welcoming him would tell the Venerable: “If you have anything to do, just tell them to call me at any time, call me at any time. If you want to go somewhere to play, I will immediately take you there."

The Venerable never once went out to play, but sometimes he could go to Tay Hiep district, 100 kilometers away from Nam Duong city, to buy rosaries. Every time that time came, the Venerable always asked layperson Vuong how many days before: “Is there anything going on these days?” Surely after hearing layman Vuong say "not too busy", the old Venerable told him to think and prepare time to go to Tay Hiep district, so that layman Vuong could arrange a driver to take him there.

Elderly Venerable Hai Hien loved to string rosaries himself. His bag always contained many souvenirs such as Buddha statues, jewelry, and rosaries, ready to marry the public when possible.

The old Venerable treated people carefully and thoughtfully. Every time after layman Vuong brought him back to the monastery, he would find some local specialties such as sweet potatoes and peanuts to give to him. Layman Vuong wanted to make him happy, so each time he obediently and happily accepted them.

Embroidery Sewing

Image of the old Venerable teaching and advising his disciples: “Eat hard, wear mended clothes; If you want to be a monk, you must be a lady."

Not only did the old Venerable often go to places with tools that he used to work. Even at the age of 112, wherever he went, he would still carry with him small tools such as a needle and thread bag, a hammer, and scissors. His eyes were not blurred and he could still thread a needle and sew clothes.

In March 2012, Dharma Master An Vinh, the abbot of Vien Minh Pagoda, welcomed the Venerable to Vien Minh Pagoda to stay for a few days. The magician gave his master a monk's robe, the old monk took it, tried it on, the robe was a bit long, so he immediately started fixing the robe himself. He sat on a chair at the corner of the wall outside the yard, put on this shiny new robe, took out the needle and thread he brought with him, rolled up a bottom border of the slightly long robe, held the needle in his left hand, and with his right hand he finished fixing the edge of the robe one line at a time.

The 112-year-old monk's eyes are not dizzy, he doesn't need to wear glasses even for sewing work, and he can re-stitch once and be successful. He was proficient in sewing and did the work beautifully. The bottom edge that He sewed, seen from the inside, the needle lines are very even; Looking from the outside, you can't see the needle lines. An elderly laywoman, watching from the side, couldn't help but reach out and grab a piece of the piece the old monk had sewn, meticulously looking back and forth at the old monk's workmanship, she could only feel emotion.

Up the Tree to Pick Roses

The old Venerable did not want to cause more trouble for people. During the few years before his rebirth, he kept saying: “I want to take the time to recite Buddha and pray to Buddha Amitabha

Da came to pick me up. When you're old, if you don't go, it will cause more trouble for you."

In fact, until before his rebirth, He was completely able to take care of himself and did not need the service and care of others. At 112 years old, he still did all kinds of work himself, had followers come to visit Him, and He even climbed up on the tree to pick roses for everyone.

On the 9th day of the 8th lunar month, 2012, several Indonesian lay people went to Lai Buddha Pagoda to visit the Venerable Hai Hien. The Venerable was very happy and moved the wooden ladder himself, like a young person, climbing up the pagoda's persimmon tree to pick roses. No need to say how healthy His body is.

Before long, the Venerable picked a basket full of persimmons. After coming down, the old monk brought a few persimmons that still had leaves, one by one and distributed them to each lay person. Seeing the old Venerable there from top to bottom, inside and out busy with everyone, the lay people present, in addition to being in awe and amazement and praising, were all moved by the old Venerable's compassion and sincerity. When everyone took the persimmon from the Venerable's hand, when they held it in their hearts, tears welled up in their eyes.

15. IT IS POSSIBLE TO SUFFER

tieu_de: 15. Only by being able to endure suffering can suffering end
tom_tat: Every day at three o'clock in the morning, he woke up. After waking up, he lit incense, bowed to the Buddha, recited the Buddha's name, circumambulated the Buddha - this was his morning session, after which a day of work began. Studying Buddha for 92 years, can...
noi_dung:
15. Only by being able to endure suffering can suffering end

Every day at three o'clock in the morning, he woke up. After waking up, he lit incense, bowed to the Buddha, recited the Buddha's name, circumambulated the Buddha - this was his morning session, after which a day of work began. Studying Buddha for 92 years, being able to do that every day, is indeed very difficult.

He suffered in all his life. When he was 12 years old, his hometown had a severe drought, the farmers had no harvest, his father had to go out to beg for food, and on the way he was beaten to death by bandits. He himself also went to beg for food. He knows that it is natural for him to suffer a little now, "if you can endure suffering, you can end suffering". Therefore, he is courageous and diligent.

Shakyamuni Buddha Before entering nirvana, Venerable Ananda asked the Buddha: Buddha is alive, we rely on Buddha as our teacher. Buddha is no longer alive, so who do we rely on as our teacher? Shakyamuni Buddha Buddha said two sentences: "Take precepts as your teacher, take suffering as your teacher."

A life of poverty makes us have a mind of renunciation. A person who practices, cannot maintain the precepts, cannot endure suffering, cannot escape the six paths of samsara.

For those who recite Buddha's name, the goal is to seek rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. So a person who practices Buddhism, regardless of lay, leaving the home life, life can be poor - at best.

In the life of the old Venerable Hai Hien, he did not need anyone to take care of him, he took care of himself, all his life he accepted to suffer, especially he could endure suffering, he told the lay people who came to the temple to recite Buddha's name: "When you come here, you must be able to endure suffering. If you can endure suffering, then you can end suffering."

The old Venerable had never enjoyed anything in his life. One year before his rebirth, some Indonesian lay people interviewed the Venerable once. Everyone was very interested in the Venerable's experiences and asked many questions. The Venerable told them that in the past, he herded buffaloes, plowed fields, and did manual labor... In Dong Bach mountain, 14 wild mountains have been reclaimed. “Do you think I enjoy it?” The old monk smiled and asked back. Without waiting for the lay people to answer, He continued: “I'm not enjoying it!”

When the Venerable has the opportunity, he will remind everyone: "Reciting the Buddha's name to practice must be able to endure suffering, take suffering as a teacher, take precepts as a teacher, cannot seek making offerings, enjoy." He spoke in a very iconic Ha Nam accent: “Suffer it, wear it, mend it; If you want to be a monk, you must be a lady." The old Venerable said "you must be a lady", meaning you must know how to serve people.

Suffering a little hardship, enduring a little hardship, the old Venerable completely did not take it to heart.

July 23, 2011, the weather that day was very hot. At that time, it was Trung Phuc period, three o'clock in the afternoon, normal people sitting under the shade of trees would have felt unbearably dry and hot, but the old Venerable was wearing the hot sun, focusing on hoeing weeds in the hot corn field. Could it be that the old Venerable could not avoid the heat?

The Venerable's disciple, Dharma Master An Chi, prepared a bucket of cold water, came before the Venerable, and said: “Master, please wash up and rest a bit, it's very hot, don't do it anymore!” The magician resolutely pulled the old monk to the downstairs door of the forest tower, removed the paper packaging box and spread it on the ground, letting the old monk lie on top to rest for a bit.

The old monk complied and lay down, his right hand resting on his head, his left hand on his thigh, lying on his right side. This sleeping position is completely compatible with the rules and virtues of walking, standing, lying, and sitting that are required in the precepts.

Dharma Master An Chi, who was beside him, used a wet handkerchief to wipe the sweat from the old monk's face. There was no way. He half-pleaded and half-advised: “Master, it's hot, don't do it anymore, wait until it's cool and then we'll do it again. If you keep doing that, the disciples will know what to do."

The old monk did not answer the Dharma Master, but only recited the phrase "Amitabha Buddha".

There was also one time, on the last winter day right before the old Venerable's rebirth, a few guests arrived at the temple, preparing to stay for a few days at Lai Buddha Pagoda. Because very few people come to the temple on weekdays, their arrival makes the temple bustling. Before a dinner, the Venerable was splitting tree roots, everyone gathered around the Venerable, waiting for him to teach everyone.

At this time, an unfamiliar person saw the Venerable's hand being rubbed, so he squatted down and said to the Venerable: "Don't cut it anymore, your hand is already bleeding."

The old monk raised his hand to look at it, looked at the young man and said softly: “Isn't it just a little blood, what are you afraid of?” Hearing the old Venerable say so, everyone suddenly burst out laughing. One sentence from the old monk made the atmosphere momentarily light and lively.

After a while, Dharma Master An Toan came over to invite the Venerable to dinner. The Venerable said slowly: "Let it cool a bit first, I'll cut it into pieces before eating."

As soon as Dharma Master An Toan heard it, he immediately took the tool from the old monk's hand and said: “Master! Teacher, go and eat, let me split!” As he spoke, he used the ax to chop the tree roots, picked up the hammer and aimed at the head of the axe.

The old monk hastily said: “Slow down a bit! A little slow! Don't break the axe." As soon as the words ended, the ax handle was indeed broken. The old monk did not have the slightest intention of blaming Dharma Master An Toan. He stood up, smiled and called out to the others and said: “Come on, let's go eat!”

tom_tat: Venerable Hai Hien's job is farming. He is an exemplary farmer, also a pedagogical farmer. He has good physical strength and likes to work; At the same time, he can use his practice of reciting Buddha in his work...
noi_dung:
16. Likes to do good deeds

Venerable Hai Hien's job is farming. He is an exemplary farmer, also a pedagogical farmer. He has good physical strength and likes to work; At the same time, he can use his practice of reciting Buddha in his work, thus, at work he will not feel tired, nor bored, but the more he works, the happier he will be. In addition to work, in dealing with people, receiving things every day, he perfectly achieved the six paramitas.

The six paramitas are also called the six paramitas, i.e. giving, maintaining the precepts, patience, diligence, meditation, and wisdom. The six paramitas are one of the important merits of the Pure Land practice. They can help practitioners achieve rebirth merit, accumulate rebirth merit, and can also achieve personal merit. Small ones lead to family satisfaction and career achievements, large ones lead to peace and social stability.

To put it specifically, if you like giving, you can get rid of greed, stinginess, and basic afflictions from beginningless kalpas up to now. In all dharmas in this world and beyond, there is not a single bit of greed, then the giving paramita is complete. For all worldly and transcendental dharmas, do not give rise to a single evil thought, maintaining the precepts of perfection. Being able to be in favorable circumstances does not give rise to attachment, in adverse circumstances does not give rise to anger, and perfects the perfection of patience. In the good dharma of the world, there is great diligence in the world beyond, there is no regression, the perfection of diligence is perfect. In daily life, maintaining purity, equality, enlightenment, not being shaken by external circumstances, the perfection of meditation is achieved. In daily life, truly seeing "all dharmas, non-existent, all-empty, impossible to attain" that Buddha said, although it is "all-empty", but does not abide in "emptiness", not only seeing, but also being able to truly understand, this is the perfection of Prajnaparamita.

The six paramitas are perfect, this is the practice, the practice is even

in normal daily use, in dealing with people, receiving things. Away from life, where else can one go to practice!

The first of the six paramitas is giving, which means taking wealth, physical strength, wisdom, etc. There are three types of giving: talented giving, dharma giving and fearless giving. Venerable Hai Hien did this all his life.

In the past, they were on Dong Bach mountain. Due to very few lay people and making offerings, their activities were completely dependent on their own support. Venerable Hai Hien was young at that time. All the housekeeping in the temple from top to bottom, including the monks' clothes, Venerable Hai Hien all helped with cleaning and washing. He did his best to help the monks have more time to gather. Later, when he and Dharma Master Hai Mac, Dharma Master Hai Vien and Dharma Master The Quang together made a hermitage for group meditation, Thap Vien pagoda allocated land to the three of them, they used it for plowing, and Venerable Hai Hien also helped them manage it. Later, he met Dharma Master Dien Cuong who had just left the home life not long ago. The Venerable gave him food, such as taro, so that the Dharma Master could feel secure in studying the Dharma.

The old Venerable gave the taro to Dharma Master Dien Cuong because he had cultivated it himself. The wasteland on the mountain had no owner. Venerable Hai Hien abandoned it and planted sweet potatoes and taro, which were his main source of food at that time. Every time he met a monk coming to the mountain, he always wanted to give a little to them. If he gave everything to others and didn't have enough to eat himself, he would dig up herbs to use as a substitute for food.

During the three difficult years (i.e. from 1959 to 1961, the country's food shortage and crop failure) made his livelihood even more difficult, the Venerable still did his best to give and help people. At that time, thanks to his diligence and wisdom, he also saved many lives.

In the summer of 1989, the locality encountered natural disasters, floods, and food shortages. Elderly Venerable Hai Hien voluntarily brought 1,200 pounds of barley that he cultivated at the temple and personally delivered it to the locality in difficulty, without even receiving food money. A local resident therefore praised the Venerable for his "very high level of thought", and said that this gesture of the Venerable reflected his "patriotism, love of religion, helping the country, always thinking of sentient beings".

There are two types of alms: External wealth giving and internal wealth giving. The family is rich in wealth, the giving they do is external giving, in the giving of Venerable Hai Hien there is internal giving, there is also external giving, external wealth is the amount of food that he plows and harvests, internal wealth is his own physical strength, he puts in the effort to cultivate and cultivate.

One time, the Venerable, who was over 100 years old, like every other day, did not rest after noon and went to the cornfield outside the temple to take a walk. This piece of corn field belongs to the temple, the harvest is a living allowance for the monks in the temple and the lay people staying at the temple. When the old Venerable went to the northeast corner of this corn field, he suddenly heard rustling, rustling for a while and a "crack, crackle" sound in the corn field. He followed the sound and looked into the field, only to see a middle-aged farmer stealing corn ears. He put all the broken corn ears in a large cloth bag that had been prepared in advance.

At this time, the farmer also saw the old monk. He felt very shy and stood there, not knowing what to do for a moment. The old monk quickly signaled and gently comforted him: "Don't rush, if you want to break, choose a big fruit to break!" After speaking, leave.

Old Venerable Hai Hien has a big heart. He did not ask for the corn that the farmer stole back, nor did he give him a lesson, but instead gave it to him, and told him to choose a bigger one to pick. He did so, so that the farmer would forever be filled with gratitude and virtue, and would not dare to steal again in the future. After that, every time that person met the old monk again, his eyes were filled with admiration and admiration.

Old Venerable Hai Hien all his life loved to do good deeds, making it convenient for everyone. His life was extremely frugal. The disciple of Dharma Master An Vinh even felt for a while that her master was too stingy. He has no greed, every little bit is making offerings for the masses, making offerings for others, not enjoying it alone. He used money from other people's making offerings, he used it to print sutras, release animals, used it to help others build ashrams, all his life he helped others build 11 ashrams! The outside disciples invited him to go. When the old monk left, he would leave behind all the making offerings of the lay people at the temple, without taking a penny of money himself. Sponsoring local schools and ashrams to buy seedlings, he was also especially generous. What about Him himself? Besides a few shirts, I don't have anything. Therefore

He said, in this small temple of his own, eating is hard work, dressing is mending.

The Venerable Master was able to do all three types of giving, and he often felt joy. For Him, as He is now, life is in the World of Ultimate Bliss, the World of Ultimate Bliss is right here. Buddha tells us: All dharmas are born from the mind, and the situation changes according to the mind. In the old Venerable's feelings, everyone is a good person, his work is a good deed, the person who stole His corn is also a good person, what he does is also a good deed.

giving can accumulate merit, merit is a rebirth support World Ultimate Bliss. If you do giving and still seek to repay favors, your merit will turn into merits and blessings. The retribution of merits and blessings is in the three good paths, not leaving the six paths of samsara. There are many people in the world who study Buddha. Accumulated practice in a lifetime are all merits and blessings, not merit! They keep in their minds all the good deeds they have done, not only in their hearts but also often hanging in their mouths, for fear that others will not know. How can I harvest merit? If you don't keep in mind the good deeds you have done, but almost forget them, merits and blessings will immediately turn into merits.

Venerable Hai Hien's giving is merit, his giving does not ask for gratitude. His mind is so pure, an uncontaminated dust, apart from a Buddha's signal, there is nothing in His mind.

17. PICK VEGETABLES, DO NOT THROW

THE REMAINING PART,

tieu_de: 17. Picking vegetables without throwing away the tender parts is better than chanting organ sutras
tom_tat: Lao Tzu said: “The Three Jewels' self-existence tells me: First, write words, second, write sparingly, third, write without feeling for the world." One of the secrets in this is saving. Many people who have come into contact with the Venerable Hai Hien, when they remember...
noi_dung:
17. Picking vegetables without throwing away the tender parts is better than chanting organ sutras

Lao Tzu said: “The Three Jewels' self-existence tells me: First, write words, second, write sparingly, third, write without feeling for the world." One of the secrets in this is saving. Many people who had contact with the Venerable Hai Hien, when remembering the Venerable, were deeply impressed with his frugality.

Old Venerable Hai Hien often said to those around him: "A single grain of rice for a sentient being is as heavy as Mount Meru", "The things of the ever-standing Sangha are the donor's field of blessings. It is necessary to preserve the permanent things, such as keeping the pupils."

Permanent residence, only prepared materials offered for Sangha to use. If you take it as your own or buy and sell it, you commit a felony. Increases include making offerings from other places, such as warehouse kitchens, fields and gardens, rice, clothes, medicine, etc.; also includes current monks and relics of deceased monks.

Old Venerable Hai Hien highly values permanent objects. He saves water and saves electricity, not even a little is wasted. He sleeps very early, and in the evening when he doesn't need lighting, he doesn't turn on the lights.

In the 80s of the twentieth century, Lai Buddha Pagoda did not have running water, the monks relied entirely on a self-dug shallow well to drink water. The Venerable used water very sparingly. Normally when he washed his hands and face, he only used a small ladle of water and filled the sink with water. The sink in his room often only had more than a bowl of water. Later, the pagoda installed tap water, but he still did not agree because it was a waste of water.

One afternoon in the summer of 2010, the old Venerable was digging the ground in the monastery tower, when suddenly there was a heavy rain. Dharma Master An Chi quickly brought an umbrella to welcome the old Venerable back to the temple. Right at the time when Dharma Master An Chi got him a pair of dry shoes, the old monk sprinkled water that had been washed over the vegetables in a large basin to wash his feet. At this time, a lay person placed a basin of clean water and invited him to wash. The old monk firmly refused and told her: “We must save water, we must accumulate blessings!”

From these small points, we can realize how much the Venerable Hai Hien is a person who values material resources, blessings come from saving, not from wasting, the Venerable accumulates blessings.

He often told people: “Picking vegetables without throwing away the tender parts is better than chanting organ sutras.” If in the kitchen door he saw a discarded cabbage leaf, he would pick it up, wash it and put it back in the kitchen. He was never picky about rice, never used specially reserved rice and water, ate meals like everyone else every day, after each meal he always rinsed the rice bowl with boiled water.

One time, the Venerable mixed some celery. After mixing, he pointed to a large jar of sesame oil on the ground and said to Dharma Master An Ham: “Use your chopsticks to dip a little and mix this celery!”

Even though it has been many years, Dharma Master An Ham still brings tears to his eyes when mentioning this story. He said: “That's a 50-pound jar of sesame oil! But the master told me to use my chopsticks to dip a little and mix the vegetables. Just based on this point, I have admired Him all my life! During these years, I have tried my best to learn my master's frugality. Maybe now I can still speak in this aspect of diligence, but when it comes to frugality, I am still far behind my master."

Another disciple of the Venerable, Dharma Master An Vinh, also admired the Venerable to the point of bowing his head to the ground. The magician said: “At first, I was a little dissatisfied that my master was too stingy. Even if I wanted to buy two coins of tofu, he wouldn't let me buy it. But later, when I saw my master raising money to buy seedlings for several schools and ashrams, and taking out thousands of coins with just a shake of his hand, this made me completely admire him to the point of falling to the ground!"

The old Venerable used the harvest he worked hard to cultivate to do charity and giving. He was happy and never tired of it; As for himself, the Venerable would not waste even a single grain of rice.

The Venerable's socks were patched over and over again. One time a layman asked his old man: “Do you have any work we can help with?” The Venerable then found his socks so she could mend them for him. The layman saw two half-torn socks and basically didn't know how to start mending them! So she secretly hid the torn socks. When the Venerable asked about the socks, everyone said they couldn't find them. The Venerable had no other choice but to change them to new ones.

Old monks still couldn't bear to throw away such old and torn socks. As for objects that people think are no longer usable, He can always find a way to use the discarded object.

One time, the old monk saw someone else throwing away an unused sweater, felt very sorry, and picked it up. He washed the old sweater first, then peeled the sweater into yarn, and used this yarn to weave it into a large roll of rope. This time, not only did I not need to buy another roll of rope, compared to buying from outside, the old Venerable's rope roll was even more beautiful and durable. Everyone who saw it admired the old monk for being able to think of this trick! Everyone saw that being able to reuse discarded items like that was really great, so they all went home to learn how to do it.

The broom that the old monk used to sweep and clean was also tied by him himself, and the diaphora tree (geo master) used to tie the broom was planted by him himself. The reason this is related to this type of plant called diatom algae is because the branches of this plant are very thick. After ripening, they are chopped and dried, then bundled can be used to make brooms.

The things the old Venerable used were all very ordinary. The stick that he often used was just the stem of a wild vegetable called "khoi khoi thai" that grew on the ground. Everyone said they had never seen Him leaning on a new cane. Once, the Venerable came to recite Buddha's name at Nghia Street in Nam Duong. Layman Truong in Nam Duong made offerings for the Venerable with a stick, a red agate ring and a purple bracelet. The Venerable at that time said: “Why do people leaving the home life wear jewelry rings? Not like the dharma. Take it! I also have a stick.”

This stick was specially bought by layman Truong to give to the old monk, so he very persistently said: “It's okay, maybe you won't wear these in your whole life. You wear them so I can see if they look good or not. And that stick of yours is too old, the bottom is cracked, in the future you will use this new stick! The Venerable happily accepted these making offerings.

After a week, layman Truong went to recite Buddha's name again, and someone said he knew: “The Venerable has something to do and has to return to the temple. Before leaving, he left his making offerings a ring and rosary, and said people leaving the home life should not wear these things, the colors are too beautiful, not like the Dharma. After listening, Layman Truong thought in his mind: “This old Venerable is truly a great practitioner! He saw that he was so attached, in order to create a joyful mind, he always accepted sentient beings and accepted making offerings. Wait until you're about to leave before leaving your things behind. This is truly compassionate and skillful! Wherever Bodhisattva is, it causes all sentient beings to have a joyful mind, it is truly like that!” Not only did he not feel angry, but on the contrary, he also developed a sense of respect for the old Venerable.

Some time ago, when the Venerable again went to recite Buddha's name at Yiwu Street in Nanyang, Layman Truong came to visit him. Seeing that the Venerable was holding a new stick in his hand that he did not give to him last time, he asked him: “That stick that I gave you, why don't you use it?” The old Venerable laughed and said: “I don't have great blessings like you, I can use this.” The old Venerable gave that new stick to someone else.

The old Venerable's life was simple, he took care of all the little things in daily life by himself. The temple land is located in the countryside, the conditions are relatively poor, there is no heater in the room, so when the winter is quite cold, the old monk himself uses a charcoal pot to light a fire to warm up. Therefore, every year after autumn passed, the old Venerable began to dig up the tree's roots, then split them and dry them to prepare for winter use. Even though he is over 100 years old, he still looks like a young person, only covered with a cotton blanket, covered with another sheet to cover the winter. One time, the lay people cleaned the room for the Venerable. They conveniently thought of helping him wash the clothes and bedsheets. As a result, they turned the blanket over and discovered that the blanket at the feet could not be shaken off no matter how much they tried to shake it. After looking closely, it turned out that the Venerable, in order to be a little warmer, used a rope to tie the blanket at the feet. Everyone laughed at how thoughtful the Venerable was.

The Venerable's life was very simple. A Dharma Master who had been in contact with him for nearly two years discovered that the Venerable had never drank tea before, so he asked him why he had never drank tea before. Old Venerable Hai Hien said: “Drinking good boiled water, drinking boiled water simply, also prevents lay people from spending a lot of money making our tea offerings. The hobby of drinking tea is also a habit. Just like boiling water can quench thirst, why must we drink tea?

The old Venerable did not like the arrangements made for him by lay people. On the 20th day of the 8th lunar month, 2012, the lay people of Nam Duong happily organized a vegetarian banquet for the Venerable to celebrate his 112th birthday. But the Venerable didn't eat a single bite of those dishes, and in the end he only ate a bowl of black sesame leaf noodles. Why? This is what the old Venerable said: All natural and normal is good; especially for Him, this is not good, not normal, not natural, it is not a good thing. So he didn't even eat a single bite.

Although the Venerable was not happy that day, the lay people still wanted to take souvenir photos with him. After the photo was developed, layman Liu, who knew the Venerable, said: This is the most unhappy photo in the Venerable's life.

The old Venerable's appearance on the photo is extremely unhappy. He has never used such a face to treat people before. His attitude is telling the lay people: If you do that, it's actually too wasteful. In the old Venerable's heart there was no discrimination, no attachment. His every move is to save sentient beings, to teach people, to move one day of life

Sir, there's nothing wrong with telling people to save money and suffer.

To suffer is to have no attachment to this world, to wholeheartedly want to go to the World of Ultimate Bliss; This world still has delicious food and interesting things, so I can't let it go.

The Buddha Sutra always says that this world of ours is eight types of suffering mixed together: Suffering from birth, old age, illness, resentment increases, love is separated, desire is in vain, the five skandhas become empty. Who can be exempt from these eight types of suffering? We live in these eight types of suffering every day, but have no intention of leaving; In our daily life, our eyes see, our ears hear, our nose smells, our tongue tastes, our body can touch... All kinds of these phenomena are unfolding before us, never interrupted before, we just cannot detect them. Old Venerable Hai Hien had already realized it, so he did not have any attachment to this world.

18. making offerings Arhat

One day, a young layperson brought two of his friends to visit the Venerable Hai Hien. At that time, he was in front of the temple yard digging a very large tree stump. In the ground, he had dug a large, very deep hole. He could only see him standing in the hole, his whole body and face were covered in clay. When the three people saw the old Venerable, they quickly bowed to him. The old Venerable kept stopping: “Don't bow! Don't bow! The ground is very dirty!”

The young man and the old Venerable were very familiar, his two friends had also lived together for a short period of three months in Thien Buddha Pagoda with the old Venerable, so the old Venerable saw them coming, was extremely happy, stopped his unfinished work and started talking to them.

He told the young man: "The people in your village have deep good roots, and many people study Buddha."

“Yes. In our village, almost every family worships Buddha."

The Venerable asked: "In your village many years ago, there was an old monk who lived, do you remember?"

The layman replied: “I was still young at that time, but I was impressed, because that Magician was my grandmother's protector. Later, he went to Bach Ma Pagoda."

The Venerable said: “At that time, I invited him to Lai Buddha temple, but he refused... I don't know if he's still alive or not."

“I heard he passed away.”

“When is it no more?”

“Soon it won't be anymore, it's already a thing of the last century.” The layman said, couldn't help but burst out laughing, thinking in his heart: If that Dharma Master were still alive, he would be over 100 years old. Do you think everyone has the same longevity as you?

The old monk looked at him, not understanding and asked: “What are you laughing at?”

The layman seemed to be joking and said to the Venerable: “Do you think that Empress Dowager Cixi is still alive?”

The old monk was also provoked by him and laughed loudly, saying: “I'm still not that confused. - Oh my! This is a heavy karma obstacle for me. If I want to go, I can't go. Seeing that the old practitioners have left one by one, I have become an old goblin."

The young layman helped the old monk out of the tree hole and said: “You rest a bit, then tell us a story, okay?”

The old monk sat down on a piece of wood, pointed to the pieces of wood next to him and asked everyone to sit too. Two people inside said they did not want to sit, so the Venerable said to the two of them: “I don't want to sit on a piece of wood, there are chairs in the room.” Then he laughed and said: “I'll tell you a koan from the Buddha Sutra, it's very good!”

Có một vị A La Hán cầm bình bát ra ngoài, gặp một nữ quỷ, nữ quỷ nói muốn cúng dường La Hán, rồi mời Ngài vào trong nhà. Arhat just looked at the eye-catching gems and jewels in this female ghost's house, extremely majestic! The female ghost brought food and drinks making offerings to Arhat on the table and invited Arhat to dine. Arhat lowered his head and saw four hungry hungry ghosts tied to the four legs of the table, feeling very curious. At this time, the female devil said: “Please wait a moment, Venerable One, I have some important things to do and go out for a moment, I will be back immediately. Please have mercy, don't give food to the four of them!”

After the female ghost left, Arhat himself ate and was puzzled: Why not give food to the four of them? Four hungry ghosts stared at Arhat who was eating there, but did not dare to speak. Arhat felt that this was too cruel, he really couldn't bear it, so he took some food and gave some to these four hungry ghosts. Unexpectedly, these four hungry ghosts put food into their mouths, each of them cried out in pain: A hungry ghost's food that enters his mouth turns into his own flesh, a hungry ghost's food that enters his mouth turns into iron pellets, a hungry ghost's food that enters his mouth turns into feces, a hungry ghost's food that enters his mouth turns into blood and pus. La Han saw such a situation and was very panicked.

That beautiful female ghost quickly ran into the room from outside, very sadly said to Arhat: “When I left, I told you that you definitely couldn't give them food or drink, so why didn't you listen? Do You love them more than me? They are your husband, son, daughter-in-law, and a reincarnation of your previous life!”

La Han did not understand and asked: “What is the cause of this?”

The female devil said: "I made offerings through an Arhat in my previous life. I told my husband, hoping he would be happy with his merit. Who knows, after hearing the contrary, he slandered and said: 'Why does he eat our food? Why don't you go eat yourself?' I was very sad, so I told this story to my son. Unexpectedly, he also opened his mouth and said: ‘Why doesn't he go eat iron pills?’ I feel even more heartbroken. That day, an in-law gave me some food, but my daughter-in-law stole it all. I went to ask her, she didn't admit it, and said: ‘Eating your mother's food is not as good as eating feces!' I gave food as a gift to my family, but it was stolen by A Huan on the way. I blamed her, she didn't admit it, and said: ‘Eating your food isn't even worth the price of blood.'”

“In my heart, great anger arose towards the four of them, so I made a vow, vowing in my next life to be in a place where I can see the four of them receive evil retribution. So in this life I will be a powerful demon king. If it weren't for this evil wish, just based on my merit of making offerings Arhat, in this life I would have been born in the Dao Loi heaven and received heavenly blessings."

The Venerable finished telling the story, laughed loudly and asked: “Does it sound good?” The young layman's hair was chilling when he heard it. He changed his mind again: “This old man is absolutely not a foolish person!” He originally thought that the old Venerable only knew how to work and recite Buddha's name, and was not sure that he could understand the Buddha's teachings too deeply, but this time he really admired the old Venerable.

The old Venerable looked at him dumbfounded, then continued: “This story is to teach people not to talk too complacently, 'talking too much is too real, not talking too much', talking too much makes people hate and quarrel with everyone. Don't have bad thoughts, if you have bad thoughts, the person who will suffer is yourself."

"The word sam, the mouth is full" that the old Venerable said is a proverb in the Indonesian dialect, which most of the Venerable Ones like to use. “Say language” refers to harsh and harsh language; “satisfied mouth” just talks arrogantly. "Fairy talk is too heavenly, no talk is too mythical" is also an Indonesian proverb, and also teaches people not to be too arrogant.

"Depending on joy" that the female ghost said, refers to depending on the good deeds of others, the joy of good results achieved by others; That is to say, seeing others doing good deeds brings joy to the mind.

Shakyamuni Buddha Buddha used a simple example in the past to help a couple understand the meaning of making offerings giving in return.

When Shakyamuni Buddha Buddha was in Xa Ve city, the Ky Vien teaching monastery once received a bowl of rice from a couple of women making offerings. Buddha Da told them: “If you plant one, you will receive ten, if you plant ten, you will receive a hundred, if you plant a hundred, you will receive ten thousand. If you use the merit of giving this bowl of rice, you will receive immeasurable blessings.”

Two skeptical people asked: “Buddha Da! We simple, ignorant people really don't understand, just by giving a bowl of rice, how great blessings can be?"

Buddha Da explained to them: “Do you see the Niguda tree? A luxuriant tree is four or five miles away, each year its fruit falls more than ten thousand dou (dau: dou: drawer: Ancient unit of measuring capacity, equal to 10 measures, now 5 measures).

At first, the seed of the Niguda tree was just a seed.”

From then on, the people of Xa Ve city, towards Buddha Da and the monks, were even more happy and enthusiastic about making offerings.
