19. the Venerable's wisdom

Even though Venerable Hai Hien was illiterate, when he spoke, he often spoke magical words, often making listeners feel great surprises.

Once, the old Venerable Hai Hien and a Dharma Master were digging taro in the reclaimed wasteland east of Thien Buddha Pagoda. The Dharma Master dug outside, the old Venerable peeled off the clay on the taro.

Two lay people saw it and went to help. Because the weather was getting a bit cold, the Venerable's nose flowed very long. Two lay people said: “Master, give me some tissue to wipe your nose.”

The Venerable said: “Leave him alone.”

Both of them laughed. A layperson asked him: “Master, you said ‘Let it be his business’, so whose business is it?”

The Venerable said: “Don't know.” Everyone laughed.

After digging the taro and returning to the temple, the old monk's entire body was made of clay. One lay person said: “Please take off your shirt, I'll wash it for you.” The old monk took off his shirt, the lay person took it and said: “Look, the new shirt was worn today, but it turned out like this.”

The Venerable said: “This is not mine.”

“Just took it off from your body. Whose is it not yours?”

The old Venerable said another sentence: “Don't know.”

This Dharma Master at that time could not understand these words of the old Venerable. He even found these responses very funny. It was not until after the Venerable's rebirth that he realized that the Venerable was not an ignorant person! On the contrary, the Venerable's wisdom and virtue are unimaginable.

Truly corresponds to the statement that Dharma Master Dien Cuong said to Venerable Hai Hien:

"We ordinary people cannot recognize the wonderful robes of the Buddha's feet!"

noi_dung:
20. Emperor Taizong's blessings

TIMING blessings

In the fall of 2004, the young man heard the Venerable tell the story of the female ghost and took his uncle to Lai Buddha Pagoda to ask for condolences to the Venerable Hai Hien, who at that time was only in his twenties. His uncle many years ago was a disciple who took refuge in the Venerable's court. Later on, when he left the home life, although he was not the Venerable, he still used the same ritual to worship the monk as before.

The old monk was extremely happy when he saw the two people. He rummaged around to find some fruit and snacks to treat this young man.

The young man said: “Or maybe you save it to eat alone.”

The old man smiled and said: "I don't eat these things, they are all for children to eat."

The young man also smiled and said: "This year I'm turning twenty, I'm no longer a child."

The old monk pointed at him and laughed loudly: “You're twenty years old and you're not ashamed to tell me you're not a child? In my place you are just a child.”

At noon, the Venerable ate rice with everyone - each person had a bowl of Lao noodles. The young man saw a piece of noodles falling on the table, so he picked it up and ate it. Venerable Hai Hien saw this and said to this young man's uncle:

"Your child really has good roots. Nowadays, it's rare among young people who don't step on food!" Having finished speaking, he put down the bowl of rice he was carrying and said to the young man: “Do you know how many blessings you can increase by picking up this noodle?”

"What is this? My grandmother taught me how to do this since I was young. I never thought about increasing blessings."

“Good! Good! Good! Good roots sprout good seeds!” Old Venerable Hai Hien also put down his chopsticks on the table decisively and said: “Let me tell you a story.”

During the Tang Dynasty, under Ly The Dan, there were two talented people, one named Vien Thien Canh, the other named Ly Thuan Phong, both of whom were proficient in the I Ching and magical math. One day, the two of them chatted with Ly The Dan, the two of them claiming to know nothing about the past and future. Ly The Dan was also suddenly excited, so he said to the two people: “So, please guess how long this lady has left to live?” Both of them said they did not dare to calculate, Ly The Dan said: “It's okay, you guys speak boldly, this lady is not shy!”

Two people, so each person told a hexagram for Ly The Dan.

Ly The Dan asked: “What was the result?” The two looked at each other and did not speak.

Ly The Dan said: "You don't need to worry about anything. No matter what the outcome is, you must speak frankly. This lady will definitely not blame you."

When the two heard the king say he would not blame them, they said together: "The result of both of our guesses is the same, the Emperor will return to heaven in the middle of the night tonight."

After hearing this, Ly The Dan laughed and said: "You two gentlemen must have miscalculated this time. Do you see my whole person's spirit, like someone about to die?"

Both of them said: “It's really not the same.”

That night, Vien Thien Canh and Ly Thuan Phong secretly planned, if the emperor did not die tonight, then tomorrow they would definitely have to prosecute them for lese majesty. The more they thought about it, the more they had no confidence, and finally decided to run away that night.

They each rode a donkey, hurriedly ran all night, and early the next morning, ran to a crossroads. I saw that right in the middle of this road, a tree grew, its trunk separate, like two arms of a person stretched out. At this moment, an old man walked across the street with a pair of canes. The two of them hugged the donkey tightly, intending to rest for a while. It was truly "three moves without leaving the cave", Vien Thien Canh said to Ly Thuan Phong: "Brother Dao, let's guess whether this old man will come from the left side of the tree, or from the right side, okay?"

Ly Thuan Phong says: “Brother Dao, I figured he must have come from the left.”

Vien Thien Canh says: “That's not right, brother! How do I deduce that he must come from the right?

The two of them were arguing endlessly when they saw the old man walking under the tree with a pair of sticks, hanging them on the tree, and jumping over from the middle of the tree branch. The two were extremely surprised, immediately stopped arguing, they really wanted to know why this old man thought of jumping from the middle of the tree, so they came to the old man to ask him for advice.

The old man smiled and asked: “You two living gods, why did you come to this place?”

The two of them were even more surprised, so they told Ly The Dan the story of fortune-telling once.

The old man said: “This is nothing, you guys go back!”

The two quickly asked: “So do you know how the king is doing now?”

“Peace and good health.”

The two of them were so panicked this time, they said: “So we don't dare to go back anymore.”

The old man said: “After you leave, if the emperor asks about you, you will say: 'Sometime last night, Your Majesty suddenly felt troubled in your heart. You wanted to drink a bowl of millet soup. While drinking, you accidentally dropped a millet grain on your boot. Your Majesty reached out and picked up this millet grain. Because of this millet grain, he moved the heavens. The Jade Emperor praised a noble person as a son of heaven, but if you can love a grain of millet, why wouldn't you love him if he had good morals towards his people? That increases your Majesty's life expectancy by 20 years'.”

The two people heard this old man say so, admired the old man, and praised the old man: “You are the living god! We are compared to You, like the water in a river compared to the water of the great ocean.”

The old man waved his hands repeatedly, saying: "Anyway, it can't be compared like that. What I've learned is that a jar taken out of the ocean is still not very full."

After hearing this, Vien Thien Canh and Ly Thuan Phong were so embarrassed that they had no face left and said to the old man: "You're a tank that's not full, the two of us can only manage half a tank!"

Old Venerable Hai Hien finished telling the story, smiled and said to the young man: “This is a legend, not necessarily true, but very meaningful. Do you understand or not?”

"If you listen and understand a little, it teaches people to regret blessings, and also teaches people to be humble."

The old monk picked up his chopsticks and stirred the noodles in the bowl, still smiling and saying: “Good! Good! Good! See how many blessings you get when you pick up this noodle! - Increase life expectancy by 20 years and increase education. If you can persevere in blessings and be humble throughout your life, then you will definitely have great achievements.”

The old Venerable spoke very wonderfully. He said, although it is just a story, it may not be true, but its meaning is very good and very accurate. People must be grateful for blessings, no matter what they do, they should not be excessive.

noi_dung:
21. maintaining the principles of purity

Buddha's precepts are extremely important. The ancient Venerable took all the sutras that Shakyamuni Buddha taught during his lifetime and divided them into three studies of morality - concentration - wisdom. Precepts are rules, keeping rules is attaining meditation. Buddhism guides us, nothing else, it's all about practicing meditation; Leaving meditation is not Buddha Dharma. meditation takes effect, then wisdom opens, the wisdom, the virtue of each person that is similar to Buddha, appears. So say: The human world attains concentration, human concentration opens wisdom. Therefore, it can be known that wisdom is the true goal of studying Buddha Dharma.

Precepts are rules, people cannot help but keep rules, rules are fundamental.

Precepts, in Confucianism, are decency, benevolence, wisdom, faith, and the four virtues and eight virtues in Confucianism, these are all basic virtues that a person must have. The "ceremony" that Chinese Confucianists say is the standard method of teaching moral conduct: "Etiquette" is used to bind our bodies, our gestures, actions, words and smiles must all be in accordance with etiquette. Rituals are the standard of behavior. “Lac” is used to regulate the mind, nourish the temper, joy and anger should be in it, not excessive.

In the Buddha's house, it is no exception, "ceremonies" are also very important. “Precepts” is equivalent to “Rites”, “Phan Boi” (chanting sutras) is equivalent to “Lac”. If "Rejoicing" is lost, then the teaching tool no longer exists, and the effectiveness of education cannot be achieved.

During Buddha's time, why did people in the world respect him so? Even people today, when mentioning Shakyamuni Buddha Buddha, are extremely respectful like in the past. This is the transformation of virtue, virtue is displayed in the world of learning. Buddha's practice was not an attempt to pretend, but a very natural way.

precepts is Buddha's body, meditation is Buddha's mind, teachings are Buddha's language. Shakyamuni Buddha Buddha teaches sentient beings using body teachings and verbal teachings. Venerable Hai Hien teaches people through physical teachings and verbal teachings.

Old Venerable Hai Hien was illiterate, so his mind was pure, with no distracting thoughts or false thoughts. His master taught him to recite a phrase "Namo Amitabha Buddha", this Buddha phrase is the supreme meditation, the general outline of Tathagata teachings. Master told him to always recite, this was the precepts for him, he truly accepted and maintained, did not change direction, continued to recite forever.

The work that Venerable Hai Hien did all his life was heavy physical work; Great Master Sixth Patriarch Hui Neng spent eight months in the Fifth Patriarch's ashram. The Fifth Patriarch assigned him the job of pounding rice and chopping firewood, which was also heavy physical work: The practice they use is the same, they are all practicing meditation. Great Master Hui Neng's concentration is to not give rise to the mind, not to move thoughts, this is not something ordinary people can do; The effort that old Venerable Hai Hien used is a Buddha-name sentence, in all times, all places, all conditions, the mind is concentrated on the Buddha-name phrase.

Old Venerable Hai Hien attaches great importance to maintaining the precepts. He often said: “It is not allowed to break the precepts.” His mother, after living 27 years in the mountains with him, proposed to return to live in his hometown, so the Venerable took his mother back to his hometown. During the “Van Cach” period

production labor team, the Venerable had no other choice, but could only eat vegetables next to the pot while eating together. This time, the Venerable took his mother back to the countryside, bringing a pot himself, because he and his mother were both vegetarians. He explained: “How can we eat other people's food? It is not allowed to break the precepts.”

Law is practice. Learning precepts is learning the life of Shakyamuni Buddha Buddha, studying the majesty and gestures of Buddha. The old Venerable Hai Hien was able to show his full majesty in his life, because people in the world showed their full majesty.

On the afternoon of Phu Thien (the hottest month of summer) in 2011, Venerable Hai Hien, who was 111 years old, was alone hoeing grass in a hot corn field. Dharma Master An Chi was heartbroken for his master. Downstairs, the door of Thap Lam (tower tomb complex) spread out a large wrapping paper box, intending to use it as a bed if needed. Then the Dharma Master pulled the old Venerable through, inviting him to rest a bit. The old monk lay down to rest in the auspicious position. Buddha Da stipulates that when leaving the home life, when lying down to rest, we must keep lying on the right side, this way of lying is also called auspicious sleeping. The old monk walked, stood, sat, and lay down without losing his majesty. He always had to do it to the utmost perfection.

Old Venerable Hai Hien not only precepted himself strictly but also used precepts to advise his disciples. In 2009, at that time the Venerable Hai Hien lived at Thien Buddha Pagoda. One time, Dharma Master Dieu Lieu, after giving rice to the Venerable, squatted next to him himself, picked up the bowl of rice, and began to eat. The old monk saw Dharma Master Dieu Lieu squatting on the ground eating, looking very stern and said to the Dharma Master: “Don't squat on the ground to eat! People leaving the home life must observe the precepts, must pay attention to dignity, be a good model for heaven and man, no one will like them if they do not observe the precepts.

The Venerable also used precepts to encourage the masses. Precepts do not simply refer to the five precepts, ten precepts, Bhikkhu precepts, Bodhisattva precepts, but more importantly are the rules of living together, that is to say, everyone in their daily life with each other must have rules, and should comply with these rules. In His small temple, one must be able to endure suffering and observe the precepts to be able to live with Him.

One Mid-Autumn Festival day in 2012, some lay people from outside came to Lai Buddha Pagoda. They arrived at the monastery and came to pay their respects to the Venerable, but asked the Venerable to say a few words to everyone. The old monk sat there, continuing to chop wood, saying: “There's nothing to teach, just diligently chant Buddha! There is nothing difficult in the world, just fear that the mind is not specialized. Everyone was very happy after hearing this and clapped their hands. The old Venerable added in his voice: “There's really nothing difficult about it!”

Next, the Venerable asked where they came from. After hearing the crowd answer each question, the Venerable smiled and said: “I am a small temple, I eat hard, I wear clothes. When you come here, you may have to suffer. Only by suffering can you end your suffering. If you don't come, I don't blame you. If you come, you have to observe my precepts. Wherever you go, you must keep the rules of that place."

The Venerable taught everyone to diligently recite the Buddha's name, maintaining the precepts of Buddha's name, and his own personal actions were still maintaining the precepts of Buddha's name.

In 2005, the old Venerable Hai Hien was 105 years old, in order to decorate the golden body of his brother Dharma Master Hai.

When Khanh went far to Guangzhou, there was a calligrapher who saw that the Venerable was over 100 years old, his body was as healthy as ever, he did not need anyone to take care of him, but he still had a quick mind, and admired him very much. He asked him to teach him the way of health care. The Venerable answered him simply: “upholding the precepts of reciting Buddha.”

Maintaining the precepts of reciting the Buddha's name is the general credo of all Buddhas. Tathagata acts on his own and transforms others. What precepts does the Venerable keep? The Three Refuges, the Five Precepts, the Ten Virtues, and the Six Paradigms, He maintained these things without violating them all his life, so He was able to attain concentration, enlightenment, and free rebirth.

The Three Refuges are the total principles, total directions, and total goals of Buddha's teachings. Firstly,"take refuge in Buddha" with enlightenment without delusion. “Return” is to return, to the beginning, “y” is to rely, “Buddha” is enlightenment, the meaning is to return from all the confusion and confusion to the beginning and rely on the original enlightenment of self-nature. Therefore, "taking refuge in Buddha" is absolutely not taking refuge in Buddha outside of one's own mind, which is called seeking the Dharma outside of one's mind. Second,"take refuge in the Dharma", righteous but not evil. The Dharma is the scriptures, what the Buddha said, what the Buddha practiced is called right knowledge and right view, which is a good example for us. We can turn from wrong knowledge and wrong views to rely on right knowledge and right enlightenment. This is taking refuge in the Dharma. Stuff ba, "take refuge in the Sangha", pure but not contaminated. “Sangha” represents the six pure senses without any dust, we turn from the pollution, relying on a pure mind.

Three Refuges is taking refuge in the Three Jewels. Especially when seeing the form of the Three Jewels, you must be able to immediately return the reflected light back to the Three Jewels of your own nature. This is a true Buddha disciple. Therefore, studying Buddha is learning, enlightenment, and purity - enlightenment without delusion, righteousness without evil, purity without contamination.

The method used in studying Buddhism is maintaining the precepts, meditation and wisdom. Buddha first taught people to maintain the precepts, the main precepts are the five precepts and the ten virtues.

The Five Precepts are not killing, not stealing, not committing adultery, not lying, and not drinking alcohol. The Ten Virtues have three aspects: body, speech, and mind: do not kill, do not steal, do not commit adultery; no false speech, no double-tongue, no evil speech, no false language; no greed, no anger, no ignorance. There is a difference between morality and goodness: Goodness is good deeds and has no binding effect; Gender has a binding effect.

The three refuges, the five precepts, and the ten virtues are the basic precepts of the Buddha. Even more advanced, there are six Samantabhadra vows and ten vows, which can achieve our virtue.

Elderly Venerable Hai Hien said that his way of nourishing life is "upholding the precepts of reciting the Buddha's name". Maintaining the precepts is to nourish the body, reciting the Buddha is to nourish the mind: We do well the five precepts and ten good deeds that Buddha Dharma talks about, which is to nourish the body, in our mind there is only Amitabha Buddha, this mind is the good within the good. The Five Precepts are also the Five Permanences that the Old Ancestors of China taught - benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, faith; Not killing is benevolence, not stealing is righteousness, not committing adultery is propriety, not lying is faith, not drinking alcohol is wisdom. What about Tam? The mind must be pure, reciting Buddha can help the mind become pure, can make the mind single, apart from this saying Buddha, there are no false thoughts, no distracting thoughts, body and mind are pure, naturally healthy.

Old Venerable Hai Hien did not violate the precepts all his life. He was able to maintain the precepts of reciting the Buddha's name. He endured hardship, was able to endure, and achieved the perfection of patience in the six paramitas. All my life I take precepts as my teacher, take suffering as my teacher, I don't compete with people, I don't seek anything from the world. There was no one to take care of Him, He took care of Himself. Even though life is difficult, every time he treats those who receive him, he always has a radiant, happy and friendly face - this joy of his is real, born from within.

Even though we can endure all the suffering in this world without even thinking about it, this is truly a feat.

Old Venerable Hai Hien is truly upholding the strict precepts. He is not attached to the appearance of maintaining the precepts, but his mind is pure and equal, that is the achievement of precepts.

noi_dung:
22. The ninja felt secure

Bodhisattva Six Paramitas, simply put, is the Dharma gate of six types of conduct that can lead from this side of samsara and suffering to reach the other side of Nirvana of peace, i.e. giving, maintaining the precepts, patience, diligence, meditation, and prajna. Giving can overcome greed, maintaining the precepts can overcome transgression, patience can overcome anger, diligence can overcome laziness, meditation can overcome distraction, and prajna can overcome ignorance. Without the spirit of giving, it is impossible to maintain the precepts. Maintaining the precepts is the means of patience; If you have concentration, you will definitely have the effort to yield. Therefore, the relationship of these six virtues is that the latter includes the former, the former does not include the latter, and the former is a means for the latter.

The Venerable Hai Hien, who practices the six levels, shows profound subtlety in his daily life. Unfortunately, we often do not know how to look. In his life, we cannot see these clues, cannot see the vitality of the Mahayana Buddha Dharma, nor can we see the active learning of the old Venerable. He never spoke before, he just strictly complied with his duty - his old duty, not to advertise, not to cause trouble. If each of us is forever willing to be looked down upon by everyone, our lives will be safe and sound.

In the past, when the Venerable Hai Hien lived for a long time on the mountain, there was a period of time when he saw some monks always gossiping and saying bad things about him, but he did not pay any attention. Later, his master called him to Phuong Truong's room and asked him if he had had an affair with a laywoman or not. Only at this time did Hai Hien realize that someone was plotting to harm him. The monks and brothers were talking loudly, and the story spread to his master.

Someone said: “Hai Hien has as many subjects as the entire forest.” The words are hard to hear. The more this story spread, the more thrilling it became, and later it was even said that there was a time and a place. Venerable Hai Hien was rejected because of this matter, some monks did not want to approach him anymore, but in his heart he was very calm, he did not speak up, nor did he argue. It wasn't until after a brother who studied abroad returned and heard about this incident, he immediately stood up to clarify the truth: During those few days, he and his disciple Hai Hien harvested corn on the mountainside. Villagers from the mountain came to help with the work. During that time, he and Hai Hien lived together all the time. At this point, the buzzing finally ended.

"One can attain patience in all dharmas", only with patience can one truly gain benefits. There are two types of patience: One is to respectfully make offerings, without arrogance and insolence. When being abused, there is no resentment; Two, hot and cold conditions, rain and wind, hunger and thirst, etc. causing harm, one can be calm and patient, without giving rise to anger or sadness.

The patience of the Venerable Hai Hien was noble, others slandered him, bullied him, hindered him, harmed him, in his mind everything was as if nothing happened, every day he worked, reciting the Buddha's name as usual, he was very happy, he did not have time to calculate these things with others, each person's cause will be the result, if you use evil towards others, this evil will will still return to yourself.

Venerable Hai Hien is like a person living in the world of Ultimate Bliss. He encounters things, his way of thinking, and his way of doing things that are completely different from ours. There are times when the things we see are so big that, for him, it's like nothing!

Many years ago, one time, an electrician as usual came to collect the Venerable's electricity bill. The old monk saw that the electricity bill was too high, so he asked him: “This month's electricity bill compared to last month, why is it so high?” He did not say a word, but slapped the old Venerable Hai Hien twice. The old Venerable did not say a word but took out the electricity bill to pay the bill collector.

After the person collecting the electricity bill left, several lay people present were extremely angry. Everyone expressed their displeasure and said: “That's not possible, we have to find him to tell us right from wrong! He doesn't speak reason like that!”

The Venerable stopped everyone and said: “Forget it, leave it, he hit me, it's like he scratched my itch; Spitting saliva on your face is like washing your face. For those who do not argue about highs and lows, there is no affliction. Those of us who leave the home life must be generous, able to tolerate others, and forever remember: The ninja is at peace."

As a human being, it is impossible not to have a conscience. The person who collects electricity bills, takes money from others, and also oppresses others. He committed karma without even knowing it. But the old Venerable saw very clearly, like the cause, like the effect, like the retribution, the cause and effect of retribution were not wrong at all.

People living in this world can change realms and be free. The bad habit of us ordinary people is that if the circumstances are favorable and everyone around us is a good person, we like them, then we give rise to attachment, attachment is affliction, giving rise to affliction does not give rise to wisdom. If it is an adverse situation, you encounter bad people, evil people, or people who oppress you, then you will be troubled and resentful. We have been transferred to the realm. Venerable Hai Hien does not change realms, he can change realms! In the Shurangama Sutra it says: "Without the ability to change realms, you are the same as Tathagata", if you can not be disturbed by realms, not be transformed by realms, then there is no difference between you and Tathagata, then you will become a Buddha. Therefore, when we are in favorable circumstances and encounter good conditions, we should not be attached to them, we should use a normal mind to handle things; When dealing with adversity or encountering evil conditions, you should not be angry.

The feeling of resentment results in unjust retribution. Everything in this world is fake ("Fake" here, absolutely does not mean fake in the traditional sense. This is where Buddha learned how to use language. It means that illusion is not real, dharma causes and conditions are in harmony to exist, illusion gives birth to illusion and perishes, illusion is not reality. The word "fake" in this book is synonymous everywhere else.) Is there any need to compare? Forgiving others, not calculating with others, this is cultivating blessings, every little bit of this is accumulating virtue. To bear loss is blessings, you must be able to bear loss, and never do anything to take advantage. People should be confused, not really confused, but fake confused, this is a rare confusion. Don't compare yourself with others, be willing to be deceived and suffer losses, never take it to heart, great blessings will come from such a person!

Dharma Master Dien Cuong, an old friend of Venerable Hai Hien, said: “There is no pretense in people's hearts, nor is it causing trouble. I want to say, Hien Cong is absolutely Buddha Bodhisattva transformed into the world! I have never heard of people in this life. He argued with someone over something. This point of the old monk is especially praiseworthy, good patience! There is no separation from anyone in a lifetime. He said these are all your own parents, brothers, and teachers in many lifetimes! Regardless of whether you practice or not, when you come to Hien Gong's place, everything is good, people don't say good things, they don't say bad things, it makes them happy. On normal days, Hien Cong does not like to talk about anything. He walks, stands, lies, and recites Amitabha. People have truly reached that level, contemplating the internal and not the external."

The mind of old Venerable Hai Hien is pure, not contaminated at all. He is patient and diligent, not comparing with others. The old Venerable stayed in this world for 112 years, leaving the home life for 92 years. He lived in this life, practicing the Bodhisattva path, no matter what kind of difficulties he encountered, how frustrated he was, how humiliated he was, he could endure everything, as if there was no such thing, he did not keep it in his mind, in his mind there was only one sentence: “Amitabha Buddha”, this is right knowledge and right view. With virtues like His, one can definitely have achievements. The frustrations and injustices that He endured were all accumulations of immeasurable merits.

23. Peaceful rear path

Moderation, generosity, supply, frugality, and concession are the five virtues initiated by Confucianism: Peaceful, honest, serious, thrifty, modest. Confucius's students, from Confucius's daily life, saw that he was full of moderation, kindness, generosity, frugality, and tolerance of these five virtues. The disciples of the Venerable Hai Hien clearly remembered the Venerable's lifelong virtues and praised the Venerable for perfecting these five virtues.

Virtue and self-nature are compatible, worldly dharma and transcendental dharma are no exception. National Master Hien Thu of the Tang dynasty pointed out four types of virtue that all Buddhas Bodhisattva displayed, which are "the virtue of depending on conditions and miraculous uses, the majestic abbot with principled virtue, the gentle nature of directly taking birth of virtue, the virtue of universal sentient beings experiencing suffering". The four types of virtues compared to the five virtues mentioned above by the Master are even more complete and far-reaching.

"Depending on conditions and wonderful effects" means being able to adapt to all sentient beings. "Majesty and principle" is to practice virtue, walk, stand, lie down and sit without losing majesty, and do everything to the fullest. This is a personal teaching, not a verbal teaching, which includes moderation and moderation. The third is "gentleness and directness". For any person, having a smiling face and welcoming them with a joyful heart, this is gentleness, straightforwardness is the true heart, a sincere heart. Inside you have to use a sincere heart, outside you have to be gentle, contact with such people can make people happy. No one has ever seen Venerable Hai Hien angry. Throughout his life, he did not use an arrogant attitude towards others, he was humble, tolerant, extremely extraordinary. For those who bully Him and insult Him, He will ignore them and will not take them to heart. Living in this world, working hard - "suffering on behalf of all living beings", creating a good model.

In this life of Venerable Hai Hien, walking, standing, lying, sitting, living, working, treating people and receiving things, he fully fulfilled these four virtues. Everyone who comes into contact with Him feels very comfortable and happy.

In the spring of 1992, a young man who had just joined the work saw his uncle holding a black Buddha chanter and listening to the Buddha's name "Amitabha Buddha". He was very curious and asked him: “Where did you buy this?”

"Not to buy, but to ask for it from Venerable Hai Hien at Lai Buddha Pagoda."

The young man heard it and wanted one too, so his uncle took him with him to Lai Buddha temple.

At this time, the old Venerable lived in a very low tile-roofed room to the west of the main hall of the back yard. This young man met the Venerable Hai Hien for the first time. I only saw the old Venerable with a tall figure and a gentle face. Although he didn't say much, he made others feel very close.

After the two people clearly stated their purpose of coming, the old monk seriously thought for a moment, then smiled and said: “It looks like there's still one left, let me try to find it.” Having finished speaking, He searched everywhere in the room and found it.

In fact, this young man just wanted to satisfy his curiosity. To him, having a small Buddha chanter really didn't matter whether he had it or not. But old Venerable Hai Hien was so serious, he put in so much effort, and finally found a machine. The Venerable was very thoughtful. He installed the battery into the Buddha chanting machine, tested it to see if there was any sound, then brought the Buddha chanting machine to this young man's hands, but also told him to go home and listen a lot, recite a lot. Finally, the Venerable also told him some Buddhist principles and the benefits of Buddha chanting.

On the one hand, the young man listened, but on the other hand, he put old Venerable Hai Hien's words out of his memory. He just felt that the old Venerable was extremely close. Old Venerable Hai Hien's gentle face and friendly tone will forever remain engraved in this young man's memory.

Kind, friendly, calm, teaching people to recite Buddha's name, these seem to be the first impressions of many people towards Venerable Hai Hien.

One day in 1988, a young girl and some friends went to Lai Buddha temple. At that time, she had no interest in Buddha's teachings, nor did she have any understanding. She wanted to try another way of living, left the leader and karma, and quietly went to Lai Buddha temple to burn incense.

When she arrived at the temple, Venerable Hai Hien was working in the fields. That day he was wearing a very old short shirt, his face was gentle, cheerful and approachable. The old Venerable continued his unfinished work while talking to everyone. As usual, he advised everyone to diligently recite Buddha's name, and also talked about many benefits of chanting Buddha's name. The young girl looked at the old monk and felt like she had seen her grandfather.

Like many people, this young girl's mind was very shallow, she basically did not put the words of Venerable Hai Hien in her ears, in her heart she thought: Reciting Buddha's name, which is the work of old people, is very far away from us young people.

Like the young man looking for the Venerable to ask him to chant Buddha, after many years, she can still clearly remember the scene when she first met the Venerable Hai Hien.

Later, without waiting for herself to grow old, she took refuge in Buddha. Twenty years later, in the summer of 2007, this laywoman and three other friends went to Lai Buddha Pagoda. This was the second time she visited Venerable Hai Hien.

They arrived at the temple, only to see the main door of the temple open, but the temple was empty without a single person. Several people waited patiently for a long time, finally waiting for the Venerable to return. It turns out, He was constantly working in the fields alone! The old Venerable told them that at present he was the only one living in the pagoda, "farm work comes, if you don't do it, you can't do it, farm work doesn't wait for anyone."

Everyone feels so heavy in their hearts! The old Venerable is over 100 years old. He is here alone, maintaining the pagoda, and planting so many fields! There is not even a person nearby to take care of him. It's so hot, it's already noon, but he still works in the fields, and when he comes back he has to cook and wash clothes himself, even a young man can't stand it!

Everyone said: “You are over 100 years old, you still work hard every day, working so hard, what do you ultimately seek? With his status, it is completely possible to come to the ashram in good conditions to grow old safely!"

The old Venerable said indifferently: “If a person leaving the home life cannot keep his own ashram or temple, then what is the point of practicing? Do you let people speak in a pleasant way? After listening, several people could not contain their respect and admiration for the old Venerable.

The following winter, on a very cold day, the Venerable was alone working in front of the gate of Thien Buddha Pagoda. At this time, a lay person whom he had only met twice came from afar by bicycle. The Venerable had good eyesight and especially good memory. As soon as he saw her, he smiled and greeted her: “Amitabha Buddha, you're back! It's cold on the street, quickly go inside!

Regardless of whether he sees a familiar or unfamiliar person, the Venerable will always say hello first: “Amitabha Buddha, you're back!” He never acted like a gentleman, making the followers who came to the ashram feel warm as if they were coming home.

This female lay follower later had a period of time staying at Thien Buddha pagoda to recite Buddha's name. During that time, the Venerable was also there, so she also had more contact with the Venerable. In her eyes, the Venerable will always be a simple, approachable, kind, cheerful and thrifty person.

After the Mid-Autumn Festival in 2012, this small, peaceful temple of Lai Buddha suddenly gathered a total of 10 lay people from places like Nanyang, Luoyang, Zhumadian, Jiangsu and Shaanxi, etc. At that time, the monastery was not yet famous, so on weekdays very few people came to visit. Master An Chi was very happy and told everyone:

“People from many places gathered at Lai Phat Pagoda, not knowing how many lifetimes of fate it was. So I suggest everyone join together to defeat the Buddha, is that okay?" Everyone unanimously agreed.

One couple also brought their 5-year-old son, who was very mischievous. While several lay people chanted Buddha's name, the Venerable was in the room, stringing beads and taking care of this child. Normally, it was not easy for the old monk to string a string of beads, but this child threw a handful on the ground, causing the beads to roll all over the floor. The old monk did not get angry at all, picked up the beads one by one, and strung them from the beginning.

Venerable Hai Hien has a gentle personality and has been respectful to others throughout his life. No one has seen him lose his temper, nor has he ever seen him slander or look down on anyone. Venerable Hai Hien has never spoken false words in his life. Not only has he never spoken, but he has never even had such a tone. Therefore, regardless of gender, whether leaving the home life or being close to Venerable Hai Hien, there is no one who does not feel joy.

He repeatedly advised his disciples: "It's better to eat salty food and recite Buddha's name than to scold others by being vegetarian."

National Master Hien Thu said that when dealing with people, you must be "gentle and straightforward", honesty is the true heart, and with people, do not use false thoughts, use the true heart. Gentleness is an expression of compassion; For people who have love, they will definitely think more about others and criticize others less. Criticizing people is easy to create resentment towards them. People who speak are careless, people who listen with meaning, holding grudges, and after that, it is very difficult to resolve, so we cannot help but be careful and cautious. In temples, Bodhisattva Maitreya (Venerable Bo Dai) is placed right in front of the main gate, so that people who enter can see an example of learning, learn from His smiling welcome to guests, and learn from His compassionate heart.

“Being a vegetarian scolds people” refers to people who are vegetarians and scold people and treat them poorly. Venerable Hai Hien throughout his life never looked down on anyone, did not treat anyone with a bad attitude, he saw everyone with joy and joy, and from the bottom of his heart came out sincere compassion. Regardless of whether it is towards good people or towards bad people, He smiles from ear to ear. In His heart, there is no one good or bad, no one likes this person, hates that person, everything is always equal, so everyone likes to be close to Him. He is extremely gentle, always using skillful means to satisfy the requests of others, making people feel joy.

Venerable Hai Hien treated all people, things and things without any evil. You offend Him, He takes it as nothing, He doesn't take it to heart; If you say wrong or do wrong in front of Him, He will not reprimand you. He knows why you are not doing things well. He will teach you and will not blame you.

An enthusiastic, outspoken layperson describes himself as the type of person who is "simple-minded, says whatever he thinks". In the early spring of 2012, at Yiwu Buddhist Temple, Indonesia, he saw the Venerable for the first time. Even though he knew he had these bad habits, that day he still thought about what he said when talking. The old Venerable most disliked criticizing and criticizing others, but this time the Venerable once met him and admonished him: “Manage your mouth, don't talk nonsense!”

After hearing this sentence, he thought: The Venerable saw my mistake and immediately showed me that he really treated me like his own child. Thinking of this, my heart was suddenly filled with gratitude and appreciation for the old Venerable.

When he was with the Venerable, he felt like he was really like a child. He always liked to be mischievous in front of the Venerable, always asking the Venerable in turn: “Have you seen Amitabha Buddha? Did Buddha tell you anything?” Every time the Venerable replied as if he were joking with him: "Buddha Gia won't tell you!"

This lay person always deeply respected Venerable Hai Hien. After the Venerable's rebirth, he remembered in detail the details of the time he was with the Venerable. It was almost like the Venerable had never told him any magical words, just taught him how to chant.

Buddha. He finally realized very clearly that: From beginning to end, the Venerable continuously taught him to be truly old and obediently recite Buddha's name.

Why can Venerable Hai Hien often see the World of Ultimate Bliss and Amitabha Buddha often? Because in His mind there were no distracting thoughts, He had long ago let go of all the people, things and things of this world, so he was greatly free in depending on conditions. Wisdom is revealed within depending on fate, He has no afflictions. Old Venerable Hai Hien used his true heart all his life. He used his sincere heart to treat people and things in daily life. The true heart is the sincere heart that one has oneself, in the true heart there is not a bit of falsehood, not a bit of deception - neither self-deception nor others. The moment a child is just born, he or she completely uses the true mind, so everyone has used the true mind. Unfortunately, the true mind is polluted by the environment. After being infected, there is no way to turn back, forever using it until old age and death. If you don't use your true mind, you will use a false mind. All false thoughts and thoughts are the cause of samsara, so after death, samsara will stay in the six paths and will never be able to come out. This is an extremely tragic thing.

All the people, things, and things that the Venerable saw from morning to night, there was nothing that he hated, nothing that he did not like, he was always in harmony, with a smiling face towards any person, thing, or thing. He always favors sentient beings and has never said before: “What should I do?”

It's good to treat people in this world in a way that makes everyone happy. So will you benefit from it or not? Sometimes it's there, sometimes it's absolutely not there, regardless of whether it's there or not, it's fun.

Every time the lay dharma protector arranged for the Venerable to participate in any activity, he never refused. He did not think about himself, only thinking about making sentient beings happy. If participating in a large-scale dharma conference, the old Venerable always prepares his robes and dharma weapons early, dresses very neatly and cleanly, and arrives at the dharma conference site early. No matter how long the release lasted, the old Venerable was always cheerful, without losing his solemnity and majesty.

In the group of people, when someone bowed or made offerings to the Venerable, his facial expression was always kind, gentle and intimate, making each lay person feel extremely warm and happy. Making offerings of money to Him, all He left at the temple or Buddha hall to invite, as funds to free sentient beings or distribute scriptures. When releasing the birds, the Venerable will personally open the bird's cage, look at the little bird with eyes full of compassion, one after another flying back to the forest, flying into the blue sky, on His face full of wrinkles, there is now a gentle and kind expression! His charisma and compassion can always touch everyone present.

The entire life-releasing activity usually has to continue from early morning until one or two o'clock in the afternoon. Young people may also feel a bit tired, but the over 100-year-old Venerable Hai Hien is always in full spirit, not realizing that he is a bit bored and tired.

Some people who met the Venerable wanted to take pictures with him alone. The Venerable had never refused before, on the contrary, he actively coordinated and tried his best to satisfy the wishes of the masses. From beginning to end, He still maintained his smile, not afraid to bother taking souvenir photos with each group of lay people, or taking photos with each person individually, or taking photos with many people, or taking family photos. He was patient, He was not afraid of fatigue, everyone liked Him very much.

For several hours in a row, without any rest, let alone someone over 100 years old, even a young person wouldn't be able to stand it. One time, after the activity ended, the straightforward-speaking Indonesian layman drove the old monk back to Buddha's temple. When he got off the bus, the Venerable said shyly to him: “I got my car all wet…”

The layman asked him: “How?”

He said: “I peed in my pants…”

It turned out that there was no toilet at the activity site. After the activity, everyone rushed to take pictures with the Venerable. In order to satisfy the wishes of the masses, the Venerable endured it all. The lay person immediately felt extremely embarrassed and guilty, tears suddenly flowed from his eyes: We don't really have any sympathy for an old person over 100 years old!

Old Venerable Hai Hien is not only a person who behaves in accordance with the world's people, but in fact he is also a person who understands human emotions very well.

The wise old monk of his life, many times confirmed that the tragic vow of Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara was indeed not false.

When Venerable Hai Hien was 12 years old, his father passed away. Because he wanted to relieve his mother's pressure, he went out to ask for food for 3 months. His filial heart was felt by the restaurant owner who hired him. From the age of 13 to 18, during these 5 years, he continuously worked at this restaurant. The owner always took care of the whole family of Venerable Hai Hien, so he was very grateful to him, and never forgot. Even though he had left the home life, every time he returned to his hometown, he always remembered to visit his original owner.

In the fall of 1938, Venerable Hai Hien returned to his hometown to handle work. The boss's son-in-law is studying at this time

Nam Duong, needs his family to send him some winter clothes and household items. But there was work in the boss's house and he couldn't leave, so he asked Venerable Hai Hien to help him bring clothes and daily necessities to Nam Duong. The day Venerable Hai Hien arrived in Nam Duong, he encountered the Japanese army dispatching 40 planes to bomb the city of Nam Duong. He was not afraid, sitting under a corner of the wall, concentrating on reciting "Namo Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva". At that time, there were seven planes circling above his head, taking turns dropping bombs. The situation was very dangerous, but Venerable Hai Hien was not the least bit hurt. Kinh says: "The world's good men, good women, the poor are in danger and terror, they are destined for Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva at their birth, they cannot achieve false liberation", throughout his entire life, the Venerable Hai Hien repeatedly confirmed that Bodhisattva's tragic wish was truly not false.

In the early fall of 2008, 88-year-old Truong Thai Thai came to Lai Buddha Pagoda to visit Venerable Hai Hien. Elder Truong Thai Thai stayed in the temple for two or three months. Because she had diabetes, she had to eat seven or eight meals a day. The Venerable specially arranged for Dharma Master An Vinh to take care of her daily activities.

Elder Truong Thai Thai's father was two years older than the Venerable, and was a childhood playmate with the Venerable. Truong Thai Thai was born in the year Venerable Hai Hien left the home life. The father and daughter of these two generations of family members maintained a relationship with the Venerable at the end of their lives. Master An Vinh only felt particularly moved and said: "Flowers are as red as the sun, people are as bright as the sun", yet the old Venerable's friends, once made, are not just a generation of people!

24. Humble and respectful

Old Venerable Hai Hien sees everything in this world as good: Favorable circumstances are good, adversity is good, bad fate is also good, nothing is bad, everything is good. He once told his disciples: “In my eyes, everything is good, nothing is bad. Say good things about everything you see, be happy about everything you see. Only then will there always be abundant Dharma joy in your mind. Only then can your mind be pure, only then will you not be troubled, only then will you not be angry or hate others. Without distinguishing between good and bad, there is no good food or bad food, it all depends on fate, then you can rest assured."

He has no discrimination or attachment to all people, things, or things. His mind is clear and clear. He knows that everything is the self-nature that appears, what's not good? Furthermore, the Avatamsaka Sutra says: "All sentient beings are inherently Buddha", "all sentient beings have the wisdom and virtue of the Tathagata", saying so, it is even more impossible to look down on others and look down on others. Therefore, in life, cultivating the virtue of humility, not being arrogant, being respectful to everyone, being happy for everyone, and only having a pure and egalitarian mind can manifest money.

The Venerable all his life did not defame anyone, did not criticize anyone. In the Infinite Life Sutra it says: "Smartly keep your karma, don't say about other people's faults", old Venerable Hai Hien has done it, all his life he does not say other people's faults, does not look down on anyone, is sincere and respectful towards everyone (in respect there is humility), this is the Buddha's teachings, old Venerable Hai Hien himself has done very well.

Chinese people say that in ceremony, the most important thing in ceremony is majesty. Khuc Le wrote: "No disrespect, no worries, peace of mind, peace of people's ears." The sentences in the Ceremony - Khuc Le express the spirit of the ceremony.

“No disrespect” has the same meaning as the first article in the Samantabhadra Bodhisattva ten vows “Respect to all Buddhas”, also the first sentence, saying first of all to be respectful, so we know, the education of worldly dharma and transcendental dharma, is to take respect as the basis of being human. Whatever the Venerable sees is good, whatever he sees is happy, it is truly "Disrespectful"! The ten good karmas that Shakyamuni Buddha often said include body karma, speech karma and karma, "No disrespect" is the meaning of karma, in the heart there are two words "filial piety", always keep a respectful mind towards people, things, and things, and don't dare to be a little arrogant. Why be respectful? Because the entire universe and ourselves are one. All dharmas are born of self-nature, self-nature is the true mind, the physical body, in other words, the relationship of all dharmas with oneself is one body.

"Nguyen Nhua Tu" is the karma body, like you are very focused on thinking about an important issue, your attitude is very serious, this means the body must be dignified and dignified. When talking, you must speak with "concentrated words", your words must be affirming and gentle, this is karma. Regarding our language, Buddha often said we must "not lie, not tell lies, not lie, not speak evil words", this is calm words.

The third thing is done, the effect is "Peace to the people", peaceful families, peaceful society, peaceful world. Everyone can do these words.

Next in the signing ceremony said: "Desire cannot last, desire cannot be satisfied, will cannot be satisfied, happiness cannot be extreme", otherwise it is contrary to the mind of reverence. If the heart is respectful, then the person is naturally humble and can naturally let go of desires. Only in accordance with a pure mind, in accordance with morality, can we practice filial piety and have effective results.

One year before the Venerable's rebirth, talking about the subject of the abbot, the Venerable said to a lay person: "I'm illiterate, how can I become an abbot?... Now I only know how to recite my Buddha's name." In this era of ours, the Buddha Dharma has declined, there are still people vying to be the abbot of a small temple, vying to be the manager. Old Venerable Hai Hien is humble and does not consider himself the greatest.

Those who respect others are blessed, those who are humble are blessed. In the 64 hexagrams of the Dich Kinh, each hexagram has bad and auspicious elements, good and bad elements, and good and bad elements. There is only 1 hexagram that has only sand and no negative elements - the six lines are all auspicious, this hexagram is called the humble hexagram. The scholar interpreted this hexagram: The person who receives this hexagram will be blessed with peace and prosperity, and all things will be achieved; The future of a humble person is very great.

The hexagram of the humble hexagram is "Dia mountain khiem", above is the land; Below are mountains, mountains are on the ground, high on the inside and low on the outside, tall but not arrogant, this is the meaning of humility. Therefore, even if we have high intelligence, high virtue, high conduct, we should have a humble expression towards all people, things, and things. There is nothing like people. Applying this principle to life, we will be humble and respectful towards anyone - including the stupidest people, those with deep karma.

Old Venerable Hai Hien is full of humility, respect, sincerity, and purity. This is a blessing; Truly old, obedient, true to action, this is his good root, his master taught him a Buddha phrase, this is the fate: A person full of good roots, merits and blessings, with such karma, how can he not achieve it!

When preaching the sutra, Dharma Master Tinh Khong said that according to his judgment, after the Venerable Hai Hien left the home life at the age of 20 and recited Buddha's name for three years, he could achieve complete success. Once you have achieved complete perfection, you will definitely be able to rebirth the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, affirming that you will see Buddha, this is the goal of Pure Land students. If you still have a life span at this time, you don't need it anymore, praying to Buddha to take you to the World of Ultimate Bliss, no problem; If he recites for three more years, he will definitely achieve undisturbed single-mindedness; In another three or five years, he can reach the principle of undisturbed mind, this is the highest realm. Therefore, Dharma Master Tinh Khong is sure that everything that old Venerable Hai Hien attained is the same realm as the great thorough enlightenment, the clear mind and enlightenment that Zen school often talks about. Having attained this position, being reborn in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, he announced the name of rebirth, which also means being reborn as an upper-class person, reborn in the third and ninth levels. This is a great, unbelievable achievement!

25. I didn't study anything, just chanted Amitabha Buddha

Venerable Hai Hien, 20 years old, left the home life. His master was a very good person. His master knew that this disciple was really old, obedient, and true to action, so he taught him a phrase "Amitabha Buddha", telling him to recite it continuously, and he really did not stop reciting it for 92 years.

Someone once asked Venerable Hai Hien: “You left the home life in such a world, the master didn't teach you anything, only taught you to recite 'Amitabha Buddha', right?”

Venerable Hai Hien calmly responded: "Teaching Buddha recitation only".

The layman asked again: “Have you ever preached the sutra?”

“Have I preached the sutras yet? I have never preached. I didn't study anything, just recited 'Amitabha Buddha'.

I never went to school a day, I don't know a word. After going up the mountain, my master taught me to just recite 'Amitabha Buddha', telling me that once I understood clearly, I was not allowed to speak or move my arms or legs."

His master said "understanding" means enlightenment. Why did His master remind Him, after understanding clearly, not to speak? The moments of fate are not the same. If the old Venerable was in the era of Shakyamuni Buddha Buddha, Shakyamuni Buddha Buddha would definitely send him to preach the sutras and teach. That year, the senior disciples achieved Buddha Da's principle of one mind and undisturbed mind. There were nine months in a year where he had to take Buddha's place and go out to preach the Dharma. If the old Venerable had been born during the Tang Dynasty, he would have avoided jealousy and obstacles like the Sixth Patriarch. At the age of 24, Great Master Huineng became the Patriarch, but everyone did not accept him. He only knew how to hide in a hunting team for 15 years. Therefore, the predestined moments are not the same.

What the master told Venerable Hai Hien, he has done, this type of teaching is for us modern people to see. If you tell others after your enlightenment, people will say that you talk nonsense and say misleading words, so the old Venerable Consecrated Precepts told him "don't say it", as long as he really does his own job well that's all.

Therefore, when people asked the Venerable what kind of realm it was to recite the Buddha's name, the Venerable smiled without answering - in fact, his expression had already answered.

This conversation was 4 months before the rebirth of the Venerable Hai Hien. Many lay people at the Buddha Recitation Hall in Yiwu Nam Duong seriously prepared a few questions to ask the Venerable for guidance.

Old Venerable Hai Hien told them: “Now that I am over 100 years old, I must be reborn to the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. The Buddha Family is the source of my Venerable! I have begged Elder Buddha Gia several times to follow Him, but Elder Buddha Gia did not teach me to follow Him, saying I practice very well, asking me to live two more years, to be an example for everyone to see - teaching me the Dharma in the world." The “Old Buddha Family” he spoke of was Amitabha Buddha.

During the life of the Venerable Hai Hien, he went through many things, but in any situation, he was able to not be disturbed or influenced. One Buddha sentence was recited to the end, in the words of his friend, the Venerable Dien Cuong, it was "a sentence 'Amitabha Buddha', chanted for a lifetime without turning away"! During the "Van Cach" period, Buddha was not allowed to recite, it was okay, he recited it silently in his mind, without speaking; At night when everyone was sleeping, he woke up and bowed to the Buddha. He recited without forgetting the Three Jewels, without leaving the Three Jewels.

After starting "Van Cach", the person leaving the home life was forced to return home, Venerable Hai Hien said: “I don't have a home, I'm not going home.” Later, he was arranged to be the head of the production team.

Layman Liu asked Venerable Hai Hien: “How many years have you been the head of the production team? Do you recite Buddha?”

Old Venerable Hai Hien gently replied: “At that time, did other people let you chant Buddha? People don't allow recitation! Why? You are all 'masses', do you dare to recite Buddha's name?"

Layman Liu continued to ask: "If you don't let me recite, then recite in my mind?"

The old Venerable smiled and replied: "Recite in your mind, on the top of the mountain, when going to release the buffalo, sit on a rock and recite."

Dharma Master Dien Cuong said that in the past, when the Venerable was on the mountain, he worked so tired during the day that he had a headache and dizziness, and at night he still chanted Buddha, bowing to the Buddha all night. He praised the Venerable's effort in reciting the Buddha, saying to the Venerable, "Walking, standing, lying down, reciting Amitabha Buddha, he has already reached this level"!

Old Venerable Hai Hien followed the precepts of the Most Venerable Monk, and throughout his life he kept and recited the name Amitabha Buddha without interruption. He often told people that for decades of his life, he always woke up at three o'clock in the morning, after lighting incense sticks, he would sit down and recite Buddha's name, or he would slowly stand up and circumambulate Buddha. If circumambulating Buddha was sleepy, he would lean against it and continue reciting Buddha's name.

It's the same all year round.

A lay person spent some time at Thien Buddha pagoda chanting Buddha, at that time the Venerable was also at Thien Buddha pagoda. The layman said that every day, the Venerable would wake up at three o'clock in the morning. When everyone heard the Venerable step by step and say "Amitabha Buddha" outside the window, they knew that he had already woken up and was on his way to the bathroom. Everyone was embarrassed so they did not continue to sleep and quickly woke up with him.

The Venerable said very sincerely to everyone:

Reciting Buddha's name doesn't mean you can practice well if you recite it just a little bit!

For 92 years, He himself has never forgotten this saying Buddha's name, His Buddha's name is constantly reciting Buddha's name, when he eats he also recites Buddha's name, wearing his clothes also recites Buddha's name, His activities do not leave the Buddha's name: When working in the fields, neither a hoe nor a shovel can leave the Buddha's name; When talking to someone, just after talking, the Buddha signal continued to appear. This is the person chanting Buddha!

noi_dung:
26. The story of the old Venerable

Venerable Hai Hien often, not even afraid of trouble, told the story of Venerable Lao Duc to everyone.

Venerable Lao Duc and Venerable Hai Hien are fellow monks. They lost their father when they were young and followed their mother to beg. On an extremely cold winter day, Lao Duc and his mother, both hungry and cold, went to Kim Son pagoda in Chi Dong district, Binh Thi town, begged the Dharma Master Abbot Hai Tham to accept him for mercy, and hoped that the Dharma Master could accept Lao Duc as a disciple. Dharma Master Hai Tham did not accept Lao Duc's invitation, but brought him to the statue of Vida Bodhisattva, so that he could worship Vida Bodhisattva as his teacher.

Because Lao Duc was stupid, his mother called him "Lao Ngai", the Indonesian language "Ngai" and

“Duc” has the same sound, so for a long time, “Lao Ngai” has become “Lao Duc”.

Lao Duc left the home life like that. He did not have a master, nor a Dharma name, nor was he ordained. Since then, the people of Binh Thi town, dozens of miles away, remember Venerable Ngai - a person who carried a cloth bag on his shoulder every day to go out to create charm.

Dharma Master Hai Tham taught him to recite "Amitabha Buddha" while walking. As expected, he was sincere while walking. The women and naughty children in the village found Him stupid and often made fun of Him. Venerable Lao Duc was not angry, he just clasped his hands and bowed to him, continuously chanting "Amitabha Buddha, Amitabha Buddha..."

Someone teased Him and said: “Old Duc, you bow once, I will give you food.”

Lao Duc said: “Without Buddha, I do not bow.”

People pointed to a rock and said: “Inside there is Buddha.”

Venerable Lao Duc put down his cloth bag, knelt on the ground, bowed his head and bowed to the rock. Everyone found this game fun, so they often teased him. For a long time, Venerable Lao Duc's forehead turned into a large bag of eggs.

There are some people who are even more outrageous, pointing to buffalo dung and saying to Venerable Lao Duc: “Inside there is Buddha.”

Venerable Lao Duc said: “There is Buddha, I bow to the Buddha.” Having finished speaking, he bowed his head and bowed to buffalo dung.

One time, someone put a string on His ear and said: "Old Duc, I've tied you here, you can't move!" Venerable Lao Duc immediately stood in that position and cried. He stood like that under the sunlight for a long time without moving.

Later, someone passed by this place and asked him why he was crying. He said: “Being tied up by someone else.”

People asked Him: “What do you use to tie it up?”

He said: “Use the rope.”

That person said: “Where is the column?”

He said: “The ear is tied.”

A passerby took the rope from His ear and said to Him: “I took it off for you, you can go.”

Old Duc immediately stopped crying and smiled, then clasped his hands and recited Buddha's name to pay respects to that person.

Every time Venerable Lao Duc returns to the monastery, he must first kneel and bow to Vi Da Bodhisattva, saying to Bodhisattva: “Master, I'm home.” Then bring the charmed objects to the Main Hall to worship Buddha.

During the day, he went out to create conditions, at night he bowed to Vida Bodhisattva, all year round, all month, every day.

In December 1954, Venerable Lao Duc fell ill, but refused medicine, so he immediately asked: “What day is December 8th?” Ask several times every day.

Dharma Master Hai Tham asked him privately: “The teacher kept asking, what are you doing on the 8th of December?” Venerable Lao Duc replied: “My master told me, on the 8th of December, Amitabha Buddha will come and pick me up.” Dharma Master Hai Tham silently remembered and silently praised.

Soon it was the 8th day of the December month, on the contrary, Venerable Lao Duc did not ask anymore. Someone said to Him: “Today is the 8th of December, what exactly do you want to do?” After hearing this sentence, Lao Duc seemed very surprised and said: “So what? So I'm leaving.” He asked someone to bring him a tub of bathing water, washed himself, changed his clothes, sat upright, recited Buddha's name, and passed away.

Two years after Venerable Lao Duc's rebirth, there is still such a legend circulating. There were a few businessmen who came to Wuhan to do business. At the beginning of Wuhan street, they met Venerable Ngai, who was carrying a cloth bag on his shoulder, and everyone said he looked like Lao Duc, so they came up to greet him and said: “Old Duc, why did you go to Wuhan?”

Venerable Ngai looked at them, smiled and said: “It's fate!”

People say: “Let's go home with us.”

Venerable Ngai said: “I won't be back in a few days.”

When some businessmen returned from Wuhan, they told the people of Binh Thi town at the beginning of Wuhan street to meet Lao Duc, only to learn that Lao Duc had been reborn two years ago. But they insisted that the person they met was Venerable Lao Duc.

No one knows the story of Venerable Lao Duc, leaving the home life in Indonesia. In Dong Bach Huyen Chi, there is also a record of this Venerable Lao Duc: “Monk Lao Duc, from Truyen Thuc, Kim Son pagoda, Binh Thi town, has a naive nature, does not know how to avoid others when going to the toilet, does not know hunger or thirst, walks straight forward, does not turn around, does not stop to look, his behavior is strange, making it difficult for people to guess. Every day he went to the village to make fun of the women and children, worshiped Vi Da at night, didn't sleep all night, every time he bowed to the Buddha his head hit the ground and made a sound, causing his forehead to swell, it went on like that for more than ten years, all year round. In the winter of 1954, he was sick in bed and refused medicine. Every day he asked what day was December 8. Everyone answered honestly. Until December 8, Venerable Lao Duc took a shower and changed his clothes, sitting upright and chanting Buddha's passing away.

Venerable Lao Duc, Venerable Hai Hien, Venerable Hai Khanh, the younger brother of Venerable Hai Hien, they all have the Buddha's name in their lifetime, their practice methods are bowing to the Buddha, chanting the Buddha's name, and disturbing the Buddha. Their lives do not leave the Buddha name, their work also does not leave the Buddha name, and when dealing with people and things, the Buddha name is not interrupted. Only when sleeping do not chant Buddha, but after waking up, Buddha's name continues. They have become a habit of reciting Buddha, and in their hearts they truly have Amitabha Buddha. This is the example of someone chanting Buddha!

noi_dung:
27. When working, don't miss reciting Buddha's name

The old Venerable Hai Hien's job was farming and labor. He was very skilled at those labors, so while working he did not need to think, just recite Buddha's name.

When Dharma Master An Chi, a disciple of Venerable Hai Hien, remembered the old Venerable saying:

“The old monk worked and recited Buddha's name, rarely speaking. The old Venerable all his life chanted the holy name 'Amitabha Buddha' to be steadfast and unshakable, to recite and not forget. Because when he meets others, he advises them to recite Buddha's name. He himself cannot help but recite Buddha's name!"

How did Old Venerable Hai Hien cultivate so successfully? This is a Buddha saying. He had no distracting thoughts, no false thoughts, no matter what he was doing, he still recited "Amitabha Buddha" in his mouth, no matter what he was doing, he did not miss his own practice. His work does not hinder his practice, his life does not hinder his practice, his dealings with people do not hinder his practice, his practice and his work and activities, blend into one.

Dharma Master An Vinh, the Venerable's disciple, saw his master busy every day from morning to night. He thought to himself that the Venerable was already at this age, so he shouldn't be allowed to do so many things. One day the Dharma Master said to his master: "Let's leave these things to you guys to do. Master just recite Buddha's name and that's enough." But the old Venerable said to the Dharma Master: "When working, don't forget to chant Buddha!"

No matter what the old monk did, his name as Buddha would not be interrupted, for 92 years without interruption.

Basically, old Venerable Hai Hien silently chanted Vajra. In Buddha's mind, if the mouth does not move, it is called silent recitation; The mouth moves but there is no sound, this is called reciting Vajra.

After interacting with the Venerable for a long time, you will discover that no matter whether he walks, stands, or sits, he always gently purses his lips. One time, a young Dharma Master and the Venerable were digging peanuts from the ground together. He saw that when the Venerable picked up peanuts, he always pursed his lips and couldn't help but asked: “Master, you always purse your lips, what are you talking about?” Old Venerable Hai Hien replied: “Amitabha Buddha!”

Every year after the fall, the old monk dug up tree roots, then split them and dried them in preparation for winter heating. Some people say that the Venerable's forte is reciting Buddha's name and splitting tree roots. Tree roots are the most difficult to split, but the old Venerable had patience. He took the ax to split and chanted "Amitabha Buddha" until he split the tree roots into pieces.

One day when Venerable Hai Hien was 112 years old

Vien Minh pagoda, he saw the branches of the sycamore tree hanging down low, obstructing worshipers from entering and exiting. He took an ax and a saw and climbed the stairs up the tree to cut it down. The disciples saw this and thought in their hearts: The Master is over 100 years old and still climbs the tree himself to work. This is the Buddha's Sangha! But let's change our way of thinking: I'm already a 112 year old person, what if something goes wrong? It seemed that the old monk saw through his disciple's thoughts and smiled and said: “It's okay, it's okay, I'm chanting Buddha!”

The Venerable was an ordinary farmer who only knew how to farm. Leaving the home life, he doesn't know how to preach the sutras, the five ways of practice of people leaving the home life, he doesn't even know how to play the Dharma weapon - He doesn't know anything, he only knows how to chant Buddha's name, he only knows that he works diligently every day, but without hindrance, chanting the Buddha's name.

Dharma Master Hongyi once said: “Amitabha Buddha is the unsurpassed king of physicians; to abandon him and not seek him is sheer folly.” Refusing to recite the Buddha's name is not stupidity but delusion. Truly knowing the merit of this Buddha's name, the meaning of this Buddha's name, is there any reason not to recite it! Where is Niem? Like Venerable Hai Hien, everywhere, at all times. When you have this Buddha name in your mind, it is the ashram - the great ashram of Amitabha Buddha, the ashram is nowhere to be found, it is never absent, this is the Dharma ashram.

28. THERE IS Buddha IN MY MIND,

tieu_de: 28. With Buddha in mind, no matter what you do, you will not be tired

noi_dung:
28. With Buddha in mind, no matter what you do, you will not be tired

That monk was a young man who in 1992 was brought by his uncle to Lai Buddha pagoda to ask the Venerable Hai Hien to chant Buddha's name. In 2010, under the guidance of Dharma Master An Chi, he entered Buddha's door.

One time the old monk was chopping wood in the monastery, this layman saw him so he came over and said: "You're old, don't do things like that anymore. What should you do when you're tired and sick?"

The old monk smiled and said: “Being a human has many jobs! If you can do it yourself, do it yourself, don't expect others."

The layman asked him again: “You keep working all day long, aren't you tired?”

The old Venerable said gently: "When you're tired from work, recite 'Amitabha Buddha' in your heart and you won't be tired anymore." After speaking, he smiled very kindly, very happily, very honestly.

In the spring of 2011, Dharma Master Khai Trung and a group of five people went to Lai Buddha Pagoda to visit Venerable Hai Hien. The old Venerable normally spoke very little, this time he talked to them for 12 hours. He advised everyone to definitely listen to the Dharma of old Dharma Master Tinh Khong, don't miss the opportunity to become Buddha in this life, don't be attached to money and worldly love, if you pass through this village, there will no longer be that inn, this world is nothingness, don't continue to suffer in the Saha World, the Ultimate Bliss World is so good, if you diligently recite Buddha's name you can reach it, why not diligently recite Buddha's name? The old Dharma Master preached sutras just to welcome us. Where can we go to find such a good thing? If you sincerely recite Buddha's name, you still have to do the things that should be done, you can't not do them, as long as your mind is pure, there is only Amitabha Buddha, don't pay attention to other things, you won't miss out on becoming a Buddha.

The Venerable finished speaking and said to them: “Don't go this afternoon, eat fragrant noodles.” Having finished speaking, he conveniently put the sickle in his belt, held the ladder towards the rosewood tree, then climbed up the tree. With a little effort, he was able to cut a large branch of rosewood sprouts.

Everyone grabbed the incense stick that the Venerable had cut, and helped the Venerable hold on to the ladder, waiting for him to climb down. A few people advised the Venerable to take care of his body and not do these things all day long. The old Venerable smiled and said: "If you have Buddha in your heart, you won't be tired no matter what you do."

The old monk is so old, working every day from morning to night, how can he not feel tired?

When he was working, he didn't think he was working, didn't think he was tired, in his mind there was only the Buddha's name. All dharmas are born from the mind. If you don't think about being tired, you won't be tired. If you don't think about suffering, then you won't be suffering. If you recite and recite "Amitabha Buddha", then the dharma will be full of joy.

When He works without "self", He forgets himself, He is selfless. So no matter how much His work is or how long He works, He is absolutely not tired. Some people praise him for his good health, but they don't know why his health is so good. That is because He has let go of all conditions.

Old Venerable Hai Hien appeared to us in a truly wonderful way. He truly let go of all conditions.

Old Venerable Hai Hien worked hard and diligently all his life, never having a day of rest. He is not tired, his outward appearance is a sign of joy and happiness. He works in the fields and is cultivating. His Buddha name lasts 24 hours without interruption. It can be said that in His mind there are no impurities, no conditions, no merits of not depending on joy, although depending on conditions, depending on joy, he does not leave any in his mind, always keeping his mind pure, equal, and enlightened. This is the old Venerable Hai Hien, this is called practicing Pure Land, pure mind means pure Buddha land. He chanted like that for 92 years, knowing in advance the day and time of his free rebirth to Amitabha Buddha's Pure Land.
