noi_dung:
34. The old Venerable and his disciples

Among the disciples of the old Venerable Hai Hien, there are many who are extremely excellent. After coming down the mountain, his disciples were divided into Dai Giang, South and North, Ngu Dai Son, Pho Da Tu, Shaolin Temple, Bach Ma Tu, Minh Son Co Sat. All of them had his disciples who passed down the teachings and propagated the Dharma to benefit living beings. Moreover, most of them were responsible for main tasks in the monastic ashram, such as Dharma Master An Tung, the head of Shaolin Monastery, which many people know, is the old Venerable. Hai Hien's world; Like the Dharma Master An Tong who restored the Co Sat Two Seat in Nam Duong, he was also a disciple of the old Venerable. Here we only record the last life story of the old Venerable and a few disciples.

Master An Chi

Currently, the abbot of Lai Buddha Pagoda is Dharma Master An Chi - the Venerable's successor. On the 3rd day of the third lunar month, 1986, he and Venerable Hai Hien met. At that time, he had not yet left the home life.

A few days before getting to know the Venerable, he discovered that a nephew of the same clan as him, also his playmate when he was young, did not eat meat, did not drink alcohol, just like him. He followed the question until the end, and it turned out that people had taken refuge in the Three Jewels under the court of Venerable Hai Hien at Lai Buddha Pagoda, receiving the five precepts. Dharma Master An Chi was influenced by his mother who had been a vegetarian and chanted Buddha all her life. Not only was she not opposed to studying Buddhism, but she was also focused on it. It was such a predestined relationship that he played with his nephew of the same clan, and a few days later they went to Lai Buddha temple to seek refuge.

As soon as Dharma Master An Chi met the Venerable Hai Hien, he felt like he had met a relative. In his eyes, the Venerable was so close, compassionate, and honest. After that day, if he did not go to the monastery for a few days and did not see the Venerable, he would miss him and feel very impatient. So every ten days to half a month, he came to the monastery once. At that time, his house still did not have a bicycle, and each walk took two or three hours.

In September 1987, because he was busy with farming, Dharma Master An Chi did not visit the Venerable for 3 months. One morning, Dharma Master An Chi was having breakfast with his neighbors outside when he saw the Venerable holding a basket and walking towards him. Master An Chi immediately put down his bowl and chopsticks and quickly ran over there. He bowed his head to the Venerable, then asked: “Where are you going?”

“Come visit me!”

Dharma Master An Chi held the old monk's hand tightly, was moved to tears and asked: “Master, are you here for something?”

"Nothing, come visit me, I haven't been to the monastery for a long time, see what you're busy doing, are you lazy to recite Buddha's name?"

Disturbing an 87-year-old Venerable, especially from a long distance to visit him, Dharma Master An Chi immediately felt extremely ashamed.

After Dharma Master An Chi left the home life at Lai Buddha Pagoda, Venerable Hai Hien told him: “Here we specialize in reciting Buddha's name, not doing Buddha's repentance sutras. It is better to not have a temple than to not have religion; It is better to have no people than to not have the Dharma.”

When he first started at the ashram, Dharma Master An Chi felt it was very new, so he studied very diligently, but after a long time, he felt monotonous and boring, he wanted to go out and change, wanted to find another shortcut. It seemed that the old Venerable saw what he was thinking and said to him: “Find the south and run north, it's not as good as keeping a small temple.”

But Dharma Master An Chi did not listen to his master's words, so he left his master and went to other monasteries to study. After five or six years of studying, he discovered that his many years of practice were all in vain, and he was completely disappointed.

In 2003, while extremely disappointed, he remembered his master's teachings, then he returned to his master's side and repented with him. Old Venerable Hai Hien did not have a single word of blame. He looked at Dharma Master An Chi and Dharma Master An Ham, and said gently: "If you don't want to stay at Lai Buddha pagoda, you can go to Dong Bach mountain, Thap Vien pagoda is also my ashram, the situation there is better than here." The old monk took out a few thousand and asked someone for help to buy a plow to plow for the two of them to use. However, when the two of them arrived at Thap Vien Pagoda not long after, they criticized the mountain land for being too steep and invited each other to "escape".

Old Venerable Hai Hien still did not blame the two disciples. He personally took Dharma Master An Ham and An Chi to Thien Buddha Pagoda, instructing them to diligently practice and revive this ancient ashram with two thousand years of history. Not long after, Dharma Master An Chi also followed him to Thien Buddha Pagoda to stay for a long time.

On August 18, 2007, at the age of 107 years old, Venerable Hai Hien, Dharma Master An Chi returned to Lai Buddha Pagoda to wish his master a long life. The old Venerable met him and said with tears in his eyes: "An Chi, don't go anymore, I'm over a hundred years old, I won't live for many more years, but until now the monastery still hasn't found a suitable successor, so don't go anymore." Seeing tears falling down his master's cheeks, Dharma Master An Chi did not have the heart to refuse, so he stayed by his master's side and remained filial.

From the first time he met Venerable Hai Hien, until now, it has been 21 years.

In the fall of 2008, in the presence of the lay dharma protectors in the village, the old Venerable solemnly entrusted Lai Buddha Pagoda to his disciple, Dharma Master An Chi. The Venerable said: "I'm old, it's time to let go. Lai Buddha Pagoda will be handed over to you. I can rest assured that you will do well in the future."

Dharma Master An Chi knelt before his master and said: “Master, please rest assured, I will definitely not let you down, I will keep your teachings in mind, recite one sentence ‘Amitabha Buddha’ to the end, take full responsibility for myself, depending on fate to save them, continue to pass on the good tradition of Lai Buddha Temple!”

Regarding monastery management, the Venerable often taught: “Don't be afraid of not having a temple, just be afraid of not having religion. It is better to have no people than to not have dharma.”

"If you don't come, I don't blame you. If you come, you must receive my precepts."

He again advised Dharma Master An Chi, "Don't be afraid of not having a pagoda, just be afraid of not having a religion." He also said, "If you are neither deaf nor blind, you are not worthy of being an abbot", the meaning of this saying is for Dharma Master An Chi to be able to endure, but also to give in, not being able to be like others.

The monastery was entrusted to Dharma Master An Chi. The Venerable Hai Hien's daily work was to work and recite Buddha's name. A year before the old Venerable's rebirth, he once said to a lay person: “I'm illiterate, how can I become an abbot?… Now I just chant my Buddha.”

Master An Chi is truly a great filial son. In November 2011, the old Venerable fell ill. Dharma Master An Chi considered his master's old age and carefully considered it. He took the old Venerable to the second people's hospital in Xa Ky district for treatment. During the treatment period, Dharma Master An Chi was always by his side to take care of his teacher. The old Venerable had a stomachache and defecated, soiling all his clothes. Dharma Master An Chi cleaned the old Venerable like he was serving his parents. He cast each spoon, each spoonful, for the old Venerable to eat, and continued to visit and care for him.

The old Venerable lay on the hospital bed and kept chanting "Amitabha Buddha".

The Venerable was in the hospital for a few days. These days, Dharma Master An Chi cannot sleep. Waiting for his illness to improve, the Venerable said to Dharma Master An Chi: “I'm fine, you should rest too!” Master An Chi was moved and said: “Master, your health is important, I don't dare to neglect it. As long as your health is good, it is my precious blessings! I hope you recover soon, let's go back to the monastery! When Dharma Master An Chi said this sentence, tears filled his eyes, and the lay people there were also moved.

It was not until the old Venerable recovered and was discharged from the hospital that Dharma Master An Chi breathed a sigh of relief.

After the rebirth of the Venerable Hai Hien, Dharma Master An Chi was extremely moved and said to the old Dharma Master Tinh Khong, whom he respected: “Master has left, recalling his every word and action, it is truly admirable! When the master was still alive, we all admired him to the point of reaching the ground; After the master left, recalling every word, every action, every move, I actually shed tears without realizing it."

In the recording room of Dharma Master Tinh Khong's daily sutra lectures, a picture of Venerable Hai Hien was hung. One day in August 2014, Dharma Master An Chi came to Hong Kong to visit Dharma Master Tinh Khong. When he saw the image of Venerable Hai Hien in the recording room, he immediately cried. Looking at it, one can see the respect the disciple has for the master.

After the old Venerable Hai Hien passed away, in order to record his master's virtues and pass them down to future generations, Dharma Master An Chi, along with a group of people, climbed the pass and waded through the stream, along the Dong Bach mountain range, looking for the footprints that the old Venerable had passed. Sometimes when they walk along steep cliffs, they suddenly encounter strong winds. If they don't pay attention, they will be blown down the cliff. At this time, they can only cling to the lava on the way to climb forward. Although it was hard work, we collected a lot of valuable documents.

Following, there were also many Buddha disciples who were close to the Venerable, writing literature carefully recalling their meetings with the Venerable. Dharma Master An Chi, for everyone, edited these literatures to make public offerings. These documents are extremely valuable and can help those who study Tinh sect to be steadfast in their faith.

Master An Ham

Another disciple of Venerable Hai Hien, Dharma Master An Ham, the abbot of Thien Buddha Pagoda, before leaving the home life was a sick person who lost all faith in life.

In the past, He had encountered incidents that almost cost him his life, but these incidents did not make Him aware that it was time to reflect on himself. In 1982, he was hit by wind again (known in medicine as "cerebral artery rupture").

By 1989, his illness not only did not improve, but on the contrary, it became more serious. At this time, someone gave him a book "Amitabha Sutra explaining the dialogue" and a small book "Thien Tai Dong Tu 53 greed".

Before that, he was influenced by atheism, did not believe in anything, never went to a grave to worship his ancestors, much less went to a temple to burn incense and bow to the Buddha, but this time, he accepted it. When reading the "Amitabha Sutra of Explanation" to the 17th page, he began to truly believe in the World of Ultimate Bliss, so he made up his mind to study Buddha to attain Ultimate Bliss.

He had a biological younger sister who in 1985 went to Lai Buddha Pagoda under the court of the Venerable Hai Hien to become a Nun. Dharma Master An Ham asked the Nun to tell his situation to the Venerable Hai Hien. The old Venerable very firmly agreed to accept him as his disciple. He honestly told the Venerable: "I have no money, I can't work, I can only bring some food with me."

In the spring of 1990, his family took him to Lai Buddha Pagoda. In the car, they also brought 400 kilos of wheat and 100 kilos of corn. He took refuge in the Three Jewels, and soon left the home life.

Lai Buddha Pagoda has land, every day Venerable Hai Hien goes to the fields to do farming work. Even though Dharma Master An Ham brought some food himself, every time it was time to eat, he still felt uneasy. He immediately said to the Venerable:

“I can't eat this bowl of rice, I want to go home.” Old Venerable Hai Hien comforted him and said: “Since you've come here, don't go back.” Then he said to Him: "In the middle of the night when there is no one around, you can go out alone to the main hall and bow to the Buddha, pray for repentance, make great vows, your vow power is greater than the power of karma, then you can naturally change your destiny."

Dharma Master An Ham listened to his master's words, every night before 12 o'clock he went alone to the main hall to bow to the Buddha, repentance. He knelt before the statue of Buddha Bodhisattva and said all the evil karma he had created, repentance from the bottom of his heart, he often cried. He vowed to absolutely not return to this world, and making vows at all times must be the standard image of someone leaving the home life, spending his whole life for Buddha's glory, absolutely not letting Buddha's family lose face, vowing to devote everything for sentient beings, only worrying about farming, not asking for harvest.

Master An Ham remembers the old Venerable's personal teachings deeply. One time, the Venerable let him dip his chopsticks into a 50-pound jar of sesame oil, used to mix vegetables. The old Venerable's frugality, he saw with his eyes and remembered in his heart. Many years later, when mentioning this, He was still very emotional, saying: “Just based on this point, I will worship you for the rest of my life! Over the years, I have tried my best to learn from my master's diligence, but now I can still speak in terms of diligence, but in terms of frugality, I am still very far from being able to compare with my master."

In 2004, Dharma Master Hai Hien personally took him and Dharma Master An Chi (two brothers) to Thien Buddha Pagoda. He also advised: “It's very difficult here, it's like building a career with nothing. In the ancient monastery, if you don't really practice, then you can't stay anymore, the Dharma Protector will cause trouble. I hope you two brothers will truly practice. If you have precious blessings, Thien Buddha Pagoda will flourish again."

Thien Buddha Pagoda, Xa Ky district was founded in the sixth year of Vinh Binh during the Eastern Han Dynasty (63 AD), four years earlier than Bach Ma Pagoda in Luo Duong, which was built in the 10th year of Eastern Han Vinh Binh. During the "Van Cach" period, Thien Buddha Pagoda was seriously damaged. The temple's room belonged to a school and was used for many years. It was not until 2006 that it was completely returned to the temple. Later, when Dharma Master An Ham at the monastery was digging land to plant vegetables, he also dug up a piece of Han Dynasty brick, on which were engraved the four words "Six years of Vinh Binh".

Master An Vinh

In 2007, after Buddha's consummation, Dharma Master An Vinh, who had studied Buddha but had not yet left the home life, bowed to the appearance of old Dharma Master Tinh Khong, when he bowed for the second time, making vows in his heart: I pray to my noble master that I can find a wise master and a pure Pure Land ashram, and I want to concentrate on practicing. Not long after, someone introduced him to Lai Buddha Pagoda, Xa Ky district, to worship Bodhisattva Dharma Master Hai Khanh. Coming to Lai Buddha pagoda, he met the Venerable Hai Hien.

As soon as he saw the old Venerable, he immediately felt immeasurable joy. He prayed to the Venerable to accept him as a disciple. The old Venerable did not refuse. Three days later, the old Venerable happily told him: "Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva told me, there is still one disciple coming here, then you are here." At that time, Dharma Master An Vinh did not pay much attention after hearing it. He thought the Venerable was talking loudly.

At this time, the farmer next to him said to Him: “This old monk, it's not simple! One time a well was being drilled in the village. After several days of drilling, there was still no water. The Venerable came to look, then used his stick to point to another place and said: ‘You drill here, there is good water here.’ Everyone followed the Venerable's words and drilled the well, and sure enough, water was drilled very quickly.”

From then on, Dharma Master An Vinh witnessed many incredible things of the old Venerable.

At the end of 2009, Dharma Master An Vinh himself went to the old ashram of Vien Minh pagoda that had been abandoned for many years. He saw a scene of desolation and ruins. He then made up his mind to restore the ashram, here propagating the Pure Land Dharma.

Vien Minh Pagoda was founded during the Jin Dynasty and has nearly 800 years of history. The Ming, Qing, and Republic of China have all restored it. When Venerable Hai Hien, over 30 years old, came to Vien Minh Pagoda to study, at that time the monastery was extremely prosperous, with more than 200 monks residing there. Later, during the "Van Cach" period, the monastery was damaged.

Vien Minh Pagoda is about 100 km away from Lai Buddha Pagoda, because Vien Minh Pagoda has only Dharma Master An Vinh, and also an elderly cook, so he cannot often visit Venerable Hai Hien. To repay his master's kindness, every once in a while, Dharma Master An Vinh would welcome the Venerable to stay there for a short time.

Two or three years before the old Venerable's rebirth, he had to come to all the monasteries he had built or the monasteries that his disciples led, especially to Vien Minh pagoda, one because there was only one person leaving the home life here, Dharma An Vinh, and also leaving the home life not long; Second, because the monastic conditions are too difficult. The Venerable once said to a lay person: “This monastery is especially poor! If I come to stay, the incense fire there will be a little brighter.”

Master An Vinh was very conscientious. Thinking about the fact that the old Venerable upstairs was having trouble going to the bathroom, he specially built a small room with a toilet.

The old Venerable always persisted in waking up very early to bow to the Buddha and recite the Buddha's name, the same thing happened when he was at Vien Minh Pagoda.

Every day in his small room, when others meditate in the morning, the lights are on, and then he can be heard in the temple chanting 'Amitabha Buddha'. The old Venerable was like reciting Vajrayana. Each time he chanted the Buddha's name, it was not long, but every morning in the monastery, he could hear his voice walking and reciting the Buddha's name for a very long time.

Every day after breakfast, the Venerable started looking for something to do, usually doing it for a few hours.

The old Venerable and Dharma Master An Vinh were at the monastery exploring wasteland. When the old Venerable saw that Dharma Master An Vinh wanted to work, he both said: "You don't need to do anything anymore, go chant Buddha!"

Master An Vinh said: “Master! How can you ask a teacher who is over 100 years old to go to work, while we young people instead go out and run around idly?"

The Venerable said: “I recite Buddha without reciting the effort, so I have to recite a lot. Recite to a certain extent, even if you are reciting Buddha all the time. - When working, don't miss reciting Buddha!"

The Venerable often said to Dharma Master An Vinh: “Don't look at me while I'm working, I'm always chanting Buddha in my mind.”

The Venerable was always like that, letting everyone go recite Buddha's name, while he himself went to work.

On a summer day in 2010, Lai Phat Pagoda was holding a Dharma Assembly of the Three Time Recitation System when the power suddenly went out. Some lay people couldn't stand the heat in the Buddha hall, so they retreated to get some fresh air, and saw old Venerable Hai Hien carrying a tool bag on his shoulder, carrying a long ladder from the monastery tower. The old monk placed the ladder against the wall, climbed up, took out his tools and started working. After a while, the electricity was actually repaired. At the time the old Venerable was carrying the stairs and preparing to return to the tower, a lay person came to help. The old Venerable waved his hand, smiled and said: “You continue to chant Buddha! I was there and didn't hear the sound of chanting Buddha's name, so I knew the electric wire was damaged again."

The old Venerable paid special attention to his disciples. He placed great importance on morning and evening practice. Almost every day, the Venerable asked Dharma Master An Vinh twice: “Is it elaborate yet?” Although it is a common saying, this saying still encourages Dharma Master An Vinh to be brave and diligent. Later, every time he entertained, he seemed to hear his master's voice asking him: “Is it elaborate yet?”

Dharma Master An Vinh especially respected and loved his master. His filial piety towards the old Venerable also made Dharma Master An Chi admire and praise him.

Dharma Master An Chi, Dharma Master An Ham and Dharma Master An Vinh divided themselves into three Buddhist monasteries. After the old Venerable's rebirth, they all expressed: The ashram in the future must be dedicated to cultivating and propagating the Pure Land Dharma, absolutely not to disappoint, the kind teachings and earnest expectations of the master, to continue to pass down the old Venerable's good deeds, to practice well the six harmonies, to take precepts as the teacher, to take suffering as the teacher, "a day of not working, a day of not eating."

35. TOPIC OF THE WORLD

tom_tat: Buddha taught us to respect all Buddhas and praise Tathagata. Everything that corresponds to virtue must be praised; If you are not compatible with your virtue, you must pay respect but not praise. This is what the ancient Chinese said: “Dear…
noi_dung:
35. Respect the teachings of juniors

Buddha taught us to respect all Buddhas and praise Tathagata. Everything that corresponds to virtue must be praised; If you are not compatible with your virtue, you must pay respect but not praise. This is what the ancient Chinese said: "Respectful children far away". What is virtue? All true, good, and beautiful wisdom is virtue, the ancient Chinese said: The five wheels, the five permanents, the four thoughts, and the eight virtues are virtues. In Buddha's teachings, it says: Precepts, concentration, and wisdom are virtues.

Old Venerable Hai Hien always moderated the teachings of his juniors. Whenever he saw words that were contrary to the virtues of his juniors, he compassionately pointed out the mistakes and taught them at the right time.

That day was a Buddhist holiday. A laywoman came to the monastery and kept entangling a Dharma Master who kept talking about her family's gossip. After a long time of talking, the Dharma Master became a bit impatient and angrily opposed her words. Later, old Venerable Hai Hien went alone to the Dharma Master's room and told him: “When talking to others, don't get angry, your attitude must be peaceful. This time you get so angry, the next time people dare not tell you something, you will lose the opportunity to save sentient beings, and will even cut off their dharma body and life. When you die, it will also be an obstacle for you, you cannot help but pay attention!” The old Venerable is truly "Duong Thien Vu Dinh, Returning to Vu Tu That" (Praise before the public, comment in private room).

One evening in the summer of 2009, the weather was very hot. Venerable Hai Hien and several Dharma masters in the courtyard sat on the ground enjoying the wind. The Venerable said: “People leaving the home life don't value food, clothing, or grace, and shouldn't expect others to make offerings for them. Other people make offerings for you, you can't say you don't need them. Once you receive them, you can put them in the merit box or print scriptures, no matter what, you can't use them for your own enjoyment. Clothes in summer can cover the body, but in winter it's okay to wear clothes that don't let you get cold. It's okay to eat rice, no matter what kind of rice you eat to relieve your hunger. If I can eat well and dress beautifully, I don't want to go to the West anymore."

The old Venerable continued: “Don't ask anyone for anything, do everything yourself, don't listen to what others often say: 'Humanity does not seek self-righteousness'? We cannot hold grudges against anyone, holding grudges means we have ego. All things in the world are not real, fighting east and west, turning back is just a waste of time, fighting back and forth, when you die you only need a piece of land, what is worth fighting for? Just diligently recite Buddha's name and you will get everything in the World of Ultimate Bliss." He himself has done these words of advice to his juniors. In this whole life, He only did one thing - pray for Pure Land, other things were not involved. In this world, all we need is normal days, we can live day by day, we only need to have warm clothes, we only need to eat enough food, He has never asked for anything. Others made offerings for Him, He took them away, released them, printed scriptures, and did not use them himself.

Practicing the Bodhisattva path without clinging to appearances, old Venerable Hai Hien in this world really did it, he is an example for us. Buddha tells us, in this world, don't compete with people, don't pray with the world; Don't compete with all people or things, don't seek all things. Why is that? It's not real.

If there is a fight and a request, then it is wrong and has unjustly committed a karma crime.

Master Hui Neng said it very well, where do all ten thousand dharmas come from? Self-nature is born,

"The great self-nature can give birth to all dharmas". All dharmas are self-nature, self-nature is all dharmas. Self-nature does exist, but it cannot be seen. Why can't you see? It has no appearance, it is a piece of permanent light, so Buddha Dharma calls it "vacuum", it has no existence. However, the vacuum is non-empty, it can express all things, all things it shows are fake, not real, because the body is empty, because it is born and dies at a moment's notice, so it is absolutely impossible to possess it. In Buddha Dharma it is often said "to let go", which means "Do not compete with people, do not seek with the world". Truly let go, don't seek, don't fight, everything depends on fate. The shape of dependent conditions is joy and good. So, no matter how the Venerable sees people, good; see how good things are. In His eyes, nothing is bad.

tom_tat: Some people say that the old monk has supernatural powers, but Dharma Master An Chi does not think so. However, Mage An Chi is sometimes a bit ambiguous: “This cannot be said… You say he doesn't have supernatural powers, all the things...
noi_dung:
36. Fertilizer bags cover the rain

Some people say that the old monk has supernatural powers, but Dharma Master An Chi does not think so. However, Mage An Chi is sometimes a bit ambiguous: “This cannot be said… You say He doesn't have supernatural powers, everything is there... Thinking back later, the old Venerable had supernatural powers, but at that time none of you could perceive it. - In the end, is it your experience, or is it your supernatural power? Can't say. But we all really don't think that He has supernatural powers." It seems that He really has something that cannot be understood.

In 1999, the monastery planted another five or six acres of canola, and the seeds sprouted very well. By the end of March and early April, right at the mustard harvest season, the monastery harvested five large piles of rapeseed. Those two days, Venerable Hai Hien started sewing fertilizer bags. He took the bag apart, then sewed all the bags together. He sewed it into a very large bag (large sheet). How big is it? Each large sheet is as large as 10 - 20 bags of fertilizer.

The old monk sewed for two days and finally finished sewing. He told Dharma Master An Chi: "An Chi, bring out a few big bags and cover those piles of seeds for me. It's about to rain."

Master An Chi looked at those five large bags: A big pile there. He did not understand and said: “Master, it can't cover the rain! Those fertilizer bags were torn and had holes. Many of them were old, old, and weathered, all with holes." He said:

“Master, it can't cover the rain!” “Cover me from the rain, please cover me!”

Master An Chi is still very persistent: "I didn't cover it for you, teacher. It can't protect from the rain."

"That's the rain cover, please cover it for me!" The old monk spoke again.

Dharma Master An Chi had no choice but to deal with his master, thinking in his heart: Okay, then cover it up. Because he was afraid of the wind, after covering it, Dharma Master An Chi also used bricks to block the four corners and tie them on top. That's right, those five piles were all covered with the old Venerable's blanket.

Newly harvested canola should be left to dry in the sun. The rapeseed shells are dried until crispy. At this time, using a beater, it is very easy to crack the rapeseed shells.

But if it rains, you can't put it out to dry.

Five piles of mustard greens were incubated by the Venerable Hai Hien's large blanket for nearly 10 days. Newly harvested canola is incubated like that, will be stewed, then the canola is ripe, the skin can easily crack when exposed to wind.

During those 10 days, there were indeed three rains, but there was no rain at this monastery. Dharma Master An Chi watched the rain pass by, but the rain did not fall at the monastery, it all fell next to the monastery. He humorously said: “The Venerable is very kind, this thing can cover the rain - but there's no rain, how can it not cover it! If it really rains, it can't cover the rain, but it still doesn't rain!”

Dharma Master An Chi said that his master may have those so-called "magical powers": The fertilizer bag covers the pile of mustard greens, so the rain won't fall there. He laughed and joked with the Venerable: “Old Venerable, this really covers the rain! Not only does it cover the rain, it covers it very well! Even the rain doesn't fall, so why can't it cover the rain?" After listening, the Venerable smiled and did not say a word.

37. TRONG THANH TAO

tom_tat: The old Venerable Chuan Gioi, Hai Hien's master, after saving him, said one sentence to him: “‘Namo Amitabha Buddha’, should always be recited like that.” Then add another sentence: “Once you understand clearly, don't talk nonsense...
noi_dung:
37. In elegance there is magic

THERE IS MIRACULOUS

The old Venerable Chuan Gioi, Hai Hien's master, after saving him, said one sentence to him: “‘Namo Amitabha Buddha’, should always be recited like that.” Then add another sentence: "Once you understand clearly, don't talk nonsense, don't wave your arms and legs." What does this sentence "understand clearly" from the old Venerable Transmitting Precepts mean? It's just enlightenment. Once enlightened, you know everything, but you can't say it. Venerable Hai listened, he really did it, he really had wisdom, he really had magical powers, but he didn't reveal anything, there were no traces.

If a person's mind is pure, not even a single false thought arises, then he can clearly understand everything facing the outside world, not only clearly understanding the immediate world, but also clearly understanding the worlds of the past and future. This is the so-called present supernatural power. Magical powers are based on the method of meditation, which has the effect of being unhindered and free, transcending the human world.

The Venerable had wisdom, some said he had supernatural powers, but the Venerable did not reveal anything. Master An Chi said, the Venerable did not believe he had supernatural powers.

Finally, does the Venerable have supernatural powers? Even if His supernatural powers appear, people still don't know. If someone asked Him, He would not admit it! This is really calling you old, why do you have to let others know? By the time everyone knew, He had already reborn the World of Ultimate Bliss.

After the old Venerable's rebirth, Dharma Master An Chi thought back to his master's actions, causing him to not understand clearly.

Dharma Master An Chi left the home life not long ago, at that time in front of the monastery was still a mustard garden, now that mustard garden has grown a row of fresh flowers. Cabbage grown in the garden is very good, but because there has been no rain for many days, combined with high temperatures for many days in a row, the mustard leaves have been exposed to the sun and withered. Villagers drying wheat in front of the temple said that on TV, there would be no rain in the next few days. That afternoon, suddenly the Venerable asked Dharma Master An Chi and An Vinh to work together to dig a sewer in the vegetable garden.

Master An Chi said: “Master, the drought is still long, the drought is about to die, what are you digging to drain the water?”

The Venerable just answered gently and simply: “I dig it.”

Wizard An Vinh also did not understand, thinking in his heart: It's so hot, drought, no rain, why dig a sewer?

Master An Chi did not know how to say: “Master said to dig, then dig.” Although Dharma Master An Chi felt very reluctant, he did not want to make the old monk angry, so he followed suit. So everyone grabbed a shovel and started digging. The farmers nearby saw and laughed at Dharma An Vinh for being so stupid, listening to the old monk's nonsense.

Unexpectedly, on the afternoon of the first day, the sewer was dug, and on the afternoon of the second day, it rained like crazy, continuously raining for several hours. Fortunately, the preventive work was completed, the vegetable garden and the new monastery were not flooded.

It was a drought, so everyone had to dig a sewer, but it actually rained on the second day. Dharma Master An Chi admires the old Venerable from the bottom of his heart! He felt that the old Venerable was truly talented and had a wealth of experience. No matter what he did, he was very skilled. This time, Dharma Master An Chi was truly convinced, no longer like previous times. Master An Vinh was still a bit puzzled about this matter, but his heart had also increased his admiration for the old Venerable.

In the summer of 2012, a few strangers came to Vien Minh Pagoda, hoping to stay here at the monastery (that is, stay overnight). At that time, Venerable Hai Hien was also at Vien Minh Pagoda. Those monks heard that there was a monk over a hundred years old in the monastery, and they all wanted to go and pay their respects. At this time, the Venerable was lying on the bed resting. When he saw a guest coming, he did not get up.

If usual, the old Venerable would have been very happy and sat up to greet guests, but unexpectedly this time his attitude was very cold. He lay there, motionless, speaking slowly: "I'm old enough, this monastery only has one person, An Vinh, and there are also women, so this place is not hospitable to us and we can't stay the night."

The Venerable's actions made Dharma Master An Vinh extremely surprised. He really did not understand why the Venerable had such an unusual attitude today. After that, the layman who knew the situation clearly told Dharma Master An Vinh that those people were the ones propagating heresy.

Outside Vien Minh Pagoda, there is an empty piece of land where some vegetables and crops are grown. Sometimes passersby accidentally step on cabbage sprouts. Dharma Master An Vinh wanted to cover that road. Just then there were two empty rice rollers next to it, so he pushed it over there. But the rice roller was too heavy, causing His feet to slip several times, the rice roller remained motionless. After the old Venerable Hai Hien saw and passed there, he only saw him stooping down, and as soon as he tried his best, he moved the rice roller to the side of the road. How does Master have such great strength?

All of the old Venerable's movements made him confused. Dharma Master An Vinh really didn't know what to do properly. He and Dharma Master An Chi were the same. He really did not think that the old Venerable had supernatural powers. He only felt that the old Venerable had rich experience and was extremely impressed.

One more time, the Venerable was able to help layman Hoang avoid the disaster of prison. Layman Hoang supported Dharma Master An Sanh for many years. One day 20 years ago, layperson Hoang went to Lai Buddha pagoda to visit Venerable Hai Hien. The monk kept layperson Hoang at the monastery for one night, but layperson Hoang refused, saying he couldn't stay, and layperson Hoang had to rush home to take his nephew to the army. The Venerable said: "He's not a child in the house, and he can't be lost, so why do you keep asking to take him away?" No matter what, the Venerable stopped the layperson Hoang from leaving. This was the only time in his life that the Venerable stopped someone else.

It turned out that there was a murder case in Dong Bach district. The murderer was familiar with layperson Hoang. That day he ran to Hoang's house to hide. Seeing that Hoang was not at home, he went to Chi Thu's house. On the second day, the police arrested the perpetrator. Chi Thu, who harbored criminals, was also arrested, fined eight thousand, and had to spend one year in prison. If layperson Hoang stays at home, the consequences need not be said.

There were several times when the old monk himself was close to danger, and in the end, the danger turned into safety. After the old Venerable's rebirth, Dharma Master Dien Cuong once said to Dharma Master An Vinh: “You don't know the hurdles He went through!

We ordinary people cannot see the wonderful robes of the Buddha's feet!"

The things that Venerable Hai Hien excels at than others are that he is honest, listens, and does what he does, so he achieves things very quickly. Based on a Buddha sentence, the principle of one mind is not chaotic, so he knows everything, but he does not say it. Why not say? No one can hear and understand, no one can do like Him. Therefore, He completely performs in daily activities, those who know how to see can see it, those who do not know how to see, it is useless to talk to Him, they will only bring trouble to themselves.

Therefore, the old monk performed very elegantly all his life, but in elegance there is magic, in elegance there is magic.

38. LIFE

tieu_de: 38. The life of samadhi and wisdom
tom_tat: Avatamsaka Sutra says: “All sentient beings have the wisdom and virtue of the Tathagata.” “Virtue” refers to the ability, talent, and technique that we now speak of; “General” is a good general, it is a precious blessings. All sentient beings are wisdom…
noi_dung:
38. The life of samadhi and wisdom

Avatamsaka Sutra says: “All sentient beings have the wisdom and virtue of the Tathagata.” “Virtue” refers to the ability, talent, and technique that we now speak of; “General” is a good general, it is a precious blessings. All sentient beings are full of wisdom, full of virtue, and full of blessings. In other words, omniscience and omnipotence, "no law knows no law, no law no knowledge", is the ability of all living beings that each person is complete.

How can we discover the original nature of these treasures of ours? All Buddhas Tathagata use the method of precepts, concentration and wisdom, that is to say, the three studies of precepts, concentration and wisdom can discover the wisdom, virtue, and good appearance of our own nature. Pure Buddhism is even more wonderful, focusing on the precepts of concentration and wisdom in one sentence "Namo Amitabha Buddha", this Buddha title fully brings together the fullness of precepts, concentration and wisdom, and this method can be used by anyone.

The three precepts of concentration and wisdom, in reality, is one's own life, from morning to night, dealing with people, dealing with things, and dealing with things are the precepts of concentration and wisdom. On the principle of worldly dharma, Buddha dharma is not two, learning "precepts" is learning how to follow the dharma, keeping the rules, Buddha dharma often says "The evil acts, the good people serve" these eight words cover all the precepts. Specifically, in China, Patriarch Venerable taught us to cultivate the five virtues internally and cultivate the six harmony externally. The five virtues are temperance and frugality, temperance, kindness, prudence (reverence and caution, no matter what you do, be careful and reserved, this is respect), frugality and tolerance. Luc Hoa refers to green harmony mirror, which means the body is in harmony, the mouth is in harmony, the world is in harmony, the world is in harmony, the view is in harmony, the benefit is in harmony. The meaning of harmony and respect is to be kind to others on the outside and humble on the inside. Therefore, cultivating the five virtues internally, cultivating the six harmony externally.

“Concentration” means having a grasp in the mind, not being scattered. One-pointed mind towards Amitabha Buddha World the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, that is, a concentrated mind.

“Wisdom” is to be clear and thorough about all external realms, but not to be confused by it, not to be influenced by it, that is, not to deceive external appearances, not to move the mind internally. It is possible that the external body cannot trick the general, this is wisdom. The external environment is good, evil is also good, positive is also good, negative is also good, everything has nothing to do with me, in this world I do not give rise to thoughts, do not move thoughts, do not discriminate, do not accept, one sentence "Amitabha Buddha" recites to the end.

Therefore, the precepts of concentration and wisdom are daily activities, from morning to evening, wearing clothes and eating, gestures and speech are all precepts of concentration and wisdom. Only then can we clearly understand that Buddha Dharma is not just talk, it is not mysticism, Buddha Dharma is life, life is Buddha Dharma, all Buddhas, Bodhisattva appear in the world, it is such a life, it is to be such a human being, it is to behave like that. Looking carefully at the whole life of old Venerable Hai Hien, we know that his whole life was the practice of Buddha Dharma, practice in life, practice in work, practice in dealing with people, receiving things, dealing with things, it was truly satisfactory. When believers come to visit Him, He will advise them: "If you diligently recite Buddha's name, you will become Buddha, the rest is fake."

Buddha decided not to not let us touch anything in life - we can touch everything, touch in practice, practice without raising the mind, without moving thoughts, without discrimination, without attachment, this is practice, truly effective. Without giving rise to thoughts, without discriminating attachments, this concentration is flexible; Sitting still cross-legged and entering concentration, that concentration does not take effect.

National Master Hien Thu said the four virtues, those who can obey these four virtues are called all Buddhas, Bodhisattva, the opposite of these four virtues are ordinary people. The first virtue is "depending on conditions and miraculous effects". Eyes see, ears hear are "depending on conditions", we ordinary people just depend on the conditions, depending on the conditions, afflictions arise, creating karma samsara; Bodhisattva depends on the conditions: He sees clearly, hears clearly, but does not give rise to afflictions, does not create karma. Therefore, do not let trouble arise in your mind; If you don't put it in your mind, you can see form, hear sound, smell scent, enjoy taste, all without giving rise to the mind, without moving thoughts, without discrimination, without attachment, this is the "wonderful use".

Practicing is cultivating here, this "wonderful use" can help us return to our nature, returning to our nature is to attain the Supreme Bodhi, this is called true practice. Venerable Hai Hien of Lai Buddha Pagoda, how does he practice? Don't keep everything in your mind. From morning to night, the six senses come into contact with the realm of the six senses, which is clear, transparent, and thorough. That is wisdom. Not keeping it in your mind is concentration.

39. OLD BUDDHA LEAVE ME

tieu_de: 39. The old Buddha left me in the world to teach the Dharma
tom_tat: One time, a few young followers came to visit Venerable Hai Hien. The Venerable stopped his work to talk to everyone.
noi_dung:
39. The old Buddha left me in the world to teach the Dharma

One time, a few young followers came to visit Venerable Hai Hien. The Venerable stopped his work to talk to everyone.

The Venerable said to one of those young men: "The people in your village have deep good roots and have studied Buddha a lot."

“That's right. In our village, almost every family worships Buddha." The Venerable asked: "In your village many years ago, there was an old monk who lived, do you remember?" The young man replied: “At that time I was still young, but I had an impression, because of that Dharma Master my grandmother protected me. Later, he went to Bach Ma Pagoda." The Venerable said: “At that time, I invited him to Lai Buddha temple, but he refused... I don't know if he's still alive or not."

“I heard he passed away.”

“When is it no more?”

“Soon it won't be anymore, it's already a thing of the last century.” Having finished speaking, the young man couldn't help but laugh, thinking in his heart: If that Magician were still alive, he would be over 100 years old. Do you think everyone has the same longevity as you?

The old monk looked at him, not understanding, and asked: “What are you laughing at?” Layman said: “Do you also think that Empress Dowager Cixi is still alive?” The old monk also laughed loudly and said: “I'm still not that confused. - Oh my! This is a heavy karma obstacle for me. If I want to go, I can't go. Seeing that the old practitioners have left one by one, I have become an old goblin."

Layman Liu sitting next to him laughed. Layman Liu repeated the Venerable's words: “

‘I have become a demon.’ All of my disciples and disciples are gone.”

The old Venerable continued: “When it's time to die, you have to die. Not dead, I don't dare say." Layman Liu asked him: “Amitabha Buddha asked Him to explain the Dharma, is that right? He practiced very well.” The old Venerable said calmly: “The expression is good, don't let me say anything. Don't say anything." “Who won't let Him speak?” Another lay person couldn't help but ask. Everyone was also excited and waiting for the Venerable's answer.

The old monk looked at that lay person, stopped for a moment, a smile appeared on his face: “Old Buddha Gia won't let me speak.”

The "Buddha Family" that Venerable Hai Hien spoke of was Amitabha Buddha. This layman Liu once told everyone: “I ask the Sage, have you seen Amitabha Buddha, has (Amitabha Buddha) said anything to you? Sage said: ‘I begged Old Buddha Gia to come pick me up, but he did not agree, he said he would leave me in the world to teach the Dharma.’ ”

Reciting the Buddha's name had an unbelievable impact. He saw Amitabha Buddha! merit and title are unbelievable. All Buddhas in the ten directions and three generations are Amitabha Buddha, Amitabha Buddha is the total title. The meaning of this title, translated into Chinese, is immeasurable wisdom, immeasurable enlightenment. Reciting this title means reciting the names of all Buddhas in the ten directions and three lifetimes, and at the same time, this title includes the boundless Dharma teachings of all Buddhas. Therefore, the old Venerable Hai Hien's master taught him a Buddha chant to the end, the meaning behind it is very profound, using this method, there is no need to take detours, this is the straight path!

Old Venerable Hai Hien is "One sentence 'Amitabha Buddha', recite it for a lifetime without changing direction!" When Dharma Master Dien Cuong praised Venerable Hai Hien, he was full of respect. He told Dharma Master An Chi: “Teacher, look at how people live their lives without illness and suffering, knowing the day and time in advance, and how free they are! … One is the incarnation of Bodhisattva, one is saving sentient beings. This is to set an example for future generations, so that all future generations can follow that example to practice and attain Buddhahood! One day, a Dharma Master accompanied the Venerable Hai Hien to Xa Ky city to work. The old monk sat in the car and muttered to himself: “Be gentle, don't go looking for someone to help you do the work. Lay people have their jobs, people leaving the home life have their jobs, leaving the home life, everyone does their own work.

Stop for a moment and say: “Those who leave the home life, if they know how to preach the sutras, will preach the sutras to others. If they don't know how to preach the sutras, they will still preach good dharma to the masses. I don't know anything, I don't know how to preach sutras, I don't know how to chant sutras, I don't know how to sing praises, I only know how to chant Buddha's name, clear land to farm, so I'll explain this dharma. If I hadn't taught the dharma, I would have left a long time ago."

The main dharma is to set an example, for everyone to see and learn what Buddha is; If you are not like Him, then you cannot call learning Buddha; being like Him is truly learning Buddha.

Old Venerable Hai Hien is truly a Buddha chanter. He let go of all conditions, in his mind there was only Amitabha Buddha. Apart from Amitabha Buddha, there were no false thoughts, no distracting thoughts. If you ask Him, He knows everything, that is enlightenment, without enlightenment you cannot do it. He is enlightened, he is finished with birth and death.

40. MEMORIAL SUPPORT

tieu_de: 40. The chant aid is not reliable
tom_tat: Old Venerable Hai Hien was very certain about his own rebirth of the Ultimate Bliss World. He said: “When I was reborn, I didn't need any supporting chanting, I chanted Buddha myself; Letting others help recite, it's not certain, it's not worth it
noi_dung:
40. The chant aid is not reliable

Old Venerable Hai Hien was very certain about his own rebirth of the Ultimate Bliss World. He said: “When I was reborn, I didn't need any supporting chanting, I chanted Buddha myself; Letting others assist in reciting is uncertain and unreliable.”

The old layman Yen at Luc Phuong Buddha Street in Nam Duong often came to tell the Venerable: “When you are reborn, you will tell me, I will find someone to help chant for you.”

Old Venerable Hai Hien replied: “If you ask someone else to help you chant, then you don't believe that person can walk. I don't need any chanting help, I can walk on my own."

Studying Buddha, studying Pure Land Buddhism, Venerable Hai Hien is the best example. He can recite Buddha freely, rebirth as Buddha, without needing others to help him chant; He knew the date and time, knew which day to go, Amitabha Buddha had already made an appointment with Him, until Buddha appeared and led Him to rebirth. His words are extremely important: Do not rely on chanting aids, chanting aids are not reliable.

You must definitely grasp it yourself. Asking someone to help recite is really uncertain. If at the critical moment you are reborn, someone helps you chant in advance and wants to find out if you have reborn or not, what realm you have gone to, then they will touch your head! This will disturb you and you will not be happy.

Are you sure that when others harass you like that, in your mind you are okay and not influenced by them? It takes that kind of effort. If you don't have that kind of effort, it's best not to bother anyone, otherwise you won't be able to go to the West. If you don't let others disturb you, then you must rebirth yourself. The time Buddha promised has come, then Buddha will come to guide you, you can rely on this. Buddha doesn't come to guide you, you don't know where the World of Ultimate Bliss is, so there must be a Buddha to guide you.

The last thought when dying was Amitabha Buddha, definitely reborn in the West. How can we ensure that the last thought when dying is Amitabha Buddha, without any other distracting thoughts? Elaboration must be nurtured in normal times. Old Venerable Hai Hien has completed it. He has recited a Buddha's verse for 92 years. He has thoroughly memorized this Buddha's verse. In his normal daily activities, he had no distracting thoughts, dressed, ate, and thought Buddha; He didn't think about the clothes being old and having to be sewn, not knowing the taste of vegetables when eating rice, not having this delicious, that not delicious, he didn't keep these things in his mind. Life is the same, work, dealing with people, receiving things, everything is the same. Once you have mastered the practice, you can rebirth freely, without the help of others. This practice is extremely important! One last thought is more important than all, it is related to the next life.

Go, there will be no pain at all. In the afternoon of the day before the old Venerable Hai Hien left, there was still a vegetable garden in front of the monastery. He and his disciples harvested vegetables and did not stop working until evening. People say: Old Venerable, you've worked all day, you can clean up and rest, don't do it anymore. He replied: "This job, I'm done, I won't do it anymore." In the evening, the Venerable finished his work and recited Buddha's rebirth during the night.

The old Venerable taught us the Dharma: live one day, do one day, live one hour, do one hour. When you say let go, you will have great freedom! His mother also walked like that, and his junior brother Dharma Master Hai Khanh also walked like that, without needing anyone to help chant. Where does this certainty come from? Let go. The common disease of everyone is not letting go, having too many desires, being very miserable, thinking too much.

Therefore, rebirth is really decided by yourself, if you say go then go, if say stay then stay, life and death are free.

Old Venerable Hai Hien knew the date and time in advance.

Or twenty-eight days before the Venerable's rebirth, a layperson Ly from Xa Ky district came to Lai Buddha pagoda to visit him. His face was calm and calm as he said to this lay person:

“Remember, diligently recite Buddha!”

“Living is better than being seven or eighty years old. I'm over a hundred years old, I think I can't live past such an old age - I'm content to die. After death, if you practice well, your soul will become Buddha, everyone in the world knows."

Twenty days before rebirth, he told some disciples in the temple: “I won't survive this year.” Everyone didn't think so, because they still saw that the master's body was extremely healthy, there was nothing unusual about it, how could he say that he could just walk?

Ten or twenty days before rebirth, the Venerable again visited his friend, his old colleague, this was an unusual event in the Venerable's life.

The old Venerable went to Co Phong pagoda, Binh Thi town, Dong Bach district, to visit his friend who had practiced for many years, Dharma Master Dien Cuong "Thiet Cuoc Tang". The Dharma Protector of Lai Buddha Pagoda, layman Hoang went with the Venerable. After "Van Cach", layman Hoang rode his bicycle to Dong Bach mountain to invite the Venerable Hai Hien to preside over the ashram.

On the way, the old monk held the hand of the old layman Hoang and said: “I only came this time, I won't come again.”

“Why don't you come anymore, master?” The old Venerable said firmly to layman Hoang: “I have to go soon. I came to greet you two, to let you know.”

The old layman said: “Impossible. Last time I told you, I said Old Buddha Family wouldn't let me go, let me stay for two more years, why do you say I have to go now?

“You don't know. Two days ago, Old Buddha Gia warned me again, telling me to leave immediately. It didn't take more than a month for me to leave.”

The old layman was not content to hear his master's words, so he immediately stopped the conversation and did not let the Venerable continue speaking. Magician Dien Cuong "Thiet Cuong Tang"

said, "I have a little bit of caution", three days ago I saw the old Venerable coming, saying he wanted a brown cushion. Three days later, sure enough, the Venerable arrived.

After lunch, Dharma Master Dien Cuong wanted the Venerable to rest a bit, but the Venerable did not agree and sat in the car. In his heart, Dharma Master Dien Cuong still remembered making a brown cushion for the old Venerable, but he did not expect that after a few days, someone would come and tell him: Old Venerable Hai Hien has passed away. Dharma Master Dien Cuong heard it and felt moved in his heart. He then understood that the Venerable asked him for a companion, and that was to say to him: I personally want to meditate and pass away.

Leaving Co Phong Pagoda, the old Venerable went to the monasteries where he left the home life and used to practice and looked back little by little, then said to the disciples there: “After this, I won't come anymore. The Venerable also went to Vien Minh Pagoda of Dharma Master An Vinh. When preparing to leave, he left behind a stick and a set of clothes. After Dharma An Vinh discovered it and immediately went to get it, the old Venerable shook his hand and said to Dharma An Vinh: “No more, I don't want to use it anymore.”

Everyone did not think much about the Venerable's unusual actions, nor at Lai Buddha Pagoda. About a week before rebirth, the old Venerable alone silently moved the corn stalks on the way to the monastery tower into the corner of the monastery wall. After Dharma Master An Chi saw it, he said to the Venerable: "It's not an obstacle. Don't move it anymore." But the old Venerable did not listen. Dharma Master An Chi saw that he could not advise him, so he could only call everyone to help. Everyone was busy working for two days before the whole thing was moved. After moving, the Venerable again swept the road clean.

Everyone couldn't particularly understand the Venerable's actions, thinking that the Venerable did unhelpful things. After the old Venerable's rebirth, when everyone carried his dharma body towards the monastery, they suddenly had a sudden and great realization. It turned out that the old Venerable was doing so to pave the way for himself!

After two or three days, four or five days before the Venerable's rebirth, a lay person came to the monastery to prepare to invite the Venerable to lunch. When the layperson arrived at the tower, he saw the old monk moving pieces of rubble from the wall of the tower to the side of his tomb tower, arranging them neatly and neatly. The old Venerable saw the lay person coming and said to the lay person: “Quick, help me move the bricks to load them up there.” The lay people obeyed and worked together with the Venerable.

During the time the two were moving the bricks, Dharma Master An Chi sent people many times to invite the Venerable to dinner, but the Venerable did not agree and continued to work like that. Although this monk had known the old monk for a short time, he had been at the monastery for more than three months, and he felt confused: Normally the old Venerable is not that stubborn, why has he become so stubborn these past few days?

After the Venerable's rebirth, Dharma Master An Chi prepared to buy bricks to build a tower for the Venerable. Only then did everyone understand the Venerable's dedication. Turns out he did not want to waste anything. He moved the ruined bricks to build a tomb tower for himself.

The old Venerable never wanted to bother others. He did everything he could do himself. Even after the funeral, he did his best to arrange it himself properly.

42. Final advice

Four days before the rebirth of Venerable Hai Hien.

On January 13, 2013, layman Vinh and layman Luu of Buddha Recitation in Yiwu Street together with a group of five people, from Nam Duong came to Lai Buddha Pagoda, Ky commune district to visit the 112-year-old Venerable Hai Hien. It was on this day that the old Venerable saw the book "If you want Buddha Dharma to flourish, only the Sangha praises the Sangha".

When everyone wanted to leave, the old Venerable and everyone reluctantly said goodbye, they walked to the front of the car, the old Venerable also sent them to the front of the car, at this time these people once again bowed and said goodbye to the old Venerable.

The old Venerable spoke loudly to them: "You have to recite Buddha's name, the rest is all fake!" After that, the Venerable once again, without hesitation, told in detail how he recited the Buddha's name. “Every day at three o'clock in the morning I wake up and bow to the Buddha. Sometimes I wake up at one o'clock and recite Buddha's name, chanting for 20 minutes in front of the statue.

Buddha, then circumambulate Buddha, then sit down and recite, sometimes chant aloud, sometimes not speak, more time is spent chanting silently, Buddha is always in the mind.

The Venerable continued to instruct them: “At any time, do not cause more trouble for others! Normally they cook food for me, more is fine, less is fine, I don't say anything, I eat as much as I can, otherwise others have to run back and forth, I don't want to bother others."

The old Venerable advised everyone to "recite Buddha, the rest are all fake", this statement is a description of the Venerable Hai Hien himself, in his mind there is only one sentence Amitabha Buddha, except for Amitabha Buddha, he does not take anything to heart, this is a true person reciting Buddha.

The old Venerable taught others hour by moment: "If you diligently recite Buddha's name, you will become Buddha, the rest is fake." This is the best saying that old Venerable Hai Hien left us, a saying that is worth seriously studying. Only reciting Buddha is real, only rebirth of the Ultimate Bliss World as Buddha is real, the rest is all fake, nothing is real. Diamond Sutra says: “Every form of existence is illusory”, “All existence is a dharma, like an illusory dream”, it is said in the Prajnaparamita Sutra: "All Dharma, non-existent, all-empty, impossible to attain."

Master Tinh Khong once said: “You must know clearly that the false cannot be obtained, the real also cannot be obtained. Why is that? In the real thing there are no appearances, no material phenomena, this is to say that the self-nature, the self-nature is pure, without appearances; Self-nature is neither born nor destroyed, inside there are no material phenomena, no mental phenomena (ie no thoughts), nor natural phenomena, so it is impossible to attain. Self-nature can manifest all dharmas, Great Master Hui-neng said most clearly, 'If the self-nature is capable of giving birth to all dharmas'. If you really understand clearly, you will recite Buddha's name, just keep the name 'Amitabha Buddha' in your mind, no distracting thoughts, no false thoughts. Why? Delusional thoughts and random thoughts are all six paths of samsara, this must be clearly known. If false thoughts and random thoughts are not interrupted, then the six paths of samsara will not be interrupted and you will not get out. Delusions and distracting thoughts are no longer there. When you want to go, you will go then, truly at ease, when you leave, you will be very relaxed."

43. 92 Years of good and good water

January 17, 2013, the last day before Venerable Hai Hien's rebirth.

This day, the old Venerable Hai Hien told a lay person that he dreamed that his brother came to him to ask for deliverance, so he hoped to be able to bury his remains in his homeland. In the afternoon, the old Venerable and his disciples dug vegetables in front of the monastery, working non-stop until dark, when everyone advised him to rest.

Dharma Master An Xuyen asked him: “Master, what are you still doing?”

The Venerable replied: “I can't do it for so long, I'm almost done.” When he finished, he said: “This job, I'm done, I won't do it again in the future.” To others, it sounded like a very normal statement. Unexpectedly, he left that night. Thinking about it later, I realized there was a meaning in the old Venerable's words. At dusk, Dharma Master An Chi and a few lay people were in the lecture hall watching a disc of the Great Sutra explaining the meaning of Dharma Master Tinh Khong, and heard the old Venerable in his room reciting the Buddha's name. Normally at this time, the Venerable will also burn incense in his room, bow to the Buddha, and recite the Buddha's prayers, but the chanting time is very short, but that day the chanting time is much longer than usual. A layperson who was listening to the sutra felt a little curious and asked a fellow practitioner next to him: "Why doesn't the Venerable stop chanting Buddha's name today?" Even though I asked like that, I still didn't let this strange thing stay in my mind too much.

After finishing dinner, the old Venerable as usual rested very early. Midnight. Just after one o'clock in the morning, a lay person who usually lives at the monastery got up to go to the bathroom and saw that the light in the old monk's room was already on. Early morning the next day. After everyone finished the morning session, Dharma Master An Thuyen offered rice to the Venerable. He called out to the Venerable, but no one answered. He opened the door and saw the Venerable lying on the bed, his clothes neatly folded and placed on the bed. Normally, the old monk absolutely does not sleep late, and his clothes are not so neat.

Dharma Master An Thuyen called several times but did not see any response from the Venerable. He came a little closer and discovered that the Venerable had already reborn peacefully. Master An Chi said: "Smiling face, very rosy face."

Because, the old Venerable's urinal was left in the bathroom, so it can be said that after the old Venerable did his morning session, he lay down on the bed again.

On January 17, 2013, on the 6th day of December in the year of the Dragon, the old monk Hai Hien was 112 years old, not sick, and passed away peacefully.

The old Venerable knew the date and time in advance, although he did not say it clearly, he still revealed some information to the old dharma protector Hoang of Lai Buddha pagoda. Ten days before the old Venerable's rebirth, he told layperson Hoang: “Two days ago, Old Buddha Gia warned me again, telling me to leave immediately. It didn't take more than a month for me to leave.” He didn't say what day it was, in fact He already knew, He just didn't say. There was a lay person who volunteered to assist him in chanting, but he did not need it, saying: "I can walk on my own", he did not let others help him recite because he was afraid that others would hinder him. His greatest fear was not being able to maintain mindfulness when he died.

"A day without work, a day without eating", the Venerable is truly responsible, he must go to the World of Ultimate Bliss in the evening, and still work all day during the day, for the benefit of sentient beings. No one expected that he would be reborn, his body was still in very good health, his mind was clear, without any confusion.

The 20-year-old Venerable Hai Hien was leaving the home life. His master only taught him one phrase, "Amitabha Buddha", and taught him to always recite it. He is really old, he listens, he truly does it. He has recited this Buddha phrase for 92 years. We have heard of this proverb "Good water, good water" but have never seen it - there are not many people who can be good and good, but we did not expect to see it in this old Venerable.

Dharma masters An Chi, An Ham, An Khong, An Vinh, An Bao, disciples of old Venerable Hai Hien, led the four disciples who heard the news and flocked to the old Venerable's spirit for seven days, reciting Buddha without interruption.

A week after the old Venerable passed away, his body was still soft and had a rare appearance.

However, the most powerful legend cannot compare to the freedom of rebirth! Who doesn't wish that in this life there would be no sickness, no suffering, no suffering of old age, no suffering of death?

Buddha said, we live in this world, eight sufferings are intertwined, these eight sufferings are: The body has birth, old age, sickness, and death. You can't seek what you want, and you can't keep the things you like forever; Loved people, things, and things are often separated; The people, things, and things you hate do not leave you for a single day, causing you to suffer. Ahead are these seven results of suffering, what we love in front of us, the following five aggregates are the cause of suffering. This body of ours is form, feelings, thoughts, actions, and consciousness of these five aggregates gathered together: The five aggregates are in harmony and have this body. This body is the root cause of the previous seven types of suffering. If we didn't have this body, it would be okay, but we have this body; plus the soul that people often talk about, the consciousness that Buddha Dharma talks about. Xi Thanh is a visualization of the creation of an extremely prosperous body and mind, suffering from afflictions, non-stop habit energy day and night, and feeling the seven types of suffering ahead.

These eight types of suffering must be experienced, at the time of experiencing it, in the place where we are experiencing it, no one can escape, so Buddha said that the six paths of samsara are a sea of suffering, an immense sea of suffering.

What is good about studying Buddha? If you diligently recite the Buddha's name and sincerely pray to be born in the Pure Land, you can escape the sufferings of old age, illness, and death. Before our eyes we see the old Venerable Hai Hien, he does not compete with people, he does not seek the world, he does not need anything, so he does not seek suffering. The old Venerable also did not have the two types of separation and resentment. He treats everyone equally, sees everyone as good, sees everyone as happy, sees everyone as joyful, He has no love for separation, no resentment. He did not even have the five aggregates of suffering, in His mind there was only one sentence "Amitabha Buddha", where did the five aggregates come from? There is no difference between this and being born in the World of Ultimate Bliss.

“You saw Amitabha Buddha, what did Buddha tell you?”

Only then will they understand that in the old Venerable's daily activities, a gesture, an action of the old Venerable all contains mysterious secrets, the supreme magic in wearing clothes and eating meals, in all movements, just like Dharma Master An Ham said: "The master's every word and every action is expressing the Dharma."

During the year before the rebirth of the old Venerable Hai Hien, he had to come and stay for a period of time at all the monasteries he built or the monasteries his disciples led. No matter which monastery or ashram he went to recite the Buddha's name, it was for the performer to speak and demonstrate the dharma in formless form. When everyone knew that he had been a vegetarian all his life and recited Buddha's name, now that he was over a hundred years old, and could also chop wood, hoe the ground, pull weeds, and thread needles for sewing, no one could not help but praise him. Many people thus entered Buddha's door, giving rise to the good mind of fasting and reciting Buddha's name and diligently reciting Buddha's name.

We definitely should not assume that he only has one Buddha name, and that other than that, he doesn't know anything. Do we have His compassion? Is there really an old man like Him? How humble and respectful he was towards everyone. In life, the whole life is lived in the bar of suffering, taking suffering as a teacher, strictly maintaining the precepts, staying with Him, also maintaining the precepts, enduring suffering.

Every day from morning to night he worked in the fields. His ashram was a small temple in the countryside, with no incense or lamps, nor Buddhist events and Dharma conferences. How did he live? Thanks to agriculture. During his entire life, he reclaimed more than a hundred acres of land, grew food, grew vegetables, grew fruit, and his harvest, in addition to maintaining the lives of everyone in the monastery, also went to help the poor. Thousands and thousands of people received his making offerings. He has been doing this for 92 years. He truly does it, and every day he does it with great joy. The old monk happily gave. The money other people make offerings for Him, He uses to recite sutras, release beings, and use to help others build ashrams.

Master Tinh Khong said: “His mind is pure, in his mind there is only one word Buddha. Seeing everyone as good people, seeing all things as good deeds, He makes no distinction, He has no attachments. Not only did he not have discriminatory attachments, I believe that after his middle age, that is, after the age of 40, his six senses came into contact with the realm of the six senses, and he was able to not give rise to thoughts. Not having a mind without moving a thought is a great enlightenment, a clear mind and seeing the nature, this is something not everyone can do.

"The person who cultivates is one who is not idle in the abode, is free from chaos, follows the truth of the mind, remembers one Buddha, specializes in calling names, depends on the Buddha's direction, corrects the body in the right direction, constantly chanting the Buddha's thoughts continuously and without delay, because of one single thought, one can gain insight into all the Buddhas of the ten directions, planning great eloquence."

That is to say, practitioners must choose a pure place to practice with few people, the ashram must be built in a very simple and simple way, making it easy to cultivate the mind and nurture the path; False thoughts and thoughts must be let go; You must keep your mind in the truth, this truth is Amitabha Buddha; commemorating Amitabha Buddha; specializes in claiming the title Amitabha Buddha, because Amitabha Buddha is in our west direction, so we must sit east and west, always facing west; a Buddha chant to the end;

In one thought, all Buddhas in ten directions can immediately be seen, because all Buddhas in ten directions praise this title, all Buddhas in ten directions advise us to recite this title.

The above sayings refer to the practice of samadhi that Bodhisattva Manjushri practices. Venerable Hai Hien has done these sayings, he is completely in agreement with these sayings.

He knew the day and time in advance, did not get sick, the day before his rebirth he was still working in the fields - He walked peacefully and freely, His practice was also a saying "Namo Amitabha Buddha". His final manifestation is a testimony to Pure Buddhism students, proving that this Buddha title is effective, this Buddha title can help us end birth and death, leave the three worlds, and be reborn to the World of Ultimate Bliss as Buddha. Bodhisattva appears, so that we can truly believe in the Pure Land. In this era, if we truly learn from the Venerable, there is no one who cannot be reborn, no one who cannot become a Buddha. merit represents immeasurable and boundless expression. "Old Buddha Family" did not take Him to the World of Ultimate Bliss, but asked Him to stay in this world to teach the Dharma, to be an example for everyone to see, to use physical teachings, not to teach Him using verbal teachings. When he was still alive, the influence was not very great, because he lived in the countryside, the scope of his life's activities were just a few districts and a few small temples. His lifelong practice is an example of a person who recites the Buddha's name, an example of a person seeking rebirth in the West, and is also a true example of complete faith and vows. He uses it to encourage everyone, hoping that everyone can achieve. In this era, how can we achieve success by cultivating Pure Land? Layman Luu and layman Vinh came to the Venerable's room and saw the Venerable holding a small, yellowed notebook. Layman Liu read the title of the book to the Venerable.

As soon as the old Venerable heard the words "If you want Buddha Dharma to flourish, only the Sangha will praise the Sangha", he was extremely happy, he was extremely happy, like a treasure that he thought about every day falling into his hands. He immediately found the new robe that he treasured, put it on with a solemn face, and very meticulously checked his body front and back in every small detail, then adjusted it again, then told the lay followers: “I'm holding this book, please take a picture for me.”

Layman Liu clearly understood what the Venerable said: “This is the only time in his life he proactively asked to take pictures for him. This action of His Holiness expressed the deep, passionate wish in His heart for the Buddha to unite and the Dharma to prosper."

After taking pictures, a few people asked the Venerable to teach me a question. Suddenly, His face went from happy to becoming extremely solemn. The old Venerable's dignified and compassionate face truly touched the layperson Vinh. She could not help but knelt down in front of the Venerable Hai Hien and blurted out: “Old Venerable! Lord rebirth World the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, don't forget to come pick us up!”

“Process! Procession!” The old Venerable did not stop responding. His tone was especially steadfast and powerful. After saying this, the old monk's smile was like a beautiful lotus flower in full bloom!

With both hands, the old Venerable held up the book "If you want Buddha Dharma to flourish, only the Sangha praises the Sangha", and took the last photo of His life - this is His last Dharma statement. Four days later, He was satisfied and went to the World of Ultimate Bliss.
